Classes (2): yes (broadcast frame), no (non-broadcast frame)

Current default version: 10.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Required Description ROBOFLOW_API_KEY Yes Roboflow API key. Used by all training scripts and upload utilities to authenticate against the Roboflow API. Obtain it from your Roboflow workspace settings.

The Roboflow SDK also reads the key from ~/.config/roboflow/config.json if you have previously run roboflow login.

Training metrics are logged to Weights & Biases if the wandb CLI is authenticated (wandb login). No explicit env var is required beyond the standard WANDB_API_KEY that the W&B SDK reads automatically.

docs.title: W&B projects
docs.text: Script W&B project train_object_detector.py footy_scan_detection train_classifier.py footy_scan_classifier

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to set up, develop, and work with the Footy Scan codebase.

docs.title: Setting Up Development Environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone <repository-url>
cd football-scan

  2. Python Environment: We use uv for Python environment and dependency management. First, install uv if you haven't already: 

    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

  3. Install the package in development mode: 

    uv pip install -e .

  4. Install additional dependencies for ML and video processing (if needed): 

    uv pip install "torch" "opencv-python" "tqdm"

docs.title: Using the Makefile (recommended)
docs.text:
Common repo-wide tasks are captured in the Makefile to standardize workflows:

make setup make deps-update

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
We use MkDocs with the Material theme for documentation. To work with docs:

# Serve docs locally (with live reload)
uv run mkdocs serve

# Build the documentation site
uv run mkdocs build

# Deploy to GitHub Pages (if configured)
uv run mkdocs gh-deploy

The documentation will be available at http://127.0.0.1:8000 when serving locally.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest        # everything (also: make tests)
make test-fast       # skips tests marked slow or needs_weights

Tests marked needs_weights skip themselves when the model weights (e.g. model_saves/sam3/sam3.pt) have not been pulled from DVC/LFS.

docs.title: Code Organization
docs.text:
football-scan/
├── docs/               # Documentation
├── src/
│   └── footy_track/   # Main package code
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── main_entrypoint.py
├── tests/             # Test files
├── mkdocs.yml        # Documentation configuration
└── pyproject.toml    # Project configuration

docs.title: Time Handling
docs.text:
The project uses two main time formats: - ContinuousTime: Continuous seconds from game start - GameTime: Referee/broadcast clock time

See Time Formats for detailed conversion rules and examples.

docs.title: Pipeline Architecture
docs.text:
The processing pipeline consists of three main components: - InputConsumer: Video frame input - Processor: Detection and tracking - OutputProducer: Data serialization

See Pipeline Architecture for detailed design information.

docs.title: Automated Tools
docs.text: When using automated tools or agents with this codebase, follow the guidelines in Agent Guidelines to maintain consistency.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: To change the docs, read How to contribute to the docs.

docs.title: Environment notes
docs.text:
Who this is for: anyone setting up a new machine, especially an older or unusual one. These notes were measured on the review's build machine on 2026-11-08.

  • Old CPUs without AVX2 crash on import. The build machine's CPU lacks AVX2. The newest duckdb and the stock polars die with an illegal instruction there. The workaround is duckdb==1.3.2 and polars-lts-cpu in the virtual environment only. pyproject.toml asks for duckdb>=1.5.3, and polars arrives through ultralytics; do not edit pyproject.toml or uv.lock to work around a local CPU.
  • Open the feature store read-only when inspecting it: duckdb.connect(path, read_only=True). See Feature store design, section 7.1.
  • Weights are not in git. model_saves/sam3/sam3.pt and the detector checkpoints come from the object store or DVC/LFS. Tests that need them fail without the file (see below).
  • No GPU is needed for the tests. No test uses CUDA (checked 2026-11-08). The slow ones are model tests that run on the CPU.
  • Where the data is is covered in Datasets and labels; the labeller finds it through FOOTY_CLIPS_DIR, FOOTY_GT_MARKS_DIR and FOOTY_BALL_CANDIDATES_DIR.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
The suite has 462 tests (collected 2026-11-08). The whole run took about 4 m 30 s before the speed-up and about 52 s after it (measured on the build machine, same date).

Why it was slow. The guess was a GPU problem. It was not: no test uses CUDA. Three things took almost all the time: two SAM3 tests (about 75 to 80 s each, and they fail anyway when the weights file is missing) and the first fiftyone test (about 17 s of start-up).

What fixes it. The chore/faster-tests changes are merged (with PR #24). You get:

Command What runs Time (measured before the merge) uv run pytest or make tests Everything about 52 s make test-fast Skips tests marked slow or needs_weights about 25 s

The needs_weights marker is for tests that need model weights that are not in the repo; they skip themselves when the file is missing. The change also makes the extract_frames test fixture create its output folder first, because ffmpeg does not.

flowchart LR
  classDef code fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111
  classDef new fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#111
  classDef data fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111

  ALL["make tests<br/>462 tests, about 52 s"]:::code
  FAST["make test-fast<br/>about 25 s"]:::new
  SAM["2 SAM3 tests<br/>about 75 to 80 s each<br/>needs_weights, slow"]:::new
  FO["fiftyone tests<br/>about 17 s start-up<br/>slow"]:::new
  W[("sam3.pt weights<br/>not in git")]:::data

  ALL --> SAM
  ALL --> FO
  FAST -. "skips" .-> SAM
  FAST -. "skips" .-> FO
  W --> SAM

Legend: blue is what existed before, purple is what the faster-tests change added, grey is data not in git. The diagram shows that the full run includes the two SAM3 tests and the fiftyone tests, and that make test-fast skips both groups.

CI runs make test-fast on every pull request (see Checks before you commit, T-08).

docs.title: Checks before you commit
docs.text:
Two kinds of automatic check protect main: small, fast ones that run on your machine each time you commit, and a fuller set that runs on GitHub for every pull request (PR). The fast ones catch most mistakes before anyone else sees them.

One-time setup. Run make hooks. This installs a git hook using uvx pre-commit, so there is nothing new to add to the project.

What runs when you commit. Each commit runs these hooks on the files you changed:

  • ruff checks the Python for mistakes and fixes what it safely can.
  • ruff-format lays the code out in the project style.
  • codespell spell-checks code and docs. Project terms such as MOT are allowed.
  • nbstripout strips outputs from notebooks so they do not bloat the repo.
  • Small file checks: a newline at the end of each file, no trailing spaces, valid YAML and TOML, no leftover merge-conflict markers, and no file over 500 KB.

If a hook changes a file, the commit stops. Look at the change, git add the files again and commit again. If a hook reports a problem it cannot fix, fix it by hand and commit again.

Run everything yourself.

make check    # lint + fast tests, the same things CI runs
make lint     # ruff check + ruff format --check only
make format   # let ruff fix formatting and simple lint problems

What runs on GitHub. Every PR, and every push to main, runs three jobs:

Job What it does lint Runs the pre-commit hooks on every file in the repo. tests Installs the project and runs make test-fast (skips slow tests and tests that need model weights or API keys). docs Builds the docs site, to catch broken pages. It is not strict yet, because system_design.md has two known broken links.

A new push to the same branch cancels the run that is still going.

flowchart TD
  classDef you fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111
  classDef auto fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111
  A["Edit code and docs"]:::you --> B["git commit:<br/>pre-commit hooks run"]:::auto
  B -->|"a hook fails or fixes a file"| A
  B -->|"all hooks pass"| C["git push and open a PR"]:::you
  C --> D["CI runs: lint, tests, docs build"]:::auto
  D -->|"a job fails"| A
  D -->|"all jobs pass"| E["Review"]:::you
  E --> F["Merge to main"]:::you
  F --> G["Docs deploy to GitHub Pages"]:::auto

Legend: blue boxes are things you do; grey boxes happen by themselves. The arrows going back to "Edit" show that a failed check sends you back to fix it.

Never skip the hooks with git commit --no-verify. If a check is wrong, fix the check in its own PR.

Planned: add a hook that runs scripts/check_docs_diagrams.py on changed docs. For now run make docs-check yourself when you change a diagram.

docs.title: Documentation Review — docs/
docs.text:
A holistic alignment audit of every Markdown file under docs/ against the canonical system description.

Note on the reference doc. The originating issue (footy_track-5h0) asks for alignment against system_design.md, but no such file exists in the repo. The closest match — and the file explicitly self-identifying as "the single authoritative reference for contributors and agents" (docs/system_overview.md:3) — is system_overview.md, which is what this review uses as the canonical baseline. Recommend either renaming system_overview.md → system_design.md or updating downstream docs/beads to use the existing name.

This is a flag-only report; fixes are out of scope.

docs.title: Summary table
docs.text: Doc Aligned with system_overview.md? Code drift? Internal contradictions index.md Partial Naming inconsistency Footy Scan vs footy-track vs football-scan development.md Partial cd football-scan ≠ package name Same naming issue pipeline_architecture.md Good None Tracking status unclear pipelines.md Poor — describes a 6-stage design that does not exist in code Massive Contradicts system_overview.md outright timings.md Good None None data_formats.md Poor Entry points + class list wrong Class list differs from training.md training.md Partial "keeper" class doesn't exist in code Class list differs from data_formats.md training/notable_runs.md Good None Reference run only reproducible with the (unversioned) local binary dataset design/player_tracking_format.md Good (explicitly DRAFT) None — Parquet schema not yet implemented None agent_guidelines.md Good None Has a typo on line 1

docs.title: 1. pipelines.md describes a system that doesn't exist
docs.text:
docs/pipelines.md:13–175 describes a six-stage video pipeline (frame embeddings, overhead-shot classification via clustering, OCR for the in-game clock, field-line matching, homography estimation, camera-geometry synchronisation). None of this exists in src/:

  • no embeddings module
  • no OCR
  • no field-line / homography code
  • no overhead-shot classifier in the live pipeline (classifier.py is used for Roboflow dataset labelling, not live filtering — labelling.py)

system_overview.md:7–31 describes a three-stage pipeline (InputConsumer → Processor (Detection/Tracking/Event) → OutputProducer) which matches the actual code.

Neither doc labels its status. A reader cannot tell which is current and which is aspirational. Either delete pipelines.md, mark it DRAFT / future-state at the top, or fold its concrete bits into pipeline_architecture.md.

docs.title: 2. Detection-class lists disagree across three docs and the code
docs.text:
The detection class taxonomy is given inconsistently in three places:

Source Classes system_overview.md:121–135 person, ball, in_play_ball, out_of_play_ball, player, player_sub, referee, coach (8) training.md:90 coach, in_play_ball, person, player, player_sub, referee, + keeper (7+keeper) data_formats.md:83–84 player, player_sub, coach, referee, keeper, in_play_ball, person (7+keeper) src/footy_track/constants.py:9–16 (truth) ball, person, out_of_play_ball, in_play_ball, player, player_sub, referee, coach (8)

keeper/goalkeeper is not a constant. detectors/ultralytics.py collapses goalkeeper detections to PLAYER_TAG. Two docs invent a keeper class that the code doesn't have. Pick one canonical taxonomy (probably constants.py) and align the other docs.

docs.title: 3. Non-existent CLI entry points referenced
docs.text:
docs/data_formats.md:35 tells the reader to run:

uv run footy-track-extract-frames data/arsenal_mancity/original_video/match.mp4 ...

The only entry point defined in pyproject.toml is scripts.footy-track = "footy_track:main". There is no footy-track-extract-frames, no footy-track-classify-frames, and no training-script entry point. Anyone copy-pasting this fails immediately. The actual scripts live at src/footy_track/scripts/*.py and must be invoked as uv run python src/footy_track/scripts/extract_frames.py ….

docs.title: 4. agent_guidelines.md has a typo on line 1
docs.text: docs/agent_guidelines.md:1 reads Rea# Agent and Tooling Guidelines — the leading Rea is garbage and breaks the H1. Should be # Agent and Tooling Guidelines.

docs.title: 5. Tracking status is unclear
docs.text: system_overview.md:49–54 calls Stage 2 (Tracking) "planned" — not yet implemented. pipeline_architecture.md:13–14 describes tracking as one of three optionally-decomposable stages without saying whether it currently exists. There's no single doc stating the current status, the roadmap, or how a contributor would enable it. The repo does have a tracking/ concept referenced (e.g. lap for Hungarian assignment per the workspace-level CLAUDE.md) but no doc describes the actual implementation surface.

docs.title: 6. Broadcast classifier role is mis-described
docs.text: system_overview.md:60–64 and the design notes around line 214 imply the broadcast-frame classifier is an optional pre-filter for live detection. In code, classifier.py + labelling.py is a dataset-curation tool that labels Roboflow uploads as Yes / No. There is no live filtering happening in the detection pipeline.

docs.title: 7. Metaflow is acknowledged but not documented
docs.text: system_overview.md:204–206 mentions metaflow/ exists for "batch processing pipelines" but says nothing more. No doc describes which flows exist, how to run them, or whether they're production / experimental. The metaflow/ directory in the repo has flow definitions but no README and no mkdocs nav entry.

docs.title: 8. Naming drift: Footy Scan vs footy-track vs football-scan
docs.text:
• index.md:3 and index.md:7: "Footy Scan" (marketing).
  • pyproject.toml:9: package name footy-track.
  • development.md:10: tells you to cd football-scan (a path that doesn't match the package). The aakevy06 W&B run was historically also produced from a football-scan directory.

This is mostly cosmetic but onboarding contributors will be briefly confused. Pick one external name and one repo/dir name and flatten the others.

docs.title: 9. SAM3 detector — undocumented config surface
docs.text: system_overview.md:45–46 describes the SAM3 detector capabilities (text prompts, per-prompt confidence thresholds, centre-distance NMS) but not that prompts and thresholds are hard-coded in _prompt_specs (detectors/ultralytics.py:113–131) or that there is a bbox_padding_percent parameter (line 102). For anyone trying to retune it, this matters.

docs.title: 10. training.md reference run note is missing
docs.text: training/notable_runs.md is internally consistent and the reference-run analysis is solid. One small gap: it doesn't note that aakevy06's reproducer (nsrl1x1g) only succeeded against a local binary dataset that is not under DVC or version control. There is no path to reproduce aakevy06 from a clean checkout. Recommend filing a bead to put the binary v10 dataset under DVC or to cut a Roboflow version=11 with the Unlabeled class removed (already discussed in notable_runs.md).

docs.title: Recommended priority order for follow-up beads
docs.text:
1. (high) Resolve pipelines.md vs system_overview.md: either mark pipelines.md as future-state or delete it.

  3. (high) Fix the broken footy-track-extract-frames invocation in data_formats.md:35 (and audit other docs for similarly-stale entry-point examples).
  4. (low) Fix the Rea# … typo in agent_guidelines.md:1.

  6. (med) Document metaflow/ flows; either give them their own page or expand system_overview.md:204–206.
  7. (med) Clarify tracking status in one canonical place.
  8. (low) Flatten the Footy Scan / footy-track / football-scan naming.

docs.title: Inference web app
docs.text:
Upload a match video in the browser. The app cuts it into broadcast shots, tracks the players, referees and ball on every shot, and shows each result as an overlay video with a short summary. It also stitches the whole upload back together into one "Full video": boxes on the broadcast shots, plain footage for everything the cutter dropped, in the original order. It is a front end for the existing pipeline: the cutting is scripts/split_broadcast_segments.py and the tracking is run_inference (see Inference pipeline). Nothing about the tracking itself is new.

Read the output with care

Ball recall is about 0.6, and the ball track can lock onto a false positive (for example a player's head) and follow it. Players and referees are tracked frame to frame only, with no team and no re-identification. Tracks restart at every broadcast cut. The results page repeats this in a banner.

docs.title: How a job flows
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U[Browser upload] --> S[Save file<br/>check it opens]
    S --> Q[Queue]
    Q --> C["Cut into shots<br/>split_broadcast_segments"]
    C --> T["Per clip: run_inference<br/>with overlay"]
    T --> E["Re-encode overlay<br/>to H.264"]
    E --> L["Work out the timeline<br/>tracked clips + gaps"]
    L --> F["Stitch full.mp4<br/>overlay clips + plain gaps"]
    F --> R[Results page]
    F -. "stitch fails: job still done,<br/>per-clip results kept" .-> R

Jobs run one at a time on a single worker thread, because there is one GPU. A second upload waits in the queue ("Waiting for the GPU"). The detector is loaded once and reused for every clip. A clip that fails (for example out of GPU memory) is marked failed and the other clips still finish.

docs.title: The full video
docs.text:
The cutter keeps only broadcast shots of at least a couple of seconds. Replays, crowd shots and short stretches are thrown away, so the clips alone do not add up to the match. To watch the whole upload in order, the app builds one full.mp4 per job once tracking is finished:

  • every tracked clip is shown as its overlay (boxes, ids, ball trail);
  • every stretch the clips do not cover (before the first clip, between clips, after the last) is copied from the original upload as plain footage, with no boxes;
  • a clip that failed to track, and the part of a clip that was not tracked because of the quick-run fields, also show as plain footage.

No detection or tracking runs on the plain stretches, so they cost only an encode. The results page opens on the "Full video" view by default. Under the player is a bar showing tracked (blue) and cutaway (dark) stretches; click it to jump, and a small "cutaway - not tracked" label appears while a plain stretch is playing. The per-clip views and downloads are unchanged, and full.mp4 has its own download button.

Details that matter:

  • Frame exact. Cuts are made in frame numbers, not rounded seconds, so full.mp4 has the same number of frames as the upload and every frame is in its original place. A clip starts at its start time times the frame rate, and the plain stretches are what is left between the clips.
  • No sound. Audio is dropped. The overlay clips never had any, and keeping the original track in step with a re-cut video is not worth the risk of drift.
  • Re-encoded. Every piece is encoded again with the same settings (H.264, yuv420p, no B-frames, even width and height, the upload's frame rate) so the pieces join cleanly. Tracked clips are therefore encoded twice (once for the overlay, once here) and are slightly softer than the per-clip overlay download. The size is similar to the upload for the plain parts. ffmpeg 5.1 or newer is needed.
  • Timeline. job.json (and GET /infer/api/jobs/<id>) has a timeline: a list of spans in time order with start_s, end_s, start_frame, end_frame, kind (tracked or skipped) and clip (the clip id for a tracked span, otherwise null). The spans cover the whole video without gaps. Odd frame rates such as 29.97 are handled exactly.
  • Failure is not fatal. If stitching fails (no ffmpeg, disk full, anything else) the job is still "done", the stitch stage is marked failed with a message, the timeline is kept and all per-clip results work. The results page then simply has no "Full video" button. Cancelling the job also stops a stitch in progress.
  • GET /infer/api/jobs/<id>/full.mp4 downloads it, with the same token rules as every other download; it answers 404 when there is none (older jobs, failed stitch).
  • The cutter decides where shots start and end, so a boxed stretch can begin or end a few frames away from where a human would cut. The stitch only follows what the cutter recorded.

docs.title: Preview quality (for slow networks)
docs.text:
The full-quality videos are large: a 1080p overlay is about 5.7 Mbit/s, so a 20 second clip is roughly 15 MB. On a slow or flaky connection (weak Wi-Fi, a phone on a bad link) the browser can receive that slower than it plays. Safari in particular then shows the first frame and sits there with the duration shown as "--:--".

So the app can also make a small preview copy of every overlay and of the full video:

  • about 720p (the same shape as the original, never enlarged), H.264, about 1 to 1.5 Mbit/s, no sound, the same number of frames and the same frame rate;
  • written with the index at the front of the file, so playback starts before the download has finished;
  • made right after each clip's overlay and after the full video is stitched, as overlay_preview.mp4 (per clip) and full_preview.mp4 (whole job), next to the full-quality files, which are never replaced.

On the results page a Quality: Preview (fast) / Full switch sits under the player. It defaults to Preview whenever one exists, remembers your choice in the browser, and keeps your place in the video when you switch. It applies to both the "Full video" view and each clip. The download buttons always include the full-quality files; the preview files are offered as extra downloads.

It is a server option, on by default. Turn it off with FOOTY_INFERENCE_PREVIEW=0 or --no-preview if you only use fast networks and want to save the (small) extra encode time and disk space. GET /infer/api/config reports preview: true or false, and each job lists the state of its previews (preview on a clip, full_preview on the job: done, failed or off).

A preview is a convenience, so it can never break a job: if making one fails (no ffmpeg, disk full) the clip and the job still finish, the failure is logged and recorded in the job, and the page simply shows no quality switch for that video. Cancelling a job also stops a preview in progress. Jobs made before this option existed have no previews and work as before (the switch is hidden).

docs.title: Run it on the GPU machine
docs.text:
The app is meant to run on the machine that has the GPU and the detector weights, and to be opened from other devices over a private network such as Tailscale. There is no remote-job plumbing: the browser talks straight to the app.

# on the GPU machine, in the repo, with the project environment
make infer-web HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=8080
# or
python -m footy_track.inference.web --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

Then open http://<the machine's private name or address>:8080/infer from a laptop or phone on the same private network. On WSL, run it inside the WSL distro; reaching it through Tailscale needs Tailscale to be running where the app is listening (inside WSL, or on the Windows host with the port forwarded). Do not forward the port to the public internet.

Needs: the detector checkpoint (CURRENT_BEST_DETECTOR_CHECKPOINT, not in git), the broadcast classifier weights, and ffmpeg on the PATH (to cut clips and to make the overlay playable in browsers). Without the checkpoint the app refuses to start and says where it looked.

Notes that matter on the WSL box:

  • If the WSL virtual machine is down, nothing answers. That looks like a network problem but is not one; start WSL from the Windows side first.
  • The app does not use dataloader workers, so the "workers must be 0" training rule does not apply to it. It runs detection in the app process.
  • Run it in tmux so it survives an ssh disconnect.

docs.title: Try it without a GPU
docs.text: make infer-web-fake (or FOOTY_INFERENCE_FAKE=1) swaps in a fake detector and a cutter that just makes fixed 100-frame chunks, leaving a 25-frame gap after each one (so there are cutaways to stitch), so the whole flow can be tried with no weights. Development only: the boxes it draws are invented and the chunks are not broadcast shots. The upload page shows a banner while it is on.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
• Upload (/infer): drop a file. The page shows uploading, cutting, then "tracking clip i of n". Optional quick-run fields cap the frames per clip or take every Nth frame.
  • Jobs (/infer/jobs): all jobs, with status and delete.
  • Results (/infer/jobs/<id>): watch the "Full video", or pick a clip and watch its overlay, read the summary (frames, fps, player and referee tracklets, ball detected, interpolated and none), and download the overlay, the cut clip, detections.jsonl, tracklets.jsonl, ball_track.jsonl and summary.json. Formats are in Inference pipeline.

The same API works from a script. Upload is the raw file as the request body:

curl --data-binary @match.mp4 "http://host:8080/infer/api/jobs?name=match.mp4&max_frames=200"
curl http://host:8080/infer/api/jobs/<id>

docs.title: Demo clip
docs.text:
To let a visitor see the pipeline in one click, point the app at a sample video kept on the server (not in git):

FOOTY_INFERENCE_DEMO_CLIP=/path/to/sample.mp4 make infer-web
# or: python -m footy_track.inference.web --demo-clip /path/to/sample.mp4

The upload page then shows a "Try a demo clip" button. It starts a normal job from a copy of that file (cut, track, overlay), with no upload, and honours the quick-run fields. If the variable is unset or the file is missing, the button is hidden. The server path is never sent to the browser; GET /infer/api/config reports only demo (true or false) and, when true, demo_name and demo_duration_s. From a script:

curl -X POST "http://host:8080/infer/api/demo?max_frames=200"

It needs the same token as the rest of the API, and answers 404 when no demo clip is available.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Environment variables, with command-line flags that win over them.

Variable Flag Default Meaning FOOTY_INFERENCE_JOBS_DIR --jobs-dir runs/web Where jobs are stored FOOTY_INFERENCE_WEIGHTS --weights CURRENT_BEST_DETECTOR_CHECKPOINT Detector checkpoint FOOTY_INFERENCE_DEVICE --device auto (cuda, mps, cpu) Detector device FOOTY_INFERENCE_MAX_UPLOAD_MB --max-upload-mb 8192 Upload size limit FOOTY_INFERENCE_TOKEN none unset Optional shared token, see below FOOTY_INFERENCE_DEMO_CLIP --demo-clip unset Sample video for the demo button FOOTY_INFERENCE_PREVIEW --preview / --no-preview on Also make small preview videos for slow networks FOOTY_INFERENCE_FAKE --fake off Dev-only fake detector and cutter

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text: Each job is a folder under the jobs directory with a job.json (status of each stage and clip, the timeline, counts, timings, errors), the upload, the cut clips, one output folder per clip, full.mp4 and the optional full_preview.mp4 (each clip folder also has overlay_preview.mp4). Folder and file names are generated; the uploaded file name is only shown on the page. The state file is rewritten safely, so finished jobs are still there after a restart. A job that was running during a restart is marked failed ("the server restarted"), and half-finished uploads are removed. Deleting a job removes its folder. A running job must be cancelled first.

docs.title: Limits and failure cases
docs.text:
• No auth beyond an optional token. Uploads run on a GPU machine, so only expose the app on a private network. If FOOTY_INFERENCE_TOKEN is set, the API and downloads need it (as Authorization: Bearer, ?token=, or a cookie that the pages set after asking once). The HTML pages themselves hold no data. It is a single shared secret over plain HTTP, not a login system.
  • Upload size is capped (default 8 GB) and checked while streaming, so an oversized upload is cut off and removed. Accepted extensions: mp4, mov, mkv, ts, avi, webm, m4v.
  • Bad file: if OpenCV cannot open it or read a frame, the upload is rejected with a clear message and nothing is kept.
  • No broadcast shots found: the job fails with an explanation (the cutter keeps only broadcast footage of at least two seconds).
  • Overlay playback: OpenCV writes mp4v, which most browsers cannot play. The app re-encodes each overlay to H.264 with ffmpeg. If ffmpeg is missing or fails, the original is kept, the results page says so, and you can still download it and play it locally.
  • Speed: RT-DETR at 1280 px needs a GPU. A full match has many clips and takes a while; use the quick-run fields for a preview. Cancelling stops at the next batch of frames.
  • Full video size and time: encoding every plain stretch and every tracked clip again is CPU work: about 5 seconds for a 40 second 1080p video on the GPU machine, so expect on the order of ten minutes for a full match, and disk space about the size of the upload. It runs after tracking, so per-clip results appear first.
  • One job at a time. Progress on a clip is shown per clip, not per frame.
  • Not run end to end with real weights on a GPU as part of writing this; see the pull request for what was and was not tested.

docs.title: Why a separate app
docs.text: It is its own small FastAPI app (footy_track.inference.web) rather than a router on the labeller. It is meant to run alone on the GPU machine, and the labeller imports a large stack that inference does not need. The routes are an ordinary router (create_router), so they can be mounted into the labeller later if wanted.

docs.title: Side fix
docs.text: split_broadcast_segments.py classified frames on a hard-coded mps device, which fails on any non-Apple machine, including the CUDA box this app runs on. It now uses the same cuda, then mps, then cpu choice as inference.

docs.title: Not done yet
docs.text:
• Interactive in-browser overlay (draw the tracks on the original video, toggle players and ball) instead of a pre-rendered video.
  • A queue across several GPUs or machines.
  • Real authentication and per-user jobs.
  • Per-frame progress and a live preview while a clip is being tracked.
  • Choosing the cutter settings (sample rate, minimum shot length) on the upload page.
  • Ball-on-player guard and team assignment, which depend on the work listed in Inference pipeline.

docs.title: Inference pipeline
docs.text:
One command takes a broadcast video (or clip) and produces detections, tracked players and referees, and a tracked ball.

python -m footy_track.scripts.run_inference \
    --video data/arsenal_mancity_example_video.mp4 \
    --weights model_saves/detector/rtdetr_1920_v11/best.pt \
    --out runs/example --max-frames 300 --overlay

The checkpoint is not in git. --weights defaults to CURRENT_BEST_DETECTOR_CHECKPOINT. Quick runs: --start N, --max-frames N, --stride N (every Nth frame). The device is picked as cuda, then mps, then cpu; override with --device. Expect CPU to be very slow: RT-DETR-L at 1280 px is a GPU job.

flowchart LR
    V[video] --> D["RT-DETR @1280<br/>conf 0.1 or more"]
    D --> L[detections.jsonl]
    L --> P["LapTracker<br/>players, referees"]
    D --> B["DetectionBallTracker<br/>ball"]
    P --> T[tracklets.jsonl]
    B --> BT[ball_track.jsonl]

To use the pipeline from a browser (upload a whole match, get it cut into shots and tracked per clip, plus one stitched full video with boxes only on the broadcast shots), see Inference web app.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
All files are in --out. frame_index is the index in the source video.

File Format detections.jsonl Machine-label format (as machine_labels/): {frame_index, bbox{x,y,w,h}, center{x,y}, tags:[label,"rtdetr"], confidence, model_id, run_id, reviewed}. All detections at conf >= 0.1 are kept. tracklets.jsonl Same as scripts/track_detections.py: {frame_index, track_id, tags:[label,"lap"], bbox, confidence, is_interpolated}. Players and referees only. ball_track.jsonl New, one row per processed frame: {frame_index, track_id, source, bbox, center, confidence}. source is detected, interpolated (gap bridged between two detections, confidence null) or none (bbox, center, track_id null). summary.json Frames, fps, detection and track counts, ball coverage, timings, run config, checkpoint, git SHA. overlay.mp4 With --overlay: boxes, track ids, ball with a short trail.

Bounding boxes are normalised x, y, w, h with (x, y) the top-left corner.

docs.title: Thresholds and why
docs.text:
Players and referees reuse the measured defaults in scripts/track_detections.py (conf 0.5, iou 0.15, max age 90). Purity of those tracklets is not measured.

The ball detector's precision depends heavily on confidence (Ball Check verdicts):

conf 0.1-0.2 0.2-0.3 0.3-0.4 0.4-0.5 0.5-0.6 0.6-0.7 0.7-0.8 0.8-0.9 precision 0.04 0.29 0.23 0.36 0.42 0.79 0.96 1.00

The sampler oversampled near the decision boundary, so read these as per-band, not global, precision. The ball tracker uses that as follows (ball_trackers/detection_tracker.py):

  • --ball-start-conf 0.6: a track starts only on a candidate that is usually right. 0.5 would start on a coin flip.
  • --ball-jump-conf 0.8: a candidate this strong is believed even outside the gate, so a false start cannot hold the track hostage.
  • Gate --ball-base-radius-px 40 + --ball-growth-px 25 * frames_since_last, around a constant-velocity prediction. Weaker candidates get a proportionally smaller gate (confidence / start conf), so a 0.15 candidate must be close.
  • --ball-max-missed 12: the track ends after 12 consecutive missed frames. Gaps bridged before that are interpolated and marked as such.

These numbers are starting points chosen from the bands above, not tuned against ground truth. Ball tracking evaluation now scores this tracker against human ball marks.

Two offline ball trackers are available as options with --ball-tracker (online is the default and what the web app uses):

  • bidirectional: runs the online tracker forwards and backwards in time and keeps the better supported answer per frame. It fixes tracks that start on a confident false positive.
  • viterbi: picks the best single path through all of the clip's candidates. It is the most precise and gives up the most recall.

Both need the whole clip, so they work for files but not for live output, they use their own tuned defaults (the --ball-* flags above configure only online), and they write the same ball_track.jsonl.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Broadcast cuts break tracks: players get new ids and the ball track restarts. Run per shot clip (see split_broadcast_segments.py) for best results.
  • Ball recall is about 0.6 on held-out clips; the tracker recovers some of the rest. See Ball tracking evaluation for scored numbers against human ball marks.
  • A persistent false positive can capture the ball track. In the 60-frame demo the track sat on a player's head at confidence 0.7-0.8 for 50 frames while the camera panned; nothing here checks whether the "ball" moves with a player.
  • No projection to pitch coordinates, no team assignment, no re-identification.
  • Without a GPU the detector runs at well under 1 frame per second.

docs.title: Open decisions / revisit later
docs.text:
Each open item below has a NOTE(revisit) comment in the code where the decision lives (the last item is already fixed, so it has none).

  • Ball start threshold (0.6). A track only starts on a detection of 0.6 or more, because the 0.5-0.6 band is only about 42% precise. This and the other tracker numbers are starting points, not tuned. Re-tune once the ball evaluation (T-10) gives real scores.
  • No guard against a ball stuck on a player. If the detector keeps finding a "ball" on a player's head, the tracker follows it. We chose not to add a guard before there is ground truth to test it against. Revisit as T-34 once T-10 exists.
  • The ball tracker is outside the BallTracker protocol. That protocol hands over pixels, this tracker consumes detections. Revisit if a second detections-based tracker appears.
  • ball_track.jsonl has no shared schema. It stays a documented minimal format until the projection step needs to read it.
  • Labeller detector ignored predict_kwargs (fixed). predict_from_path in the labeller's detector used to skip the configured confidence and image size. That was fixed in a separate change (PR #29, merged), so the labeller detector now honours them.

docs.title: Pipeline Interfaces
docs.text: Names, responsibilities, and data contracts for each component in the footy-track pipeline. Implementation details live in the source; this document records what each component promises, not how it delivers it.

docs.title: InputConsumer
docs.text:
Responsibility: Read a video source (file or live feed), decode frames, and yield them with timestamps.

Contract: - Accepts a video file path or stream URI. - Yields frames paired with GameTime and GameMetadata (half number, half_start_continuous). - Does not interpret frame content — that is the detector's job.

Output per frame: 

Frame(
    image_path: Path,      # path to extracted frame image
    game_time: float,      # seconds on the referee clock for this frame
    game_metadata: GameMetadata,
)

docs.title: BroadcastClassifier
docs.text:
Responsibility: Decide whether a frame is a pitch view worth running detection on.

Contract: - Accepts a frame image path. - Returns a BroadcastClassification with a Yes/No label and confidence. - Must be cheap enough to run on every frame. - Does not modify frame data or produce bounding boxes.

Interface: 

classify(image_path: Path) → BroadcastClassification

Output: 

BroadcastClassification(
    label: "Yes" | "No",
    confidence: float | None,
)

docs.title: ObjectDetector
docs.text:
Responsibility: Locate all objects of interest in a single frame and return their bounding boxes and labels.

Contract: - Accepts a frame image path. - Returns a FrameDetections containing all detected objects. - All bounding boxes are normalized [x, y, w, h] with top-left origin, values in [0, 1]. - Does not maintain state across frames.

Interface: 

predict_from_path(image_path: Path) → FrameDetections

Output: 

FrameDetections(
    uri: Path,
    width: int,
    height: int,
    detections: list[ObjectDetection],
)

ObjectDetection(
    label: str,        # one of DETECTION_CLASSES
    confidence: float,
    x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float,  # normalized, top-left origin
    model: str | None,
)

Known labels (from constants.py): person, ball, in_play_ball, out_of_play_ball, player, player_sub, referee, coach.

docs.title: Tracker (planned)
docs.text:
Responsibility: Associate detections across consecutive frames to produce persistent object IDs.

Contract: - Accepts a FrameDetections for the current frame. - Returns the same detections annotated with stable track_id integers. - Maintains internal state between calls — must be called in frame order. - Handles object entry (new ID) and exit (ID retired) gracefully.

Interface: 

update(detections: FrameDetections) → TrackedFrameDetections

Output: 

TrackedFrameDetections(
    uri: Path,
    width: int,
    height: int,
    detections: list[TrackedDetection],  # ObjectDetection + track_id: int
)

docs.title: EventExtractor (planned)
docs.text:
Responsibility: Infer higher-level match events (passes, shots, tackles, substitutions, set-pieces) from tracked trajectories.

Contract: - Consumes a window of TrackedFrameDetections (not a single frame). - Emits zero or more MatchEvent records when an event boundary is detected. - Events carry ContinuousTime timestamps, not GameTime. - Does not modify or re-emit detection data.

Interface: 

process(frames: Iterable[TrackedFrameDetections]) → Iterator[MatchEvent]

Output: 

MatchEvent(
    event_type: str,          # e.g. "pass", "shot", "tackle"
    continuous_time: float,   # seconds from first-half kickoff
    player_ids: list[int],    # track IDs involved
    coordinates: ...,         # pitch coordinates if available
)

docs.title: OutputProducer
docs.text:
Responsibility: Serialize pipeline outputs and write them to disk, a message bus, or an API.

Contract: - Accepts any pipeline record (FrameDetections, BroadcastClassification, MatchEvent). - Supports JSON (one record per line) and CSV (flattened table view) formats. - All written records include a continuous_time field. - Does not perform inference or modify records.

Interface: 

write(record: PipelineRecord) → None
flush() → None

docs.title: Time contract (applies to all components)
docs.text:
Every record produced by any component must include a continuous_time: float field representing seconds from first-half kickoff. This is the canonical timestamp for alignment, resampling, and merging across sources.

GameTime values from the video source are converted to ContinuousTime by InputConsumer using GameMetadata.half_start_continuous. No downstream component should receive raw GameTime values.

See docs/timings.md for the full conversion formula.

docs.title: Data flow summary
docs.text:
InputConsumer
  └─► Frame(image_path, game_time, game_metadata)
        │
        ▼
BroadcastClassifier
  └─► BroadcastClassification(label="Yes"|"No", confidence)
        │ (Yes only)
        ▼
ObjectDetector
  └─► FrameDetections(uri, width, height, detections=[ObjectDetection, ...])
        │
        ▼
Tracker  [planned]
  └─► TrackedFrameDetections(... detections=[TrackedDetection(track_id), ...])
        │
        ▼
EventExtractor  [planned]
  └─► MatchEvent(event_type, continuous_time, player_ids, coordinates)
        │
        ▼
OutputProducer
  └─► JSON / CSV on disk, message bus, or API

docs.title: Labeller requirements
docs.text: Moved: the canonical labeller specification (requirement IDs LAB-nnn, test traceability, OPEN items) lives at src/footy_track/labeller/README.md.

docs.title: SAM3 Labeller — Single-Timeline Design (authoritative)
docs.text: The web labeller's bugs (dropped edits, wrong restart frame, scrambled labels, boxes drifting) all came from multiple disconnected box stores. This replaces them with one server-owned timeline as the single source of truth.

docs.title: Source of truth: the timeline
docs.text:
Session.timeline: list[list[Box] | None], length = total_frames. Each Box = ObjectDetection (normalized x,y,w,h, label) whose model field records provenance:

  • "labeller" — a manual edit. Ground truth.
  • "yolo" — YOLO auto-detect.
  • "sam3" — SAM3 propagation.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
• labeller > {yolo, sam3}. yolo and sam3 are peers (for now).
  • A per-box rule: labeller boxes always win and are never overwritten by yolo/sam3 on any frame.

docs.title: Who writes to the timeline
docs.text: Actor Writes Provenance Respects YOLO auto-detect timeline[N] yolo replaces non-labeller boxes at N SAM3 propagation timeline[N+1..] sam3 keeps each frame's labeller boxes, replaces yolo/sam3 User edit timeline[frame] labeller overwrites that frame

docs.title: SAM3 merge into a frame (per-box hierarchy)
docs.text:
When SAM3 produces boxes for frame F: 

new_frame = [b for b in timeline[F] if b.model == "labeller"]   # keep ground truth
          + sam3_boxes                                          # add propagated
timeline[F] = new_frame
So your edits on any downstream frame survive a re-propagation; only the yolo/sam3 boxes get replaced.

docs.title: Restart semantics
docs.text: Restart from frame N: 1. Seed = timeline[N] verbatim (whatever is there — your edits if you edited, else yolo/sam3 boxes). 2. Frame N is left untouched (it's the ground-truth seed). 3. SAM3 propagates N+1 → end, writing into the timeline with the merge rule above (labeller boxes on those frames are preserved).

docs.title: Client (thin)
docs.text:
• Renders GET /timeline/{frame} for the viewed frame.
  • On edit: POST /edit {frame, objects} → server writes labeller boxes.
  • WS run/restart {start_frame} → server seeds from timeline[start_frame].
  • Live: WS streams {frame, idx}; client fetches/renders that frame from the timeline (or receives boxes inline).
  • No client-side box cache. No frameEdits. The timeline is authoritative.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Purpose POST /session/load open video, allocate empty timeline GET /frame/{idx}.jpg raw frame image GET /timeline/{idx} boxes at idx (with provenance) POST /edit {idx, objects} → write labeller boxes at idx POST /autodetect {idx} → write yolo boxes at idx, return them WS /ws run/restart/pause; streams propagated frame indices

docs.title: The N+1 drift bug (fold into rebuild)
docs.text: Auto-detect (frame N) is correct but the first propagated frame (N+1) drifts. Suspect: seed boxes are scaled with SESSION.width/height but Sam3VideoLabeller re-reads its own video_dimensions; if they differ the seed region is wrong. During the rebuild: seed Sam3VideoLabeller from timeline[N] using ONE agreed dimension source, and verify the first propagated frame lands on the players (Playwright + a numeric check).

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
1. Add timeline to Session + the merge/seed helpers (server.py).
  2. Point /autodetect, /edit, WS run/restart at the timeline.
  3. Have the SAM3 worker write into timeline with the merge rule (seed frame verbatim already implemented via _seed_frame_detections).
  4. Strip client frameEdits; client reads/writes the timeline only.
  5. Verify drift + restart + edit-persistence end-to-end.

docs.title: Future: selectable tracking engine (after timeline is solid)
docs.text: A later enhancement: choose SAM3 OR YOLO-tracking (UltralyticsTracker / ByteTrack) as the propagation engine. - SAM3: prompt-driven — seed boxes on frame N steer it. - YOLO-track: detector-driven — re-detects + assigns IDs each frame; does NOT take seed boxes. Fills the timeline with yolo provenance. Restart = re-run from frame N onward. Your labeller edits remain ground truth (merge rule), but don't "re-seed" it. Both write into the same timeline with provenance, so the timeline model is engine-agnostic. Deferred until the SAM3 correction loop is working.

docs.title: SAM3 Video Labeller — Web App Design (FastAPI + Canvas)
Why move off Streamlit
docs.text:
The labeller is an interactive, stateful, frame-by-frame video annotation tool with mid-flight model correction. Streamlit's model (re-run the whole script on every interaction, no client-side state, fixed-pixel canvas, no selection feedback) fights this at every turn. Every recurring bug this session — flashing loops, ghost/doubled rows, frozen scrubbing, sluggishness, width misalignment — traces back to whole-script reruns and the drawable-canvas's inability to report state back to Python.

Off-the-shelf tools (CVAT / Label Studio / FiftyOne) don't fit either: they treat the model as a black-box pre-labeller and have no concept of pause propagation → correct → resume from here, which is the core workflow. Managed versions also cost money to run models.

So: a custom local web app. The minimum that supports the correction loop is a long-lived server that owns the hot SAM3 model + a real frontend canvas that owns interaction state.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Browser (single-page app)                   │
│  • Konva/Fabric canvas: draw/edit/select    │
│  • Frame scrubber + playback                │
│  • Class dropdown, tool toggle, run/pause   │
│  • Holds ALL interaction state client-side  │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                │  WebSocket (control + frame stream)
                │  HTTP (load video, fetch a frame image)
┌───────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
│ FastAPI server (one process, model hot)     │
│  • Wraps the existing BackgroundLabeller /   │
│    Sam3VideoLabeller (reused as-is)          │
│  • SAM3 predictor stays resident in memory   │
│  • Streams propagated FrameDetections        │
│  • Serves frame images (jpeg) on demand      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The backend is essentially the current BackgroundLabeller promoted from a Streamlit-session object to a server-owned singleton. No re-derivation per interaction — that single change removes the whole class of bugs.

docs.title: Backend (FastAPI)
docs.text:
Reuse, almost unchanged: - Sam3VideoLabeller (labeller/video_utils.py:236) — iter_frames_from(start_frame, stop_event, …) - BackgroundLabeller (:507) — submit(...), pause(), completed_frames() - get_cached_predictor(...) — model stays hot (already implemented) - _yolo_seed_objects(...) — auto-detect seeds (move from app.py into a service module)

New thin layer: labeller/server.py

docs.title: HTTP endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Purpose POST /session/load {video_path} → opens video, returns {fps, total_frames, width, height}. Wipes prior results. GET /frame/{idx}.jpg Raw frame image (no boxes; the canvas draws boxes itself). Cached. POST /autodetect {frame_idx, conf, iou, model?} → YOLO seeds for that frame as boxes. GET /detections/{idx} Propagated FrameDetections for a completed frame (for scrubbing). POST /export Save labels JSON.

docs.title: WebSocket /ws (control + stream)
docs.text:
Client → server messages: - {type: "run", objects, imgsz, conf, start_frame: 0} - {type: "restart", objects, start_frame, imgsz, conf} ← objects = corrected boxes - {type: "pause"}

Server → client messages: - {type: "status", state: "compiling"|"running"|"paused"|"idle"} - {type: "frame", idx, detections} — emitted per propagated frame (the live stream) - {type: "anomaly", idx} — track jump/area anomaly detected; server auto-paused - {type: "done", last_frame} - {type: "error", message}

The server pushes frame messages as BackgroundLabeller produces them — no polling. Anomaly detection (_has_track_anomaly) stays server-side and emits the anomaly message instead of the Streamlit auto-pause hack.

docs.title: State ownership
docs.text: • Server owns: the video handle, the hot predictor, the propagated completed[] timeline, run/pause state. One session per server (single user, local) keeps it simple — no multi-tenant session map needed for v1.

docs.title: Frontend (single page)
docs.text:
Stack: plain Vite + TypeScript + Konva (or Svelte if you prefer components). No framework lock-in needed; one page.

Components: - Canvas (Konva Stage): background = /frame/{idx}.jpg; a Layer of editable rectangles. Konva gives selection, drag, resize, transform handles, delete — natively, with no server round-trip. Each rect carries {label}; colour by class. - Scrubber: a range slider + prev/next + play. Scrubbing to frame N fetches /frame/N.jpg + /detections/N and renders read-only (or editable when paused). Smooth because it's client-side. - Toolbar: Edit/Draw toggle, class dropdown, Auto-detect button, Run/Pause, Restart-from-current-frame. Show-boxes toggle. - Object list panel: rows synced to canvas rects; click a row ↔ selects the rect (bidirectional — trivial in Konva, impossible in Streamlit). Class dropdown + delete per row.

docs.title: Interaction flow (the workflow that Streamlit couldn't do cleanly)
docs.text:
1. Load video → /autodetect frame 0 → seeds render on canvas (editable).
  2. Edit boxes client-side (instant, no reruns) → Run sends {run, objects}.
  3. Server streams frame messages → canvas shows live propagated frames.
  4. Pause (or auto anomaly) → client switches canvas to editable on the current/anomaly frame, prefilled with that frame's detections.
  5. Scrub freely (client-side, smooth) to find where it went wrong; the Restart-from-current-frame button sends {restart, objects, start_frame} using the currently viewed frame — no ambiguity, no rerun races.
  6. Repeat; Export when happy.

docs.title: What this fixes vs Streamlit
docs.text: Streamlit problem Resolved by Sluggish / clunky No whole-script reruns; canvas edits are local Flashing / ghost rows No widget-key churn; DOM owned by frontend Frozen / wrong scrub frames Client fetches the right frame + detections directly Can't tell which box is selected Konva reports selection natively → row highlight Width misalignment Responsive CSS layout Live frames need polling hack WebSocket push Model re-derived per rerun Server owns the hot predictor for its lifetime

docs.title: Scope / effort
docs.text:
• Backend: ~150–250 lines (server.py) — mostly wiring existing BackgroundLabeller to FastAPI + a WebSocket loop. Logic already exists.
  • Frontend: ~400–600 lines (one page: canvas, scrubber, toolbar, list, WS client). The bulk of new work.
  • Launch: uvicorn footy_track.labeller.server:app; frontend built with Vite and served as static files by FastAPI (single command, no separate dev server needed in prod).

docs.title: Risks / open questions
docs.text:
• Frame serving cost: decoding arbitrary frames on demand via cv2 seek is fine for scrubbing; for smooth playback we may pre-extract or cache a window.
  • Single-session assumption: v1 assumes one user/one video at a time (local use). Multi-session would need a session registry — out of scope for v1.
  • Frontend build toolchain: adds Node/Vite to the repo. If undesirable, a no-build option (vanilla JS + Konva from CDN, served by FastAPI) keeps it Python-only to run, at some ergonomic cost.

docs.title: Migration path (incremental, low-risk)
docs.text:
1. Build server.py wrapping BackgroundLabeller; verify the WS frame stream with a trivial HTML test page (no Konva yet).
  2. Add the Konva canvas + draw/edit + Run/stream (the vertical slice).
  3. Add pause → correct → restart-from-current-frame.
  4. Add scrubbing, object-list sync, auto-detect, export.
  5. Retire app.py once parity is reached (keep it until then).

The existing video_utils.py backend is the asset — it carries straight over. Only the Streamlit presentation layer (app.py) is replaced.

docs.title: Best pipeline and label needs
docs.text:
Research of 2026-11-08 against main @ 26d2506. Evidence tags: [V] verified against code, data or run logs; [H] stated only in <storage>/tools/HANDOFF.md (2026-08-28) or a doc, not re-checked; [I] inference. Context: Architecture, Datasets and labels, TODO list.

Update 2026-11-21: the plan is now two detectors (ball; player/referee/coach/person) instead of one multi-class RT-DETR, so "Detection (ball, players, refs)" below describes the historical single model. See full_frame_labelling.md.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The best measured ball detector is RT-DETR-L trained at 1920 on Roboflow v11: ball mAP50 0.665, recall 0.591 on v11-val [V]. The older ".221 / .209" quoted next to it was yolo11n on v11 (xeval.log); it was pasted next to the RT-DETR path by commit 24229bb (2026-08-29). The comment in detectors/ultralytics.py and the docs now say so.
  • The number is not a multi-match estimate: 156 of the 211 val balls (74%) come from one 10-second clip (arsenal_example) [V]. The production machine labels were made at imgsz 1280 while the checkpoint was trained at 1920 [V].
  • No ball tracker exists in code. Misses are dominated by long blind spells [H], so the next gains are a tracker for precision and diversity of labels, not more frames from the same clips.
  • Four label-pipeline bugs (T-01 to T-04) will corrupt the next training export; fix them before any retrain.

docs.title: 1. Best measured pipeline
docs.text:
Stage Component Status Shot segmentation split_broadcast_segments.py with yolo11n-cls 0.987.pt Works; 0 interior cuts in 3,175 frames [H/doc] Detection (ball, players, refs) RT-DETR-L (rtdetr-l.pt init), fine-tuned on Roboflow v11, 50 epochs, imgsz 1920 rect, batch 4, RTX 5090, 2026-08-28. rtdetr_1920_v11/best.pt, 66.8 MB, not in git Measured [V] Tiling / ROI None. One full-frame pass. Batch inference imgsz 1280, half, conf 0.1 or more; 162 Man City clips, 97,625 frames, 2,767,151 boxes. Script not in repo. Produced [V] Ball tracker None wired. VitTrack (labeller only) stays on the ball 9/176 frames. UNSOLVED Confidence threshold No operating point chosen in code (get_current_best_detector(min_confidence=0.3)). Player tracking LapTracker over machine labels. Fragmentation measured; purity, IDF1, HOTA unmeasured. Partial Team, gap bridging, ReID Team not computed; linker unproven; cross-clip ImageNet embeddings at chance. Unproven

Players are the easy part: yolo11n at 1280 reaches player mAP50 0.974 (KB:footy-ball-detection-findings). RT-DETR's per-class player mAP was never logged.

docs.title: Ball detector leaderboard
docs.text:
v11-val, 215 images, 211 in_play_ball; Ultralytics val [V: <storage>/backups/vast_run_20260827-*/exp.log, vast5090_final_20260828-195228/exp5090.log, 20260826-214555/trainlogs/{xeval.log,rtdetr_ep9_val.json}].

Model, train imgsz, data, epochs ball mAP50 mAP50-95 P R Weights exist? RT-DETR-L @1280, v11, 50 ep (A4000) 0.668 0.364 0.852 0.602 No, logs only RT-DETR-L @1920 rect, v11, 50 ep (5090) = production 0.665 0.360 0.862 0.591 Yes yolo11m @1280, v11 0.451 0.241 0.775 0.327 No yolo11l @1280, v11 0.364 0.198 0.894 0.240 No RT-DETR-L @1280, v3, 50 ep 0.328 0.166 0.912 0.244 Yes (object store, gpu_runs) RT-DETR-L @1280, v11, 9 ep 0.314 0.176 0.759 0.283 ? yolo11n @1280, v3 / v11 trained 0.250 / 0.221 0.846 / 0.763 0.209 / 0.209 yolo11s v3 @640 (old default) about 0 0.000 in git

The two top rows differ by noise (about 2 balls of 211). Corrections to the KB: (1) "more data did not help" holds for yolo11n only; with RT-DETR-L, v3 to v11 took mAP50 from 0.328 to 0.665 and recall from 0.244 to 0.59. (2) The capacity confound is tested: yolo11m/l lose clearly to RT-DETR-L. (3) v11 train has 1,010 balls, not 826.

docs.title: Held-out recall at the production setting
docs.text:
Machine labels (imgsz 1280) against tier 1/2 GT sidecars, Man City clips; a hit is a machine box within max(12 px, box size) of the GT centre [V, my matching rule]:

GT clips n balls r@0.1 r@0.3 r@0.5 r@0.7 Held out of v11 train 74 0.69 0.62 0.60 0.51 Overlap v11 train 330 0.96 0.92 0.88 0.71

Held-out recall at 1280 is about 0.6, consistent with 0.59 at 1920, but n=74 is dominated by one clip, and the overlap row shows memorisation.

docs.title: Ball Check precision by confidence band
docs.text:
257 decided verdicts on machine candidates (ball, corrected count as hits), measured from the verdict logs of 2026-09-24 and 09-25 [V]; recomputed counts of the 364 verdicts are in Datasets and labels. The sampler oversamples near the boundary, so these are per band, not global precision.

conf 0.1-0.2 0.2-0.3 0.3-0.4 0.4-0.5 0.5-0.6 0.6-0.7 0.7-0.8 0.8-0.9 precision 0.04 0.29 0.23 0.36 0.42 0.79 0.96 1.00 n 52 14 26 42 48 38 26 11

Boxes at 0.7 or more are near-certain, 0.6-0.7 mostly right, below 0.6 mostly wrong. A low-confidence second pass must therefore rely on motion gating. Human-checked vittrack ball boxes are about 97% right (81 verdicts: 71 ball, 6 corrected, 2 not_ball, 2 unsure).

docs.title: Is the benchmark trustworthy?
docs.text: Partly. The instance count is reasonable and val clips are disjoint from train at clip level [V], but 74% of val balls are one clip, so HANDOFF's "independent" confirmation (arsenal_example 0.585 against val 0.591) is the same clip. The v11 test split (268 images, 243 balls) has never been evaluated. Cross-match generalisation is unmeasured. Unverified: whether arsenal_example overlaps a Man City training clip in time.

docs.title: 2. Target pipeline
docs.text:
1. Per-frame RT-DETR-L at 1280 (keep it).
  2. An inference-only ball association layer over the stored conf 0.1 or more detections: ByteTrack/BoT-SORT-style low-confidence second pass, Kalman with high process noise and camera-motion compensation, gap interpolation.
  3. Later, a temporal detector: prior-conditioned RT-DETR (CenterTrack, bead ft-1zq), a heatmap over a frame stack (TrackNetV3, WASB), or YOLOFT-style correlation. The segmenter already gives cut-free clips.

What the data says [H + I]: misses are dominated by long blind spells (one 51-frame gap holds 70% of arsenal_example misses; only 7% fall in 1-2 frame gaps), so a t-1 prior is estimated to buy about 0.585 to 0.62 recall. The larger lever is diversity; a tracker mainly buys precision. The CenterTrack run reached epoch 11/80 before the desktop reset and no result is recorded.

Gaps between today and the target: no committed ball eval; no ball tracker in code; the producers are outside git (training command, batch inference, candidate filter, the temporal package, which exists only in <storage>/backups/temporal_work.tgz, and the ft-1zq code, only on the desktop machine); the held-out dense GT is too narrow to see a 0.03 gain; the label-plumbing seams corrupt exports; the 1920-train versus 1280-serve mismatch is unmeasured.

docs.title: 3. Label needs and gaps
docs.text:
Need Have Does the gap matter? Ball training boxes (tier 1/2) v11 train 1,010; sidecars 692 T1 + 825 T2 over 45 clips; T3 machine 352k Yes, for diversity not count. 520 of 1,035 v11 train images are one clip (astonvilla_seg080) and 212 another (bournemouth_1st_seg070). v3 to v11 doubled RT-DETR recall; more frames from the same long clips will not help. Player and referee boxes v11 15.5k player, 1.7k referee; sidecars 18.7k, 2.1k No. Players are about 0.97 mAP50. Hard negatives (not_ball verdicts, no_ball frames) 144 not_ball verdicts; 68 no_ball, 138 not_broadcast markers Moderate. not_ball verdicts are now stored in detection_review and dropped from exported positives (feature_store/ball_checks.py, scripts/export_training_dataset.py:85-97), but nothing trains on them as negatives yet (T-26). Below 0.6 confidence precision is 0.42 or less. Single-frame eval, 2 or more matches v11 val 211 (74% one clip); test 243 unused Yes, highest. Every decision depends on it. Dense ball-tracker eval (contiguous frames, explicit no_ball) arsenal_example (250 frames, 176 balls, video only as the example mp4), mancity_seg031 (53). Other long clips are in train. Yes. Needs about 5-10 held-out clips of 250+ frames from 2 or more matches, 1.5-3k balls [I]. Temporal training About 1,450-1,520 ball frames; 942 in runs of 3 or more (KB) No new label type; only after the eval exists. Identity (purity, jersey, merges, team) 9 reviews, 68 proposals, 0 team labels Defer; not needed for the ball.

How route J would address these gaps (planned, nothing built). The Claude-assisted ball labelling loop targets the first and third rows. For ball training boxes it aims at diversity: it runs on new matches first, so a person confirms doubtful frames instead of drawing every box. For hard negatives, every Claude "none" or Ball Check "no" on a candidate is a stored negative. It does not touch the single-frame eval or the dense ball-tracker eval: held-out clips stay human-only and the loop never enters them. Whether it works is unmeasured; it is gated on a calibration run over the 26 human-marked clips.

Do not bother: importing external single-frame ball sets at volume, more Man City or Aston Villa seg080-style frames, player boxes, identity labels for the ball pipeline.

docs.title: 4. How labels are created today
docs.text:
Who this is for: anyone deciding where to spend labelling time, or tracing why a label did not reach a model. There are nine routes today, plus a tenth that is only proposed (J). Only two of them (A and E) have fed a model that anyone has measured.
