Piece Where State Top-1 + up to 5 candidates per frame, offline tid tracklet ids per window ball_eval/job_suggest.py::suggest_job, ball_eval/panel_suggest.py, ball_eval/tracklets.py::add_tracklets BUILT, but require_heldout_job makes it heldout-only Roll-forward ranking from human anchors: score = log(conf) - d^2/(2 sigma^2) (+ tid bonus), constant-velocity prediction from the last two human boxes, sigma = SIGMA0 + K*abs(frame - last) ball_eval/suggest_rank.py::rank_candidates (mirrored in labeller/web/index.html), served by labeller/suggestions.py::candidates_for_job (also returns existing human boxes as anchors) BUILT, runs in the browser for ball_place jobs Whole-clip best-path tracker with emission from Ball Check precision bands, transition cost by distance and gap, max_gap ball_trackers/viterbi.py::ViterbiBallTracker BUILT, no anchor / forbidden constraints in the code: the "verdict = anchor, wrong = forbidden" re-track exists only as the KB simulation. Constrained version is NEW Detector + bidirectional tracker candidates, gap plausibility ball_mining/track.py::run_tracker, gap_plausibility; pool schema ball_mining/schema.py BUILT Round: plan, tick rule, idempotent create, hooks ball_mining/round.py (plan_round, create_round, tick_decision, next_key, ROUND_HOOKS) BUILT Refit every 50 verdicts, reorder_unanswered with if_rev, Platt on R/A cards only, LTT on A cards ball_mining/refit.py::refit_round, ball_mining/threshold.py BUILT Append cards to a live job, dedupe on unit, if_rev labeller/job_edit.py::append_items, jobs_client.append, hooks.HookContext.append BUILT Re-track seeds from a rejected series window labeller/series_review.py (reproposals.json, _anchors) BUILT (anchors recorded, nothing consumes them yet) Per-group frame state with method precedence feature_store/schema.py::FrameLabelStateRow, store.py::upsert_frame_label_states BUILT Ball Check verdicts ball / not_ball / box_off / corrected / unsure labeller/ball_check.py::VERDICTS BUILT

So the missing part is small: a server-side, verdict-driven candidate generator (anchors in, next cards out) that reuses rank_candidates scoring and the Viterbi tracker, plus the bookkeeping in sections 3 and 7.

docs.title: 1.2 The loop
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    S[Select frames: train-split windows<br/>selected-frame set F] --> C0[Seed cards: top-1 offline suggestion<br/>per window, bucket R/U/M/N/A/G round]
    C0 --> BC[Ball Check: human verdict]
    BC -->|ball / corrected| A[Anchor: frame, centre, hop 0]
    BC -->|not_ball / box_off| X[Forbidden position on that frame]
    BC -->|unsure| D[Deferred, re-queued]
    A --> G[Candidate generation job<br/>one run per window]
    X --> G
    G --> |forward and backward<br/>Viterbi with anchors + forbidden,<br/>gated by motion prior| N[Next cards: best candidate for<br/>neighbouring unjudged frames in F]
    N --> BC
    G -->|no candidate in gate| H[Hand-label fallback<br/>ball_place job mode, no suggestion]
    H --> T
    BC -->|no-ball / not-broadcast| T[Terminal state written]
    A --> T
    T --> Q{All frames of window in F terminal?}
    Q -->|yes| DONE[Window done: export, series, teacher data]
    Q -->|no, nothing generated| H

One iteration (the unit of work, per window w):

  1. verdict(card) is written by the labeller (ball_check._append_verdict) and hooks.emit counts it.
  2. State after the verdict: ball/corrected gives an anchor (centre of the human or confirmed box, hop = 0); not_ball/box_off adds a forbidden disc on that frame; unsure is neither.
  3. The generator (NEW, section 2) loads the window's anchors and forbidden set, runs the constrained Viterbi both ways, and writes per-frame best candidates with a score and the track margin.
  4. It picks the next cards (section 2.2), appends them to the live job (append_items, deduped), and reorders the unanswered ones (reorder_unanswered with if_rev).
  5. The labeller answers them; return to 1. A human-confirmed frame is always an anchor (weight of a human label); hop on a card is the search distance in sampled steps from its nearest anchor, kept so ranking, decay and audits can see how far the search has walked (section 5).

docs.title: 2.1 Generator (NEW: ball_mining/anchor_search.py)
docs.text:
Inputs per window (a window = a run of sampled frames inside one _segNNN clip, as full_frame_labelling.md §4 stage 1; segments are not chainable, so a search never crosses a clip): - candidates per frame: the pool / run_tracker output or the job_suggest boxes[...]["cands"] (top-1 + up to 5, conf >= 0.1, tid); - anchors: human-confirmed centres from the dataset's marks (same reader as suggestions.candidates_for_job's human map, job_suggest.job_human); - forbidden: not_ball / box_off boxes of the window (radius = box size, grown by a margin); - the version of the candidate generator (detector sha8 + tracker params + scorer version).

Algorithm: ViterbiBallTracker extended with two hard constraints (NEW, small): at an anchor frame the only allowed candidate is the one nearest the anchor (or a synthetic node at the human centre when the detector had none, which is what makes missed balls reachable), and any candidate inside a forbidden disc is removed. Run on the whole window, which yields forward and backward propagation in one pass, instead of two causal passes. Per frame output: best node, its posterior margin vs the second-best path (the existing simulation's "smallest Viterbi margin" signal), and hop = frames to the nearest anchor.

Motion gate (so a far-away FP cannot be proposed): a node is eligible only if it is within allowed = base_px + speed_px * gap of the predicted position from the nearest anchor on each side (the same gate ViterbiBallTracker already applies as transition cost, and tracklets.SPEED_PX = 65 px per video frame at 1080p). Frames with no eligible node get no card; they are handled by the fallback in section 3.4.

docs.title: 2.2 Which cards are emitted, and in what order
docs.text:
Per refresh, over the unjudged frames of the window in F: 1. Frontier first. Frames adjacent (in the sampled grid) to an anchor: the smallest hop wins, because the prediction is sharpest there. 2. Within equal hop: lowest Viterbi margin first (most informative; the simulation's order), then highest conf. 3. Track agreement. A candidate on the same tid as the anchor's candidate gets a bonus (already in rank_candidates, TID_BONUS); candidates where forward and backward passes disagree are demoted to the audit pool rather than dropped. 4. Step distance. Do not emit every frame: emit every k-th (default 2) sampled frame in a run and let k = 1 only for low-margin frames. The human confirming frame t and t+2 pins t+1 by interpolation inside the gate, which is then offered as one bulk "accept the run" card (Series-review style, series_review.py) rather than N single cards. NEW, optional. 5. De-dup against judged frames. Skip any (clip, frame) with a live verdict (ball_mining/clips.py::read_verdict_frames, tombstones honoured), any frame in a live round job (round.pending_frames), and any frame whose ball frame_label_state is already complete/absent. append_items dedupes by unit again as the last line.

Card content: the existing ball_check card (crop, box, context clip) plus hidden sampling/search metadata (section 6).

docs.title: 2.3 Integration with the round (ball_mining/round.py)
docs.text: A round today is one ball_check job ball-round/<date>/<n> with quota buckets and the two ROUND_HOOKS. Anchor iteration does not make a second job type; it adds a third hook and a new bucket: - New bucket S (search): cards generated from anchors. It is appended to the same round job (append_items), not a new job per iteration, so the board shows one job with growing "done N / M" and the phone page stays in the same session. - Seed cards (R/U/M/N/A/G as in ball_sampling.md §3.2) are unchanged. A, G and R cards stay interleaved and never move (refit.priority_order only re-deals U and M); S cards are re-dealt by frontier order in the slots they occupy. - Adaptive trigger (primary). New hook anchor-search in ROUND_HOOKS: {"trigger": {"every_n": 10, "min_interval_s": 60}} (prefect action floor is hooks.MIN_PREFECT_INTERVAL_S; check the value, the refit hook already uses 60), deployment ball-anchor-search/ball-anchor-search (JOBS-REPO). Every 10 verdicts, not 50, because search is cheap CPU and latency is what the labeller feels; refit stays at 50. - Nightly sweep (secondary). The same flow, run with {job_id: null, mode: "sweep"}, regenerates every open window, which catches windows whose hook never fired (labeller down, dropped events: hooks.EVENT_QUEUE_MAX drops are counted but not replayed) and picks up a new generator version. - Generation is CPU-only at stride-5 sampled frames when candidates are already cached; only a candidate-cache miss (new window, new detector) needs the GPU (section 7.3).

docs.title: 3.1 Per-frame states (selected frames F)
docs.text:
F = the frames chosen into a job or window (job items, job_suggest.job_frames). Every frame in F is in exactly one state; none may sit in pending forever.

State Meaning Terminal Written as ball human confirmed or drew the ball box (verdict ball/corrected, or ball_place box) yes frame_label_state(ball, complete, method=verdict/hand_frame) BUILT writers no_ball human full-frame check: no ball visible (never inferred from "no candidate") yes (ball, absent, ...) BUILT unusable not broadcast / too few points / frame type mark yes NEW mapping: frame_type mark -> ball absent with reason not_broadcast? Needs a reason column (section 6) deferred explicit, with a reason (unsure twice, video unreadable, window rejected) yes, but counted separately and never exported NEW: partial state + deferred_reason queued a card exists, unanswered no job item unreachable search produced no eligible candidate no, routed to fallback NEW unreviewed in F, no card yet no absence of row

unsure stays non-terminal on its first answer (as in full_frame_labelling.md §1): the card is re-queued once at the end of the job; a second unsure becomes deferred(reason=unsure_x2).

docs.title: 3.2 Window and job completion rule
docs.text: A window is done when every frame in F(window) is terminal (ball, no_ball, unusable, deferred). A job is done when all its windows are. Not done by silence: a job cannot be marked done while unreviewed, queued or unreachable frames remain; the reconciler (section 7.7) lists them. deferred frames count toward "terminal" but the progress bar shows them as their own segment so they cannot pass as labelled.

docs.title: 3.3 Progress
docs.text:
• Job bar: the existing done N / M (round._cards reads progress.done/total). With appended cards M grows; to avoid a moving target, the job also reports frames_total = |F| and frames_terminal, and the page bar uses frames, not cards (NEW fields on the job progress).
  • /progress/labelling (labeller/progress.py): the ball-complete target gets a breakdown of ball / no_ball / unusable / deferred / outstanding per dataset and per window (NEW; the two-target rewrite in the two-detector decision is already a TODO there).

docs.title: 3.4 Unreachable frames fall back to hand labelling
docs.text: After a refresh, frames in F that are unreviewed and have no eligible candidate, or that stayed queued unanswered past a stale age, are moved by the generator into a companion ball_place job in labeller job mode (ball-place/<window>; the generator writes it with jobs_client.submit, idempotent key). A frame the search cannot reach is never defaulted to no_ball: it goes to this explicit full-frame human check (laptop job mode, or a full-frame card on the phone). When the human places a box it becomes an anchor and the search re-runs for the window; a human no_ball is the only way a no-candidate frame ends as no_ball. This guarantees the loop terminates: every frame is reached by a card or by a full-frame check, and recall is not inflated by silently dropping frames the model missed (section 4.1).

docs.title: 4. Eval and train sharing the flow: what stays separate (revised 2026-11-21)
docs.text:
Eval frames exist to measure the detector and find its false negatives. Both families now use the same card mechanics (offline suggestion on a Ball Check card, anchor search, full-frame fallback), so one phone flow covers both. Because every selected frame must be completed anyway, showing a suggestion does not change which frames are measured; anchoring bias is accepted and not mitigated here (no machine-box hiding, no blind audit slice). The measure stays valid only if the following hold.

  1. Selected set fixed first, with logged inclusion probabilities. Each job's F is chosen up front (eval: panel windows with pi_window/pi_frame, BUILT in ball_eval/panel.py; train: the round's bucket sampler and its sampling block) and written to selected_frame before any candidate is generated. Candidates never decide which frames are measured; they only order and pre-fill cards.
  2. Every selected frame reaches an explicit terminal state (section 3.1). No candidate is not no_ball.
  3. False-negative rule. A frame where the search finds no confirmed candidate (zero candidates, all rejected, unsure, not found) goes to an explicit human full-frame check: laptop labeller job mode, or a full-frame card on the phone ("tap the ball, or no ball"). Only that check can write no_ball. This is the false-negative hunt (4.1).
  4. Split separation. split_of(match, clip) (footy_track/splits.py) puts every frame in exactly one set. The generator runs per split and per job: anchors and candidates come only from that job's own selected set, so anchors propagate only inside the same F (guard + test, NEW). Eval and train F are disjoint; eval labels never enter a training export (the exporter's split_of gate stays: heldout and eval_in_match frames are excluded); an appended item whose split differs from the job's is rejected (extend the job API's mixed-split check to append_items).
  5. Versions on everything. Every card and label records generator_version (candidate model sha8 + tracker params), teacher_version, run_id. Eval scores (panel_score.score) are reported per version, and an eval label is read together with the version of the model whose box the labeller saw.
  6. Two job families stay separate (7.0): own keys, caps and done counters, though the card mechanics are shared.

Existing code that fits: ball_sampling.md §2.2.1 already shows suggestions on 75% of panel windows with a 25% blind control; accepted suggestions are ordinary tier-1 labels tagged accepted_suggestion + suggest_det:<sha8>; panel_score.suggestion_report compares blind vs shown. The blind control is no longer required by this design; it may stay as an optional diagnostic and nothing here depends on it. job_suggest.require_heldout_job limits job-keyed suggestion files to heldout jobs; the train family needs the same builder with a per-job split guard instead (task 1).

docs.title: 4.1 The false-negative hunt
docs.text: False negatives = ball present, no correct prediction (miss; off for a wrong top-1). They are visible only if frames with no confirmed candidate are looked at in full, which is rule 3. - Stratum model_no_ball (eval and train): windows where the frozen reference model gave zero candidates or top-1 conf below a floor, with logged pi and HT weighting (ball_sampling.md §2.3 difficulty bands) so it never inflates the headline unweighted. - Measurement (ball_eval/panel_score.py::score, BUILT): hit/off/miss/false_ball/true_empty per frame, HT totals, bootstrap CIs. NEW columns: miss per bucket (easy/gappy/contested/low_evidence, ball_mining/buckets.py); whether a candidate within r px existed (detector recall ceiling vs ranking error); and the share of terminal frames found by a card vs by a full-frame check (the latter are the candidate source's false negatives). - Feedback: eval results feed back only as measurement and as new targeted TRAIN strata (train windows resembling the failing buckets). Eval labels are never copied into training.

docs.title: 5. Risk
docs.text:
Anchoring bias (a shown box pulling the label) is accepted by decision (2026-11-21); no mitigation is built for it.

Risk Mitigation Wrong anchor propagates A human-confirmed anchor is treated as ground truth but cards carry hop; cap hop at 3 steps beyond the last confirmation (a card further than that is not auto-extended, it needs a fresh seed); confidence on the card = p_cal * decay^hop; a later not_ball/box_off on a card adjacent to an anchor flags the anchor suspect and re-runs the window with that anchor released; a not_ball is always a forbidden zone (ball_ck rejects stay forbidden for all later refreshes, kept per window) Auto-propagation (bulk "accept the run" for interpolated frames) Never auto-accepted: it is a card a human answers Wilson/LTT thresholds (ball_mining/threshold.py) LTT requires exchangeable A-bucket audits: verdicts on S cards are chosen by the anchor and are not exchangeable, so threshold.audit_rows must keep excluding them (ExchangeabilityError on a non-"A" tag). The auto-accept set is still computed from A cards; S-card verdicts feed training labels and the report only. S frames' p_real for Platt uses only R/A cards, as refit.fit_calibration already does Teacher drift Every card and label records generator_version, teacher_version (offline_vN) and run_id; eval scores are reported per version; a card whose generator version is older than the current one is stale (section 7.5), still answerable, and its verdict still counts Selection of "easy" frames Search favours frames near confirmed balls, which are easy. Training export composition check per bucket and hop; hard strata still come from U/M/N, and hop >= 2 labels are loss-weighted 0.5 until an audit shows their precision Eval leakage Section 4 rules 4 and 5

docs.title: 6. Data model / API changes (all NEW)
docs.text:
Card (hidden sampling/search block, persisted with each verdict like the existing sampling): anchor_id (job id + clip + frame of the nearest anchor), hop, direction (fwd|bwd|both), source (seed|search|fallback), generator_version, teacher_version, run_id, search_round (monotonic per window), margin, p_cal, stale (derived).

Job kinds: no new kind for cards (ball_check round job + appended S cards); the fallback is a ball_place job ball-place/<window>. Job progress gains frames_total, frames_terminal, by_state.

Per-frame state: frame_label_state (BUILT) covers ball complete/absent/partial/unreviewed. Add nullable reason (not_broadcast, unsure_x2, window_rejected, video_unreadable) and generator_version; method precedence unchanged (hand_series/hand_frame > verdict > offline_audited). A new small table (or store file) selected_frame(job_key, game_id, frame_index, window_id, split, selected_at) is the expected set F that the reconciler diffs against (section 7.7).

API: reuse POST /api/jobs/<id>/append and /reorder (if_rev) BUILT; add GET /api/jobs/<id>/frames (state per frame of F) and accept search meta on appended items.

docs.title: 7. Orchestration and sync between jobs, schedules and the store
docs.text: Three systems own parts of the state, so each fact gets exactly one owner.

docs.title: 7.0 Two job families that both stay (assumption: "both jobs" = these two)
docs.text:
Neither replaces the other; they advance side by side, share card mechanics, and never exchange labels. (Revised 2026-11-21: both now use suggestion + anchor cards on the phone.)

Eval job family Train job family Phone ball_check cards from the offline suggestion + anchor search, key namespace ball-eval/<panel>/<match> (NEW card job; the panel's frozen windows and pi are BUILT in ball_eval/panel.py) ball_check round ball-round/<date>/<n> (BUILT) Laptop full-frame hand-label checks for frames with no confirmed candidate: ball_place job mode ball-eval-place/<panel>/<match> (NEW, idempotent) the same for train: ball-place/<window> (NEW) Selected set F panel windows of heldout matches (split_of = eval_heldout_match; in-match eval clips eval_in_match as a secondary panel), fixed at creation with pi train-split windows (split_of = train), fixed per round Purpose score the detector, find false negatives training and teacher data Done every frame of F terminal (ball, no_ball only via full-frame check, unusable, deferred(reason)); QA repeat/gold cards excluded from estimates section 3.2 Progress counter /progress/labelling ball-eval block: frames_terminal / frames_total per panel and match, found-by-card vs found-by-check, panel-score CIs per version ball-train block, per window

Rules that keep them from starving or contaminating each other: 1. Disjoint by construction. F_eval and F_train are disjoint because split_of is a function of (match, clip) and assignments are sticky; the creator records each frame's split in selected_frame; the reconciler fails hard if a (game, frame) is in both sets or in a job of the wrong family. 2. Separate caps and namespaces. tick_decision counts only ball-round/* jobs (refit.is_round_job filters on the key prefix), so eval cards never consume the train cap (open < 100, today < 600) and S cards never count against eval. Eval has its own cap and no daily tick: its F is fixed at creation (the panel version), and the anchor flow appends to it only within F, bounded by its own open-card cap so the phone is not flooded. 3. Both advance on the phone and laptop. The board shows both families as separate lines with their own counters. A nightly report lists per family frames_outstanding and days idle, and an eval family with outstanding frames raises a board task so training rounds cannot absorb all human time. Time split is a policy (open question 9). 4. Nothing generated crosses over. The generator runs per job and reads only that job's F (section 4 rule 4). Search files are per job (<marks>/ball_mining/search/<job>/<window>/), so train anchors can never seed an eval frame and the reverse. 5. Eval feeds back only as measurement and targeting. Allowed: the per-version panel score (per-bucket miss, model_no_ball, section 4.1) and new targeted TRAIN strata derived from it. Not allowed: copying an eval label or box into training, or using an eval frame as a train anchor. 6. The reconciler checks each set independently (7.7 loops over families): own F, own job, own store rows, separate reports and alerts.

docs.title: 7.1 Single source of truth, and who may write
docs.text:
Fact Owner (only writer) Others A verdict / human box the labeller (ball_check._append_verdict JSONL under the dataset marks dir; ball_place sidecars) read-only: generator, refit, store ingest Which cards exist, their order, rev the labeller job file (job_edit.append_items / reorder_unanswered; the only mutators) flows go through the API, never the files Terminal frame state the feature store frame_label_state, written by ingest from verdicts / sidecars (ingest_gt, feature_store/ball_checks replacement) the labeller never writes the store directly; progress reads it Anchors / forbidden / generated candidates the generator output <marks>/ball_mining/search/<window>/vNNN.json (immutable, versioned like refit.write_state) derived: always recomputable from verdicts + candidates Expected set F the creator of the job (round planner / window selector), recorded once in selected_frame reconciler reads

Nothing is derived in two places: anchors are not stored as a separate truth; they are verdict in (ball, corrected) rows read at generation time. The search file is a cache with a version, rebuilt on demand.

docs.title: 7.2 Event chain
docs.text:
verdict (labeller, durable JSONL) -> hooks.emit (in-memory, may drop) -> hook anchor-search every_n=10 -> prefect_client.create_flow_run("ball-anchor-search/...", {job_id, window?, hook, trigger, dataset}) -> flow reads results (jobs_client.results) + marks -> writes search/<window>/vNNN.json -> jobs_client.append(items, if_rev=rev) then jobs_client.reorder(order, if_rev=rev) -> labeller serves new cards. In parallel the nightly flow ingests verdicts to the store (frame_label_state) and bumps dataset versions.

Because emit can drop events and a labeller restart loses the in-memory counters, the hook is a latency optimisation, not a correctness path: correctness comes from the sweep and the reconciler, both of which derive everything from durable verdicts.

docs.title: 7.3 Idempotency and dedupe
docs.text:
• Round and fallback jobs: idempotent key (round.next_key -> ball-round/<date>/<n>; the jobs layer returns the existing job with created=False on the same key, jobs.py _sha_id(key)). Fallback jobs use ball-place/<window_id>; a window has at most one live fallback job.
  • Appended cards: a deterministic search_round and a per-card unit key (clip, frame_index); append_items already skips units present in the job (_dedupe_key), so a retried append adds 0 and reports skipped_duplicates.
  • Generation runs: skip key = sha1(window_id + sorted anchors + sorted forbidden + generator_version). If the latest search/<window>/vNNN.json carries the same digest, the run is a no-op (the way refit reuses the latest state for the same data). Overlapping nightly and hook runs therefore converge on one result.
  • No verdict is ever lost by regeneration: verdicts are keyed by (clip, frame, box) in the labeller marks and never rewritten by flows. A card answered after it was reordered or went stale still writes its verdict (the API never moves answered cards; staleness is metadata).

docs.title: 7.4 Concurrency and locking
docs.text:
• One generation run per window: Prefect concurrency tag anchor-search:<window_id> with limit 1 (JOBS-REPO). A second trigger for the same window queues or is dropped by the skip key. Hook bounds already give one in-flight run per (job, hook) and MAX_PREFECT_INFLIGHT across jobs.
  • if_rev conflicts: the flow reads rev with the unanswered positions, appends with if_rev, then reads the new rev and reorders with it. On 409 it re-reads and retries up to REORDER_TRIES (BUILT in refit._apply_order); the generator reuses that helper. Append before reorder, never in parallel with a refit run: the refit and search hooks share a per-job mutex (Prefect concurrency tag ball-job:<job_id>, limit 1) so two flows never fight over rev. NEW.
  • GPU: the gpu pool has concurrency 1. Only a candidate-cache miss (new window or new detector) needs the GPU; it goes through the existing stage-inputs -> GPU -> push-outputs chain as a separate low-priority flow (ball-candidates), never inside the hook flow. The hook flow is CPU-only and returns "no candidates yet, retry" when the cache is missing; it never blocks the GPU slot or waits on it. Candidate generation is demand-driven by the window's selection, once per (window, detector_sha).

docs.title: 7.5 Ordering and staleness
docs.text:
• A search file records generator_version and rev_seen (the job rev and the verdict count it was built from). Cards appended from an older generator version than latest are stale: they stay in the job, still count when answered, but are re-ranked behind fresh frontier cards at the next refresh, and a stale unanswered card is replaced by a new one only if its frame's best candidate changed by more than a gate (otherwise leave it, to avoid churn under the labeller's hands).
  • Version bumps (new detector, new tracker params, new scorer) never rewrite history: new vNNN.json, old cards keep their recorded versions. Training export reports composition by version.
  • Out-of-order events (verdict 53 processed before 51): irrelevant, because each run reads the whole verdict set, not the event.

docs.title: 7.6 Failure and recovery
docs.text: Failure Behaviour Flow crashes mid-iteration (after write of search file, before append) next run has the same digest: sees the file, skips regeneration, repeats the append (idempotent) Crash between append and reorder cards are present, order is the old one: harmless; next refresh reorders Labeller restarts / redeploys verdicts are durable; hook counters reset, so the nightly sweep and the reconciler cover the gap; flows retry API calls with backoff and fail closed (as refit: "any other API error propagates") Labeller / laptop offline flows cannot append: they write the search file and mark pending_push; next tick pushes. The laptop labelling site runs the same API; the board shows the latest rev Partial batch (some cards appended, API error) append_items is one transaction under the job file lock; a retry sees 0 or N, never half (verify in the task below) Deploy of the labeller mid-round follow the existing rule: deploy only from /home/george/footy-track-main when idle ~5 min; Prefect deployments are never redeployed mid-run (SignatureMismatchError gotcha in prefect-job-system)

docs.title: 7.7 Schedules, backpressure, reconciliation
docs.text:
• Existing tick (BUILT: round.tick_decision): create a round only when open training cards < 100 and cards created today < 600; 15-minute autolabel-queue-tick; weekly flow. The anchor search obeys the same caps: S cards count as open training cards, so the search never appends beyond open_cards_max (it appends the best frontier cards up to the headroom) and counts toward daily_cards_max. Backpressure therefore shapes iteration speed automatically, and a human working fast gets more cards because the open count drops.
  • Adaptive vs nightly: adaptive (every_n=10 hook) for latency while someone is labelling; nightly sweep (new ball-anchor-sweep, runs after footy-nightly-datasets ingest at 03:30 Europe/London so it sees fresh store state) for windows with no recent activity, generator-version rollovers and missed events. Different run keys (hook vs sweep) but the same skip digest.
  • Reconciler (NEW: ball_mining/reconcile.py, nightly flow ball-reconcile, report-only; read-only by default, --apply only re-queues): diffs three sets per window: expected selected_frame F, job items/cards (labeller API + marks), and frame_label_state (store). Reports: orphans (card with no F entry, verdict with no job), missing (F frame with no card, no terminal state and no fallback job), stuck (queued longer than N days, unreachable with no fallback), split violations (any F or anchor on a non-train clip, a hard fail), store lag (verdict present, no frame_label_state row), and version skew. Output is a JSON report on /progress/labelling plus a nonzero exit that raises a Prefect notification. This is what enforces "every selected frame reaches a terminal state".

docs.title: 7.8 What must change in the jobs repo (not edited here)
docs.text:
1. New deployment ball-anchor-search/ball-anchor-search (cpu pool, mini): runs python -m footy_track.ball_mining.anchor_search --job <ref> [--window W], params {job_id, window?, hook, trigger, dataset, labeller_url?} (same signature as ball-refit; redeploy only when no parent flow is running).
  2. New deployment ball-candidates (gpu pool, desktop, concurrency 1, via stage-inputs/push-outputs), key (window, detector_sha).
  3. Concurrency tags anchor-search:<window> and ball-job:<job_id> (limit 1); make ball-refit and ball-round-close take ball-job:<job_id> too.
  4. ball-anchor-sweep after the nightly ingest in footy-nightly-datasets, and ball-reconcile nightly.
  5. autolabel-queue-tick (15 min): after the round tick, also top up open S cards through the sweep flow when below open_cards_max, inside the same daily cap. Keep auto_conf at 0.95 (ball_sampling.md §3.3).
  6. Extend ROUND_HOOKS in this repo (round.py) with the third hook; set FOOTY_HOOKS_PREFECT_ALLOW to include the new deployments.

Status (task 5, BUILT in this repo): ROUND_HOOKS has the third hook anchor-search (every_n 10, min_interval_s 60, prefect ball-anchor-search/ball-anchor-search, params {}; the labeller adds {job_id, hook, trigger, dataset, labeller_url?}). The CLI is python -m footy_track.scripts.ball_anchor_search run --job <ref> | sweep (docstring there = the exact contract of the JOBS-REPO flow: mode == "sweep" or job_id is None runs sweep, else run --job <job_id>; both take --labeller-url). Both take the per-job mutex refit.job_lock (flock on <marks>/ball_mining/locks/<job>.lock) that refit and close also take, so the Prefect tag ball-job:<job_id> has a local twin; a busy job is skipped (exit 0). Bucket S verdicts are removed before the Platt fit and Learn-then-Test (refit.exclude_search) and only reported as their own hit_rates bucket. Items 1-5 of the list above remain JOBS-REPO work.

Status (task 10, BUILT in this repo; decisions of George 2026-11-22): the eval family runs on the shared flow as ball_check job ball-eval/<panel>/<match> (ball_eval/eval_flow.py: F and splits to selected_frame first, build_job_body refuses without them; one seed card per panel window, bucket E, pi on the card; appended search cards stay bucket S; no-candidate windows, rejected-out frames, unreachable / beyond-cap frames go to ball-eval-place/<panel>/<match>, never no_ball). scripts/ball_anchor_search runs the eval iteration (seeds + search + fallback, the eval family's own open cap) for ball-eval/* jobs, also in the sweep. (1) Candidate source (ball_eval/eval_source.py): the offline teacher while its recall within 20 px of human gold (any candidate) is >= the best student's (ties -> teacher), else the best student; the scored model is never used silently (ties prefer another source; if it is chosen anyway the record says selected_is_scored_model); candidate_source (kind, id, version, teacher_version / model_version, gold recall, rule) is on every card (sampling and search), search document and suggest file, and all scores per version are in the selection record. (2) Fixed eval share (ball_mining/share.py): EVAL_SHARE = 0.30, merge() interleaves the families' cards so every prefix of k cards holds floor(0.3 k) eval cards until the eval list is empty; each side is cut to its own room first (caps untouched) and a card of the wrong split raises. It is the ordering rule plus a CLI; nothing in the labeller page calls it yet (the page serves one job at a time). (3) False-negative report (ball_eval/fn_report.py, ball-eval-fn-report/v1): from the terminal states of F, per scored version the ball frames with no detection within 20 px (no_detection vs off), plus ball / no_ball / unusable / deferred / outstanding counts, complete only when nothing is outstanding. Also fixed: resolve_selected now finds selected_frame rows by job KEY (progress and reconciler write them by key), and run_search loads candidates / anchors for all of F, not just the cards already in the job (job_with_selected).

docs.title: 8. Task list (dependency order)
docs.text:
Legend as in full_frame_labelling.md §5. All NEW.

  1. Per-job split guard + candidate cache reader. Files: ball_mining/anchor_search.py (guard, loaders), ball_eval/job_suggest.py (drop heldout-only restriction for a per-job split check), labeller/job_edit.py (reject appended items of another split), tests. Accept: a job only ever reads/writes frames of its own selected set and one split; anchors never cross jobs; reads job_suggest cands or pool candidates uniformly; anchors read from marks. Deps: none.
  2. Constrained Viterbi. Files: ball_trackers/viterbi.py (anchor/forbidden args, synthetic anchor node), tests with a fixture clip. Accept: anchor frame returns the anchor; forbidden disc never chosen; unconstrained output unchanged (regression); both directions in one pass. Deps: 1.
  3. Generator + ranking + versioned search file. Files: anchor_search.py, search/<window>/vNNN.json. Accept: frontier order = hop, margin, conf; skips judged frames (verdicts, pending round cards, terminal frame_label_state); same input digest -> no new file; no candidate in gate -> frame listed unreachable. Deps: 2.
  4. Append/reorder client with caps. Files: anchor_search.py using refit._apply_order's retry. Accept: respects open-card and daily caps from round.tick_decision; retried append adds 0; 409 retries; append is atomic (kill test). Deps: 3.
  5. Hook + CLI + round integration. Files: ball_mining/round.py (ROUND_HOOKS third hook, bucket S tag), scripts/ball_anchor_search.py, refit.py (S cards excluded from Platt/LTT). Accept: S verdicts never reach learn_then_test; hook fires every 10; refit unaffected. Deps: 4.
  6. Per-frame state and reasons. Files: feature_store/schema.py (reason, generator_version, selected_frame), store.py, ingest_gt.py, tests. Accept: no_ball, unusable, deferred map as in section 3.1; re-ingest idempotent. Deps: none (parallel to 1-5).
  7. Fallback hand-label job. Files: anchor_search.py, jobs_client use. Accept: unreachable frames produce one idempotent ball_place job with no suggestion; a placed box re-runs the search. Deps: 3, 6.
  8. Progress. Files: labeller/progress.py, jobs.py progress fields, page bars. Accept: frames_total/terminal/by_state equal a fixture store; deferred shown separately. Deps: 6.
  9. Reconciler. Files: ball_mining/reconcile.py, scripts/. Accept: fixtures detect orphan, missing, stuck, store lag, split violation; read-only by default. Deps: 6.
  10. Eval on the shared flow + false-negative report. Files: ball_eval/panel.py (eval ball_check job from the frozen panel, selected_frame written before candidates, model_no_ball band), panel_score.py (miss by bucket, found-by-card vs by-check, per-version scores). Accept: F and pi logged before candidate generation; a no-candidate frame becomes a full-frame check, never no_ball; scores carry the generator version; report has miss by bucket with CIs. Deps: 1, 6, 7.
  11. Wrong-anchor controls. Files: anchor_search.py, refit.py. Accept: S-gold cards injected at 5%; hop cap enforced; suspect anchor flow. Deps: 5. BUILT (2026-11-22) in ball_mining/anchor_controls.py + hooks in anchor_search.push_search/run_search, refit, reconcile, scripts/ball_anchor_search.py: S-gold controls at CONTROL_RATE = 0.05 (cumulative, deterministic, same split, never from F, hidden sampling.gold / search.control), per-window / per-job agreement (refit state search_controls, reconcile controls), suspect anchors (control disagreement or a hop-1 not_ball/box_off) recorded in <marks>/suspects/<job>.jsonl, released by run_search(suspects=...) into a new vNNN search file with a changed digest, impact (open / answered / previous-search cards) in the run output. Hop cap stays 3, decay 0.8, no bulk-accept card (George, 2026-11-22). Controls are bucket S, so they stay out of Platt / LTT.
  12. Jobs-repo changes (section 7.8). In ~/code/jobs. Accept: concurrency limits verified with two overlapping triggers; a dry run produces the same state twice. Deps: 5, 9.
  13. Replay evaluation on already-labelled train clips (before any rollout). Accept: with a perfect oracle on 5 held-out-by-us train clips, taps-to-90% beats the 13 of the KB simulation or the design is revised. Deps: 3.

docs.title: 9. Open questions for George
docs.text:
1. Eval candidate source: should it be a different model or version from the one being scored (so the suggestions are not the scored model's own output), or the same one? Recorded either way (generator_version), but the per-version eval number reads differently.
  2. hop cap and decay: stop at 3 steps beyond the last confirmation? Or let long runs bulk-accept after two confirmations either side?
  3. Card cadence: one card per every second sampled frame plus bulk "accept the run" for interpolated frames, or every sampled frame?
  4. deferred frames: allowed to remain forever (reported, never exported), or must a human resolve them before a window counts as done?
  5. Trigger cadence: hook every 10 verdicts vs 50 (matching refit)? A 60 s Prefect floor sets the lower bound.
  6. Does Claude verify run on search cards (as pre-filter) or are they human-only until their precision is measured?
  7. Window size for search (250 frames = 5 s as in full_frame_labelling.md, or longer)? Segments are not contiguous, so windows cannot span _segNNN.
  8. Should the reconciler be allowed to auto re-queue (--apply), or report only?
  9. "Keep both jobs": I read it as the eval family and the train family run side by side with shared card mechanics (section 7.0). If you meant something else (for example keeping the old per-frame ball_place flow beside Ball Check cards), say so. Also: a fixed share of labelling time for the eval job until its panel is done?

docs.title: 10. Replay results (task 13, 2026-11-21)
docs.text:
Harness: ball_mining/anchor_replay.py + scripts/ball_anchor_replay.py (CPU, read-only, train clips only via splits.split_of_name). It runs the real generate_window after every verdict. Oracle: human ball GT (labeller-tagged sidecars of ball_gt_marks + ball_gt_marks_ball_train_v1, aliases merged by canonical clip id). Candidates: RT-DETR jsonl (ball_candidates, sha b4ea4b22, conf >= 0.1, top 6/frame). A card is ball when its centre is within 20 px of GT, else not_ball (anchor / forbidden disc). A GT frame counts as covered when it has a correct anchor or the current card for it is within 20 px (nothing beyond the hop cap is credited). Re-seed = top-1 detection on an uncovered frame, oracle-judged; no detection left = hand placement (one tap, counted as hand_in_90). The tracker also gets a stride-5 grid of non-GT "bridge" frames (never asked or scored), because max_gap = 12 otherwise cannot link GT frames that are about 25 frames apart. Windows are 250 frames, clip taps = sum over windows.

Real data available. 7 train clips have both dense human GT (>= 20 ball frames) and per-frame detector candidates, all arsenal_mancity_seg{010,030,031,050,060,100,110} (GT 124/26/53/80/20/24/29 frames). 7 more train clips with >= 11 GT frames have NO candidates on disk (arsenal_example, arsenal_mancity_part050, arsenal_astonvilla_seg080, arsenal_bournemouth_1st_seg009/031/035/040): their only candidate source is a sparse ball_pool parquet (a few clips per match, a handful of frames each) and machine_labels / ball_candidates exist only for arsenal_mancity_20250925_* plus a few eval clips. Most ball_gt_marks_ball_train_v1 clips have a single human frame (Ball Check outcomes), useless for a replay. GT frames are sparse (about one per 25 frames), unlike the dense per-frame GT of the KB simulation. Detector recall ceiling: of the 356 GT frames, 34 have no candidate within 20 px (per clip in the table below).

Result: the acceptance criterion is NOT met. Perfect oracle, design as specified (hop cap 3, order hop / margin / conf, judged frames skipped, window 250), real candidates:

clip GT unreachable taps to 90% of which hand taps to 100% of reachable wrong anchors seg010 124 11 129 11 129 0 seg030 26 0 24 0 26 0 seg031 53 18 64 15 55 0 seg050 80 2 75 0 80 0 seg060 20 2 14 0 15 0 seg100 24 0 23 0 25 0 seg110 29 1 27 0 30 0

Mean 50.9, median 27 taps to 90% against the baseline 13 (no clip but seg060 is near it). Confirming every frame once to reach 90% would cost 323 taps over the 7 clips (90% of 356 frames); the design needs 356 (design policy), so it is no better than confirming every frame once. Variants (same data, --help for flags):

variant mean / median taps to 90% spec (design order, hop cap 3) 50.9 / 27 smallest margin first (KB simulation order) 50.3 / 24 requeue (rejected frame stays open for its next candidate) 57.6 / 26 margin order, hop cap 12 35.0 / 24 margin order, hop cap 100 22.6 / 8 margin order, hop cap 100, whole clip as one window 32.3 / 5 spec with a 5% noisy oracle 54.7 / 29 (1 wrong anchor)

Why: (1) the hop cap counts sampled steps, so on a 25-frame GT spacing almost every frame is beyond the cap and needs its own seed card; lifting the cap gives 1-8 taps on four clips (seg050, 060, 100, 110, one continuous ball track) but seg010, seg031 stay at 80+ (hop cap is a wrong-anchor safeguard, so a safe value is the open question); (2) cards are asked in frontier / margin order, including frames whose pick is already right, so correct frames cost a tap without raising coverage, while confident wrong picks (large margin) come last; (3) the detector ceiling (seg031: 18 of 53 GT frames without a candidate) forces hand placements before 90% is reachable; (4) max_gap = 12 means the unmodified tracker cannot link frames more than 12 apart: the stride-5 grid is required.

Verdict: revise the design before rollout. Suggested changes to test next in this harness: spend the first taps on the most-informative frames only and let high-margin runs be bulk-accepted (section 2.2 item 4, never auto-accepted) instead of one card per frame; make the hop cap depend on the margin / track continuity (the replay shows wrong anchors are rare, 0 with a perfect oracle); keep the stride-5 bridge frames as part of the generator input (task 3 follow-up). The 13-tap KB figure came from dense per-frame GT, so this replay is a harder test than that simulation; a like-for-like rerun needs dense GT, which does not exist for these clips. A synthetic run (--synthetic 5, labelled as such, not a measurement) only proves the harness: mean 72 taps (design) / 95 (requeue).

docs.title: Ball sample mining: evaluation panel and training miner
docs.text: Status: proposal, 2026-11-18. It builds on feature_store.md, calibration.md, the autolabel design (§12, on feat/autolabel-retrack) and the labelling-jobs/hooks system (labeller README §19c).

docs.title: 0. Summary
docs.text:
There are two regimes. They use different populations, sampling rules and cards, and a different question to Ball Check.

Evaluation panel Training miner Question "How good is model M on unseen matches, ± what?" "Which frames most improve the next model per human second?" Population Main-camera frames of heldout matches only Main-camera frames of train matches only (in-match eval clips excluded) Selection Fixed probability sample with logged inclusion probabilities π. It does not depend on the model being scored. Adaptive, model-driven quotas (uncertain, missed, hard-negative, random, audit) Card Blind: no model box. "Tap the ball" or "no ball visible". Verify: the proposed box is shown, with ball / not_ball / box_off / corrected / "ball elsewhere" (tap). Labels are Model-independent, so any future model can be scored on them About one model's proposals, used for training and for calibrating auto-accept Output HT-weighted hit@10/25, precision, false-ball rate, with CIs, per match and pooled Tier-1/2 labels, negatives, and audit data for the auto-accept threshold

Rule zero: a heldout match never feeds training. That includes pseudo-labels, even though self-training on a match's own video is our biggest measured win (held-out hit@10 went from 0.49 to 0.70). Using it on heldout footage would be training on the test set.

docs.title: 1. Why (evidence that shaped this)
docs.text:
From our own data: - Today's ball eval is a convenience sample: 101 frames from 4 Forest clips, labelled while reviewing detector output. Recall is optimistic (docs/ball-tracking-eval.md). The only designed sample is the Forest placement job (24 windows, about 10–20% done). - Generalisation across matches is the binding problem. The detector scores 0.92 in-distribution, 0.67 on arsenal_example and 0.49 on held-out clips. Per-match numbers matter more than a pooled one. - 37% of human ball frames have no detector candidate within 25 px. A regime that only verifies proposals can never measure or fix recall, so both regimes need "ball is elsewhere" and "no ball". - Detector confidence is badly calibrated: Ball Check precision is 0.04 at conf 0.1–0.2, 0.42 at 0.5–0.6 and 0.96 at 0.7–0.8. - Claude verify is calibrated very differently by band: 33/33 correct at ≥ 0.95, 28/43 at 0.8–0.95, 8/23 at 0.5–0.8. - The deployed autolabel queue auto-accepts at 0.8 (~/code/jobs/footy_autolabel_queue.py:79). That admits a band measured at 65% precision. The design target was 0.95. - Human throughput is about 100–260 cards per labelling day, at a median of about 2 s per verify card (mean 4.6 s). The pool is about 1.8M broadcast frames in the 12 segmented matches, with 34 more matches coming. Labels are scarce; frames are not.

From the literature (snippet-level reads; the papers are linked in the research notes): - Unbiased eval with a chosen sample: Horvitz–Thompson/LURE (active testing, Kossen 2021) and active statistical inference (Zrnic & Candès 2024; over 80% label savings in their settings). Both stay unbiased if π is logged and bounded away from 0. PPI++ adds a model-prediction control variate to a uniform sample. Small π inflates variance, so mix in a uniform floor. - Active learning for detection: gains over random are small and unstable, and random is a strong baseline (2212.10836, 2403.14800). Diversity and redundancy removal reliably help (+3.4 mAP, 2307.08414). In video, select clips or windows, not single frames. Use temporal-coherence errors (flicker, detector/tracker disagreement) as the acquisition signal. At low budgets, typical/diverse beats uncertain (TypiClust). - Verification: verifying a box is about 3× cheaper than drawing one (Open Images: 9 s vs 25.5 s). Humans over-accept proposals, and more so when rejecting requires entering a correction. - Pseudo-labels: a single fixed confidence threshold skews the set toward easy, frequent cases. Use adaptive thresholds, and route hard cases to humans. - Auto-accept: Learn-then-Test turns verified outcomes into a threshold with P(precision ≥ target) ≥ 1−δ. It needs calibration data that is exchangeable with what gets auto-accepted, which means random audits within the band, not the human-review queue.

docs.title: 2.1 Population and unit
docs.text:
• Population U: every frame at stride 5 (10 fps at 50 fps), inside main-camera segments (segments.json) of heldout matches. That is 9 of 51 today, selected by sha1 % 4, and the rule is sticky.
  • The population is fixed by the segmentation run, not by the current broadcast classifier's p_yes, so it does not move when the classifier is retrained. Frames that are not main-camera are out of scope for the ball metric.
  • Sampling unit: a window of 5 frames, 0.2 s apart (about 1 s). Neighbouring frames make placement faster and give a little tracking signal. The cost is intra-window correlation, which the cluster bootstrap in §2.4 accounts for.

docs.title: 2.2 Card: blind placement (Ball Check "blind mode" = the ball_place job kind)
docs.text:
• No model box is shown. The labeller taps the ball centre, or marks no ball visible or unsure. The 3 s context clip stays.
  • Rationale: blind labels are independent of the model, so the panel is reusable for every future model and tracker. They also have no automation bias and give exact pixel error, which hit@10 px needs and accept/reject cannot provide.
  • Cost: we have not measured it. Assume about 4–6 s per frame against about 2 s to verify. That is an acceptable price for a set built once and reused.
  • QA layer, about 8% of cards:
  • 5% repeats of earlier panel frames, in a different session. The spread between repeats gives the label-noise floor; if it is about 5 px, hit@10 is meaningful.
  • 3% gold frames from existing tier-1 GT.
  • Both are excluded from the estimates.

docs.title: 2.2.1 Update 2026-11-19: detector suggestions with a random blind control (LAB-1445..1447)
docs.text:
• Why. Placing a ball from scratch is slow (the 4-6 s per frame assumed above, 5 panels about 630 cards), and George asked to be able to accept a detector box straight away or draw over it. Speed is the reason; the cost is that a shown box can pull the label towards the detector (automation bias), and the suggesting detector then looks better than it is.
  • What. ball_eval_panel suggest (the model sits behind a small Suggester interface, so the pooled RT-DETR + motion + tracker top node can replace RT-DETR top-1) precomputes, per panel frame, the top-1 RT-DETR ball candidate (production weights, 1280 px, CPU about 2.1 s per frame, 120 frames per match, one process at a time) into <FD>/ball_eval_panel/<version>/<match>.suggest.<detector_sha8>.json. Frames with no candidate get null: "no ball" is never suggested, George must look for himself. This is eval-only inference on heldout footage; nothing is trained, mined or cached into a training pool, so rule zero still holds.
  • Page. The suggestion is a dashed yellow overlay (not a box, never saved). Y / button accepts it: it is saved as an ordinary human box [in_play_ball, labeller, accepted_suggestion, suggest_det:<sha8>]. Drawing a box replaces it. Accepted boxes are ordinary tier-1 labels everywhere (scoring, ingest, export, job done rule); the marker is audit only and never excludes or down-weights a label.
  • Bias control. A random 25% of each panel's windows (sampling.suggest = "blind", seeded by sha1(panel_version + match), reproducible from the panel file) and all QA cards (repeats and gold) never show a suggestion. Because the blind subset is random, blind-vs-shown labels are comparable: panel_score reports, per match and pooled, the share of labels that were accepted suggestions and the model's hit@r / recall / false-ball rate (HT estimate) on blind vs shown with the difference and its CI. A big gap means the suggestions move the labels. score --blind-only scores the suggesting detector on blind windows only (the model most favoured by its own suggestions).
  • Labels placed before suggestions existed (George's first Forest cards) are unsuggested: the suggest meta file records them and the scorer counts them as blind-equivalent.
  • Live jobs keep their items. The flag is also derived from the panel file at request time (same seeded rule), so no job mutation is needed; new panels get it in sampling.suggest.

docs.title: 2.3 Design: stratified two-stage sample with logged π
docs.text:
• Strata = heldout match × difficulty band. Allocation is equal per match, because per-match CIs are the deliverable.
  • Difficulty bands come from a reference model frozen at panel creation: the current detector plus tracker on the window, using the existing easy / gappy / contested / low_evidence buckets. Hard bands are oversampled toward Neyman allocation, n_h ∝ N_h·√(p_h(1−p_h)), with p_h from the Forest pilot.
  • Bound the weights: every band gets at least 30% of its proportional share, so max/min weight stays ≤ about 10. Frames are re-weighted by 1/π, so oversampling never biases the estimate. Bands only buy variance reduction, so a stale reference model costs efficiency, not correctness.
  • v1 can be simpler: uniform windows within each match, with match as the only stratum. This needs no detector run on heldout matches. Add difficulty bands in v2, once v1 gives per-band pilot rates.
  • Every card stores sampling = {regime:"eval", panel:"ball-eval-v1", match, stratum, window_id, pi_window, pi_frame, seed}, plus the sampler code sha.

docs.title: 2.4 Estimators
docs.text:
• Per-frame outcomes for model M (top-1 ball after tracker, or detector top-1 for detector eval):
  • hit (prediction within r px of the human centre)
  • off (prediction > r px away)
  • miss (ball present, no prediction)
  • false_ball (no ball, prediction)
  • true_empty
  • Metrics:
  • recall@r = hits / ball-present frames
  • precision@r = hits / predicted frames
  • false-ball rate = false_ball / no-ball frames
  • All are reported at r = 10 and 25 px.
  • Each metric is a ratio of Horvitz–Thompson totals. Its CI comes from a stratified cluster bootstrap, resampling windows within strata, 2,000 draws.
  • Reporting: per match, plus pooled as both match-averaged (headline: "a typical new match") and frame-weighted.
  • Later (v3): a PPI++ control variate. Use the auto-labeller's verdicts on every population frame as f, so θ̂ = mean_U(f) + HT-mean(Y − f). This cuts variance as far as f tracks Y, and it stays unbiased if f is poor.

docs.title: 2.5 Size and budget
docs.text:
• Recall around 0.7 with a design effect of about 1.5 needs about 120 frames per match for ±10 pp per match. Pooled over 9 matches that gives about ±3–4 pp.
  • Panel v1 = 9 × 24 windows × 5 frames ≈ 1,080 frames. At about 5 s each that is about 1.5 h, or 4–6 sessions. Start with 4 matches (about 480 frames) to get a usable number within a week.
  • The Forest "ball placement r1" job (600 frames, stratified, 10–20% done) becomes the Forest stratum of v1, re-expressed with its π.

docs.title: 2.6 Hygiene
docs.text:
• The panel is versioned and frozen. A new heldout match adds a new stratum and a new panel version; scores are always quoted with the panel version (cohort reporting).
  • Lockbox: keep 2 heldout matches out of day-to-day model selection. Score them only on promotion, to catch overfitting to the panel from repeated reuse.
  • In-match eval clips (1 in 5 of train-match clips) remain a secondary in-distribution number, using the same card and estimator.
  • Fix known contamination first: bournemouth_1st_seg070 is in Roboflow v11 training and hashes to in-match eval.

docs.title: 3.1 Pipeline per train match (machine-only before any human)
docs.text:
1. Run the detector (conf ≥ 0.1) plus the bidirectional tracker at stride 5 over main-camera segments. This is a GPU job via Prefect. Today it covers only Man City and Forest, so the 12 newly segmented matches need it.
  2. Build track segments: runs of frames the tracker follows. The candidate unit is the track segment, or a 2 s window of it, not a frame. This is how video redundancy is removed.
  3. Compute signals per segment:
  4. detector conf (mean, min)
  5. detector vs tracker disagreement
  6. forward vs backward tracker disagreement
  7. flicker (detections appearing and disappearing)
  8. trajectory plausibility (acceleration and jump limits in image space, homography-normalised where PTZ exists)
  9. static-object flag (near hoardings, i.e. spare balls)
  10. gap frames (tracker interpolates with no detection)
  11. appearance embedding (72-d ball descriptor) for diversity
  12. Run Claude verify on candidates, as the autolabel loop does now. Its confidence c becomes one more signal.

docs.title: 3.2 Buckets and per-round quotas
docs.text:
The quotas below are for a 300-card round, which is about one labelling day.

Bucket What Card Share Selection within bucket U: uncertain Signals disagree, c in 0.5–0.95, or det conf 0.3–0.7 verify 35% Rank by uncertainty, then one card per cluster (k-means on embedding × match × 30 s time bucket) and at most 1 card per 2 s window. Across rounds: no card within +-3 s of any earlier card of the same clip (exclude_s), and at most 3 U/M/N/R cards per clip per round (max_per_clip); each round's seed derives from its key M: missed Tracker gaps, plausible trajectory with no detection, ball-in-air candidates verify-or-place (tap if the ball is elsewhere, or "no ball") 20% Longest and most plausible gaps first; diversity as in U N: hard negatives High-conf detections off any plausible track, static near the hoardings, or on heads and feet verify (expected not_ball) 15% Highest conf first, capped per location cluster so it isn't 30 cards of the same spare ball R: random Uniform over the train-match population verify-or-place 15% Uniform. This is the cold-start and robustness floor, and also an unbiased audit of the whole pipeline on train data A: auto-accept audit Uniform random within the auto-accepted set, per score band verify, blind to c 10% Uniform within band. This is what calibrates the threshold (§3.3) G: gold Known-wrong boxes: GT shifted 15–30 px, or known spare balls verify 5% Measures over-acceptance. Excluded from training
  • Match balancing: cap each match at about 15% of a round. Prioritise matches with the fewest labels and the highest broadcast-OOD score. Generalisation across matches is the bottleneck, so breadth beats depth.
  • Labeller check: if the planted-wrong (gold) cards are accepted more than 10% of the time, the round's verify labels are flagged. The fix is then UI (e.g. making "box_off" one tap), not the labeller.
  • Adaptive within a round: a hook fires every 50 verdicts (§19c; the ballcheck-rescore flow named in the README doesn't exist yet). It refits the cheap pieces: the per-bucket hit rates, and the Platt fit of c → P(correct) as was done for broadcast. It then reorders the unanswered U and M cards. No retrain is needed mid-round.

docs.title: 3.3 Auto-accept threshold (Learn-then-Test)
docs.text:
• Score s = calibrated P(correct | c, tracker-consistent, det conf, plausibility).
  • For each candidate threshold t on a grid, the A-bucket audits with s ≥ t give a binomial p-value for H₀: precision < 0.98. Fixed-sequence testing from high t downward finds the lowest t whose H₀ is rejected at δ = 0.1.
  • Only A-bucket (uniform within band) cards are valid for this. U-bucket verdicts are not exchangeable.
  • About 150 audits per band are needed before a band can open. Until then, auto-accept stays at c ≥ 0.95. I recommend setting the queue's auto_conf back from 0.8 to 0.95 now.
  • Track audit precision per match. The existing circuit breaker (< 0.97) should trip per match, not just globally, because broadcaster shift is the likely failure.

docs.title: 3.4 Turning verdicts into training data
docs.text:
• Positives:
  • tier 1 (placed or corrected)
  • tier 2 (ball on a shown box)
  • tier 3 (auto-accepted at the LTT threshold), loss-weighted 0.5 and capped at 3× the human positives per match
  • Negatives: a frame with a rejected FP enters as a background image only if the frame's ball status is known: an accepted ball elsewhere in it, or a "no ball" verdict. Otherwise an unlabelled true ball could be taught as background. export_training_dataset.py currently drops not_ball boxes and needs this case added.
  • Composition check per export: % from each bucket, each match and each difficulty tag. Auto-accepted labels skew easy (ball on grass), so hard strata must come from U, M and N.
  • Retrain cadence: a round ends at about 300 human cards plus the auto-accepts. Retrain when cumulative new labels reach about 1,000 or weekly, whichever comes first. Then re-score the pool and re-mine. Report every model on the eval panel (§2) at its fixed version.

docs.title: 4. Leakage rules (enforced in code, not by convention)
docs.text:
1. split_of(match) gates every sampler. The eval sampler accepts only heldout matches and the training miner only train matches.
  2. The job API rejects a ball_check or ball_place job whose items mix splits or whose sampling.regime disagrees with the split.
  3. In-match eval clips, plus ±10 s around them, are excluded from mining. Consecutive _segNNN clips are not contiguous; use footage-time overlap once T-33/T-49 land.
  4. Heldout footage is never pseudo-labelled. A "self-train on the deployment match" mode, if wanted, gets its own lockbox eval.

docs.title: 5. What has to be built
docs.text:
P0 (small, now): - Set auto_conf back to 0.95. - Add a sampling metadata block to job items and persist it with each verdict. - Make the README list the 5 Ball Check verdicts.

P1: eval panel v1. - A ball-eval-panel sampler (jobs repo) that emits ball_place jobs on 4 heldout matches, uniform windows, with π logged. - An HT + cluster-bootstrap estimator in ball_eval, with CIs on the progress page. - Fold the Forest r1 job in. - Dependency: heldout matches segmented (pipeline running now). No detector run is needed for v1.

P2: training miner. - Merge tap-to-place, "ball elsewhere" and "no ball" into Ball Check on main. They are built on feat/autolabel-retrack (f92fdc8). - A detector+tracker GPU flow for the new train matches. - A bucket sampler with quotas and diversity. - Gold injection. - The A-bucket audit and LTT threshold. - Export negatives.

P3: - The ballcheck-rescore hook flow (in-round reordering). - Eval difficulty bands (panel v2). - PPI++ surrogate. - OOD-driven match priority.

docs.title: 6. Scheduling: the two loops (Prefect)
docs.text:
Loop 1, on ingestion (per match). It runs after match-pipeline (jobs docs/design/match_pipeline.md) has segmented a match, and branches by split_of(match): - heldout: ball-eval-panel(match) (cpu, merlin) samples windows uniformly within main-camera segments, logs π, and submits a blind ball_place job. It needs no model output. - train: - ball-candidates(match, detector_sha) (gpu; detectors at stride 5 plus SAM2 gap-fill; skip key is the detector sha) - ball-motion (desktop cpu) - ball-pool-score (merlin cpu): pool, then solver, then the scorer gives P(real); writes ball_pool/<match>/pool.<scorer>.parquet - Tier-3 auto-labels are the nodes with P ≥ the LTT threshold.

These are added after the pooled-labeller experiment (exp/ball-candidate-pool) settles which sources stay. - Trigger: an hourly, deduped sweep (ball-eval-panel-sweep, ball-pool-sweep) finds matches that are segmented but not yet done. It does not edit match-pipeline, so it works whichever orchestrator produced the segments.

Loop 2, the recurring round.

Step Trigger Runs Sample Tick (every 15 min): create a round only if open training cards < 100 and today's cards < 600 ball-round: miner quotas (§3.2) over the train pool, then a ball_check job, then ballcheck-prepare Refit Labeller hook, every 50 verdicts Scorer calibration + LTT threshold refit; reorder unanswered U/M cards Close Hook on_done Ingest verdicts, recompute the auto-accept set, nightly dataset export Retrain Weekly or ≥ 1,000 new labels ball-train (gpu) Evaluate After train Score the candidate on the fixed eval panel (no human); promote via the single promotion mechanism if it is better Re-infer On promotion Backfill ball-candidates + pool for train matches at low gpu priority, behind ingestion

docs.title: 7. Decisions needed
docs.text:
1. Eval cards: blind placement (reusable, unbiased, slower), versus showing the model box (faster, but tied to one model). Recommendation: blind.
  2. Headline metric: match-averaged or frame-weighted? Recommendation: match-averaged, with both shown.
  3. Lockbox: which 2 of the 9 heldout matches?
  4. Auto-accept target precision: 0.98 at δ = 0.1, and the 0.8 → 0.95 rollback now.

docs.title: Research: Bidirectional + Trajectory-Aware Ball Tracking for Offline Autolabelling
docs.text:
Update (2026-11). The detection-based bidirectional tracker from this note now exists and is scored in Ball tracking evaluation; it works on detector candidates rather than pixel trackers seeded from human marks, so it answers a different question. The anchor-plus-fusion idea below is reused by the proposed Claude-assisted ball labelling loop, where Claude-confirmed detections are the anchors. The text below is unchanged and historical.

Bead: ft-dva · Date: 2026-06-21 · Researcher: polecat flint Question: In offline video autolabelling for ball tracking, can we exploit bidirectional temporal information — track forward and backward from sparse human GT marks, then fuse with trajectory interpolation to fill difficult frames — and is it worth adding as Method E in the bake-off?

Headline. Yes, bidirectionality is real, native, and cheap to get — SAM2's video predictor already propagates backward (propagate_in_video(reverse=True)), and "fit a ball trajectory through sparse anchors + gated candidates" is a 20-year-old, well-validated idea in broadcast-soccer tracking. But it is not a "Method E" in the current bake-off. It is a different kind of thing: the bake-off scores causal, per-frame trackers (track(prev_bbox, frame) called in forward order), and a bidirectional/trajectory method by definition needs the whole clip and all anchors up front. It does not fit the BallTracker protocol and should not be forced into it. The right move is to treat bidirectional + trajectory fusion as a post-processing / fusion layer that wraps the bake-off winner, not as a competitor inside it — and, given the architecture review's finding that detection, not tracking, is 100% of the failure, to build the cheapest version of it (SAM2 backward propagation from anchors) now, because it directly buys the thing we actually lack: filled-in GT between sparse human marks.

docs.title: 1. Why bidirectionality matters here specifically
docs.text:
The whole premise of this pipeline is sparse human GT every ~N frames (the architecture review argues N must be measured, not the assumed 5 — see §3 of that doc). A causal forward tracker seeded at anchor frame k tracks until it drifts, then waits for the next human mark at k+N. The frames just before k+N — where forward drift is worst — get the worst labels, even though there is a perfectly good human anchor sitting one or two frames ahead of them.

Bidirectional tracking is the obvious fix and it is only available offline, which is exactly our regime:

anchor k                                                    anchor k+N
  ●───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────●
  ├──▶ forward track (good near k, drifts toward k+N)
                                          backward track ◀──────┤
                                          (good near k+N, drifts toward k)
  └────────────── fuse the two estimates per frame ────────────┘
       weight by distance-to-nearest-anchor / per-frame confidence

Every interior frame is now bracketed by two estimates, each most reliable at the end nearest its own anchor. Fusing them (confidence- or distance-weighted) strictly dominates a single forward pass, and the residual gaps (mutual low-confidence = occlusion) are exactly where a trajectory prior (parabolic / constant-velocity) should interpolate. This is the single highest-value temporal trick available to an offline autolabeller, and the current design uses none of it.

docs.title: 2. Angle 1 — Models with native bidirectional tracking
docs.text:
Model Bidirectional? Mechanism Fit for us SAM2 (video predictor) Yes, native propagate_in_video(reverse=True) walks frames range(start_frame_idx, end, -1); memory bank is acausal in offline mode Best fit — already promptable from a box, already a bake-off candidate (Method B/D family). Backward pass is one extra call. DEVA (Tracking-Anything w/ Decoupled VOS, ICCV'23) Yes — bidirectional by design "task-agnostic bi-directional temporal propagation" + in-clip consensus over a short future window; XMem as the propagation core Strong, but built around dense mask propagation of generic objects; heavier than we need for one tiny ball. Good source of the fusion idea. XMem Online/causal core, but used bidirectionally inside DEVA Feature-memory propagation Only bidirectional when wrapped (DEVA does the wrapping). SAM3 (incumbent) Same video-predictor lineage as SAM2 Expected to expose the same reverse propagation Already the control/ceiling (Method D); a backward pass should be ~free to add. TrackNet / WASB (heatmap, multi-frame) Symmetric multi-frame, not "bidirectional" per se Consumes a window of consecutive frames (e.g. 3) and outputs a center heatmap; learns the flying pattern, not just appearance Different paradigm — a detector that already uses local temporal context. Relevant as a candidate-generator (§5), not as the bidirectional engine.

Takeaway: we do not need to adopt a new model to get bidirectionality. The segmenter family we are already benchmarking (SAM2/SAM3) provides it natively. DEVA is the reference design for how to fuse the two directions, not a model we must run.

Sources: SAM2 issue #253 — "prompts from the future", SAM2 video predictor source, DEVA (ICCV 2023), DEVA GitHub.

docs.title: 3. Angle 2 — SAM2 backward propagation: confirmed and trivial
docs.text:
This is the load-bearing fact, so it is worth nailing precisely. From the SAM2 sam2_video_predictor.py source, the propagation entry point is:

def propagate_in_video(
    self,
    inference_state,
    start_frame_idx=None,      # defaults to earliest frame with input points
    max_frame_num_to_track=None,
    reverse=False,             # ← the bidirectional switch
):
    ...
    # reverse=True  →  end = max(start_frame_idx - max_frame_num_to_track, 0)
    #                  for f in range(start_frame_idx, end - 1, -1):  ...

So the recipe to fill the interval [k, k+N] from a single human box at frame k is exactly two calls:

state = predictor.init_state(clip_frames)
predictor.add_new_points_or_box(state, frame_idx=k, box=human_gt_box, obj_id=1)
predictor.propagate_in_video(state, start_frame_idx=k, reverse=False)  # k → k+N
predictor.propagate_in_video(state, start_frame_idx=k, reverse=True)   # k → k-N

Two practical notes from the source / issue thread:

  1. Backward from frame 0 is skipped ("skip reverse tracking if starting from frame 0") — irrelevant for us, anchors are interior.
  2. The community-recommended pattern (issue #253) is precisely ours: seed on the frame where the ball is biggest / least occluded, then propagate both ways. This is the right anchor-selection heuristic — the human should be nudged to mark clean frames, and the labeller can then bracket each anchor in both directions.

The memory bank carries object identity in both temporal directions in offline mode, so the backward pass is not a hack — it is a supported, documented mode.

Cost: one extra propagation pass per anchor interval. For an offline batch labeller (no real-time constraint) this is negligible, and it halves the worst- case drift distance (each frame is now at most N/2 frames from its nearest anchor, not N).

docs.title: 4. Angle 3 — Trajectory interpolation with ball physics
docs.text:
Two regimes, and they want different priors:

  • Ball in free flight (pass, shot, clearance): disregarding air friction, the ground-plane velocity is constant and the ball follows a single parabola. In image space a 3D parabola projects to a smooth conic-ish arc; a low-order polynomial / spline fit per flight segment is the standard, well-validated model.
  • Ball rolling / dribbled / in a ruck: motion is near-linear and slow; a constant-velocity Kalman prior (already in the design — KalmanBoxState) is the right model.

The classic broadcast-soccer literature does exactly this fusion:

  • Trajectory-based ball detection & tracking (Yu et al., and the broadcast-video line of work): generate many ball candidates per frame (not one detection), build a candidate graph across frames, and find the trajectory as the smoothest physically-plausible path through that graph. Occlusion gaps are bridged by interpolation between contiguous trajectory fragments. This is structurally a global, offline, bidirectional optimisation — it uses future and past candidates to disambiguate the present. It directly handles our two hard cases: false positives (other white/round objects are pruned because they don't lie on a smooth trajectory) and occlusion (interpolated through).
  • Physics-based 3D position work fits a parabola to the 2D trajectory to recover depth — over-kill for 2D autolabelling, but it confirms the parabola is the right interior model for flight.
  • Modern multi-mode state models (real-time 3D reconstruction papers) keep centimetre accuracy through severe occlusion by switching between motion modes (flight vs. ground) — the practical lesson is use a mode-switched motion model, not one global parabola, because a match is a sequence of short flights and rolls, not one ballistic arc.

For us this means: after bidirectional propagation, the remaining holes (both directions low-confidence ⇒ occluded) are filled by a piecewise trajectory fit — parabolic within a detected flight segment, linear/CV otherwise — anchored on both the human GT boxes and the high-confidence propagated boxes on either side of the hole. The two human anchors that bracket an interval already give the interpolation its endpoints; bidirectional propagation densifies the interior; the trajectory fit only has to cover the genuinely-occluded residue.

Sources: Trajectory-based ball detection & tracking in broadcast soccer, Physics-based 3D ball position from monocular sequences, Real-time 3D soccer ball trajectory reconstruction (multi-mode state model), Ball trajectory inference w/ Set Transformer + Bi-LSTM.

docs.title: 5. Angle 4 — Prior work on football ball tracking (bidirectional / smoothing)
docs.text:
The field has converged on a clear pattern for broadcast soccer/sports ball tracking, and it is not "one detector per frame":

  1. Over-generate candidates, then resolve globally. Broadcast ball tracking has been candidate-graph + trajectory-fitting since the mid-2000s precisely because per-frame detection of a tiny, blurred, occluded ball is unreliable — the exact failure our failure analysis reports (detection = 100% of misses, 21.6% recall). The trajectory layer is what makes an unreliable detector usable. This is strong external corroboration that temporal/trajectory reasoning is the right lever for our bottleneck, not just a nicety.
  2. Heatmap multi-frame detectors (TrackNet / WASB). Instead of a box detector, regress a Gaussian heatmap of the ball centre from a window of consecutive frames, learning the flying pattern. TrackNet reports F1 ≈ 98.5% on tennis; WASB is the current SOTA heatmap family across several sports. These are detectors that bake in short-range temporal context — a far better candidate-generator for the trajectory layer than our single-frame YOLO, and a plausible answer to the detection bottleneck independent of the bake-off.
  3. Bidirectional sequence models. Recent work (Set Transformer + hierarchical Bi-LSTM) infers ball position from multi-agent (player) context when the ball is unobservable — i.e. when even the trajectory is broken, players' trajectories constrain where the ball must be. This is the long-occlusion backstop, and it is inherently bidirectional (Bi-LSTM reads the sequence both ways).

Takeaway: every mature broadcast-ball system uses more temporal information than we currently do, and the bidirectional/trajectory direction is the mainstream, validated approach — not a speculative add-on.

Sources: TrackNet (arXiv 1907.03698), Ball trajectory inference (Set Transformer + Bi-LSTM), Real-time localization of a soccer ball from a single camera, AWS ball-trajectory tracking in broadcast sports.

docs.title: 6. Angle 5 — Should this be "Method E" in the bake-off?
docs.text: No — and forcing it to be one would corrupt the bake-off. Here is the precise reason, grounded in our own code.

docs.title: The bake-off protocol is strictly causal
docs.text:
ball_eval/interface.py defines the contract every method must meet:

"One BallTracker instance is created per eval clip. The harness calls track() once per frame in forward temporal order."

def track(self, prev_bbox: BBox | None, frame: np.ndarray) -> BBox | None: ...

A method only ever sees the current frame and the previous box. It has no access to future frames, to the full clip, or to the downstream anchors. This is correct and deliberate: it measures forward tracking quality, which is what an interactive labeller needs.

A bidirectional / trajectory-fusion method fundamentally violates this:

  • It needs the entire clip (to propagate backward and fit trajectories).
  • It needs all the GT anchors at once (the brackets it interpolates between).
  • It cannot produce frame f's label from (prev_bbox, frame) alone — its whole value comes from using frames >f and the anchor at k+N.

You cannot honestly score it on the per-frame, forward-only frames_held / center_distance metrics, because it isn't doing per-frame forward tracking. If you shoehorned it in (e.g. by pre-running both passes and replaying the fused result through track()), it would post near-perfect numbers by construction — it has seen the answer at the next anchor — and would not be comparable to the honestly-causal A/C/D methods. It would not win a fair fight; it would refuse to fight fair.

docs.title: What it actually is: a fusion / post-processing layer
docs.text:
