Bidirectional + trajectory fusion is orthogonal to the per-frame runner choice. It wraps whatever per-frame tracker the bake-off crowns:

        ┌─────────────────── bake-off scope (causal, per-frame) ───────────────────┐
        │  Method A/C/D runner: track(prev_bbox, frame) → box, in FORWARD order     │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                          │  winner = best per-frame runner
                                          ▼
        ┌─────────────── Method E scope (offline, whole-clip) ──────────────────────┐
        │  for each anchor interval [k, k+N]:                                        │
        │     fwd  = run winner forward  from anchor k                               │
        │     bwd  = run winner backward from anchor k+N   (SAM2 reverse=True)       │
        │     fuse fwd/bwd per frame  (distance-to-anchor / confidence weighted)     │
        │     fit piecewise trajectory through residual occlusion holes              │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

So "is it Method E?" is the wrong question. The bake-off picks the per-frame engine; bidirectional fusion is the offline harness that runs that engine twice and stitches the results. Adding it as a peer competitor would be a category error.

docs.title: How to evaluate it instead
docs.text:
It needs its own metric, scored against held-out human GT it did not receive as anchors: - Hold back a subset of human-marked frames as hidden test points. - Give the fusion layer only the other anchors. - Measure centre-distance / IoU at the held-out frames → this is the true autolabel quality between marks, which is the number that actually matters for the flywheel (label quality → retrain set → recall lift).

This is a leave-anchors-out evaluation, not a forward-tracking race.

docs.title: 7. Recommendation
docs.text:
Build the cheap version now; do not add it to the bake-off. Ordered by leverage:

# Priority Action Why E1 P0 Add a backward propagation pass to the SAM2/SAM3 labelling backend: for each anchor, call propagate_in_video(reverse=True) as well as forward, and fuse the two estimates per frame (weight by distance-to-nearest-anchor, break ties by confidence). Native, ~free, halves worst-case drift. This is the single biggest offline win and uses a model already in the bake-off. Directly densifies GT between sparse marks — the thing we lack. E2 P0 Treat bidirectional fusion as a post-processing layer wrapping the bake-off winner, not a BallTracker. Keep the bake-off protocol strictly causal (do not add Method E to interface.py). The protocol is forward-only by design; a whole-clip method can't be scored on it honestly (§6). Preserves the integrity of the A/C/D comparison. E3 P1 Add a piecewise trajectory fit (parabolic in flight segments, constant-velocity otherwise) to interpolate the residual holes where both directions are low-confidence (= occlusion). Anchor the fit on human GT and high-confidence propagated boxes either side of each hole. Standard, validated broadcast-soccer technique (§4). Mode-switching beats one global parabola. Fills exactly the frames bidirectional propagation can't. E4 P1 Evaluate the fusion layer by leave-anchors-out: hide a subset of human marks, feed the rest, measure centre-distance at the hidden frames. Report this as autolabel-quality-between-marks. This is the honest metric for a non-causal method, and it is the number the flywheel depends on — not a forward-tracking score. E5 P2 Evaluate a multi-frame heatmap detector (TrackNet/WASB-style) as a candidate-generator feeding the trajectory layer, independent of the bake-off. Attacks the actual bottleneck — detection recall (failure analysis: 100% of misses). A temporal detector is a far better candidate source than single-frame YOLO. Separate track from the tracking bake-off. E6 P2 Backstop for long occlusions: a bidirectional sequence model conditioned on player trajectories (Bi-LSTM / Set-Transformer style) to infer ball position when even the trajectory is broken. Only worth it once E1–E3 are in and long occlusions are the residual failure mode. Highest effort, narrowest payoff — defer.

docs.title: One-line summary
docs.text: Bidirectionality is real, native (SAM2 reverse=True), and the mainstream broadcast-ball approach — but it's a whole-clip fusion layer that wraps the bake-off winner, not a Method E inside the forward-only bake-off. Ship the backward-pass + fuse step now (it directly densifies the sparse GT we're short on), add piecewise-trajectory interpolation for occlusion holes, and score it leave-anchors-out — keeping the causal A/C/D bake-off uncontaminated.

docs.title: Appendix: source grounding
docs.text:
• SAM2 native backward propagation — propagate_in_video(reverse=True) source, issue #253 "prompts from the future"
  • Bidirectional VOS design — DEVA, ICCV 2023 / GitHub
  • Trajectory-based broadcast-soccer ball tracking — Trajectory-based ball detection & tracking, Real-time 3D multi-mode reconstruction, Physics-based 3D position
  • Multi-frame heatmap detectors — TrackNet (arXiv 1907.03698)
  • Player-conditioned bidirectional inference — Set Transformer + Bi-LSTM ball inference
  • Project context — autolabelling architecture review, SAM3 motion-guided design, ball tracker failure analysis
  • Bake-off protocol (causal, forward-only) — src/footy_track/ball_eval/interface.py, src/footy_track/ball_eval/runner.py

docs.title: Calibration (camera → pitch) — Implementation & Inspection Plan
docs.text:
Status: PLAN · Stage §2.3 of system_design.md · Feeds §2.6 projection.md · KB bead ft-wn9

Goal: for every broadcast frame, estimate the image→pitch mapping so that detection boxes become (x, y) in pitch metres. Output lands in the feature store's source-tagged calibration table (see "Feature store" below; the old inline frame.homography columns are deprecated), and the existing PitchProjector logic consumes it.

docs.title: 0. What already exists (and what doesn't)
docs.text:
Piece State projection/projector.py — PitchProjector (anchor = bottom-centre for players, centroid for ball; NaN on low quality) Written + unit-tested, never fed a real H Feature store calibration / pitch_keypoint tables, frame_calibration_best and detections_on_pitch views, GT/proposal importer Implemented (see below) Broadcast classifier (classifier.py) — gates which frames are main-camera views Implemented Pitch model, line/keypoint detector, calibrator, any inspection UI Nothing

Two conventions to fix up front (both currently unspecified):

  1. Image coordinates of H. Detections are normalised top-left xywh and PitchProjector applies H straight to normalised anchors. So we define H as normalised image coords → pitch metres (origin centre spot, +x along the long axis, per projection.md §2). Internally the calibrator works in pixels and converts with H_norm = H_px · diag(W, H_img, 1).
  2. Pitch dimensions per game (game table / match metadata), default 105 × 68. The pitch model is parameterised by them.

docs.title: 1. Approach
docs.text:
Broadcast main camera = fixed position, pan/tilt/zoom only. That gives a clear progression:

  1. Per-frame homography (8 DOF) from detected pitch features. Enough for ground-plane projection; simplest to get working.
  2. Temporal propagation: calibrate keyframes robustly, carry H between them with frame-to-frame motion (feature tracking on pitch pixels, masking out players), reset on scene cuts (broadcast classifier / shot boundary). Smooth.
  3. Constrained camera model (later): solve the camera position once per game, then per frame only pan/tilt/roll/focal (≤4 DOF). Much more stable on close-ups with few visible lines, and it is what later enables ball height (not just ground shadow).

docs.title: Feature detector: pretrained first, own training only if needed
docs.text:
Broadcast pitch calibration is a well-studied task (SoccerNet camera calibration challenge), with public models trained on exactly this kind of footage. Options, to be evaluated in M1:

Option What it outputs Fit Pitch-keypoint pose model (YOLO-pose style, ~30 named pitch keypoints) Keypoints with ids → direct DLT/RANSAC homography Easiest to integrate (ultralytics already a dep); weak when few named keypoints are visible Keypoints + line heatmaps (SoccerNet-calibration-style HRNet models, e.g. "No Bells Just Whistles", PnLCalib) Keypoints and line intersections/tangent points → H or full camera Best reported accuracy; heavier, needs GPU for full-clip runs Classical, known-size features: white-pixel mask inside pitch → line segments + ellipse fits → identify features (penalty box, goal area, centre circle r=9.15 m, halfway line) by their geometry → solve Named lines/conics → H, and via plane-based calibration (Zhang) focal length + camera pose No training data and fully inspectable; the hard part is identifying which line is which (partial views, symmetric halves, occlusion). Contender for M1 and always used as the refinement step

The pitch model's known dimensions are what make calibration possible in every option above. The options only differ in how features in the image get matched to their counterparts in that model: hand-written geometric rules or a learned detector.

Plan: wrap whichever pretrained model wins behind a PitchFeatureDetector interface; add classical line-snapping refinement on top. Licences and weights availability are checked before adopting any of them. Fine-tune on our own frames only if M1 numbers say so (lesson from ball detection: measure before assuming more data helps).

docs.title: 2. Module layout
docs.text:
src/footy_track/calibration/
  pitch_model.py      # canonical pitch: lines, arcs, named keypoints (metres), param'd by dims
  geometry.py         # DLT/RANSAC homography, px<->norm, reprojection error, warp helpers
  detectors/          # PitchFeatureDetector protocol + pretrained impl(s)
  calibrator.py       # single-frame: features -> H + quality (inliers, reproj err)
  refine.py           # snap model lines to observed white pixels
  temporal.py         # keyframes + frame-to-frame propagation + cut reset + smoothing
  camera.py           # (M4) fixed-position PTZ camera model
  store.py            # write calibration / pitch_keypoint / run rows
scripts/calibrate_clip.py   # CLI: clip -> calibration run in the feature store
labeller/calibration.py + web/calibration.html   # inspection page (§4)

calibration_quality ∈ [0,1] is derived from inlier count + mean reprojection error so the projector's existing H_quality < 0.3 → NaN gate works unchanged; raw numbers are kept in run diagnostics.

docs.title: 3. Milestones
docs.text:
# Deliverable Done when M0 Pitch model + geometry utils + manual calibration in the inspection page (click ≥4 pitch points → H). Saves clicks as calibration GT. Overlay of reprojected pitch lines sits on the real lines for hand-clicked frames; ~50–100 GT frames across the eval_data/clips M1 Single-frame automatic calibrator (pretrained detector + RANSAC + refinement), run on sampled frames Scored against M0 GT: reprojection error (px), % frames calibrated, % within 5 px; ≥2 detector options compared M2 Temporal: keyframes + propagation + cut reset + smoothing; calibrate_clip.py writes to the store Whole clips calibrated; jitter metric low; failures flagged rather than silently wrong M3 Projection end-to-end: store H → PitchProjector → pitch positions; minimap in the page Players project inside pitch bounds; plausible speeds (< ~10 m/s); formation shapes look right M4 Fixed-position camera model; optional fine-tune on own GT Better accuracy on hard frames (close-ups, few lines) vs M2

Each milestone is its own PR, with tests, against main.

docs.title: 4. Inspection plan — how you check each step
docs.text:
One page, /calibration in the existing labeller FastAPI app (same hub, same Konva frontend patterns; per the KB, keep overlays as siblings of the Konva stage container). It grows panel by panel with the milestones:

Panel Shows Catches From A. Frame + model overlay Video frame with the canonical pitch lines reprojected through H⁻¹, toggled on/off The main check. Misalignment shows straight away, e.g. a penalty box drawn in the wrong place M0 B. Feature overlay Detected keypoints/lines with ids, green = RANSAC inlier, red = outlier Detector errors vs fitting errors M1 C. Bird's-eye warp Frame warped to top-down and alpha-blended over a pitch template Global distortion, wrong-half flips M0 D. Minimap Top-down pitch with projected players/ball/refs. Hovering a box highlights its dot, and the other way round Projection/anchor bugs, out-of-bounds players M3 E. Timeline strip Per-frame quality/reproj-error/keyframe/cut markers under the scrubber, with "jump to worst N" Temporal drift, bad stretches, missed cuts M2 F. Camera-param plots Pan/tilt/focal (or H-derived proxies) over time Jitter and jumps that look fine frame by frame M2/M4 G. Manual edit Drag points / click correspondences → re-fit, save as GT Produces GT and fixes bad keyframes M0

Plus a run comparison selector (two calibration run_ids, overlays in different colours) and a non-interactive contact-sheet report (grid of worst/median/best overlay thumbnails + metric table per run) generated by calibrate_clip.py --report, so a batch run can be judged in 30 seconds.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
• After M0: open a frame, click 4–6 points (corners of the penalty box, centre spot…), confirm panel A lines up across the whole visible pitch and panel C looks like a flat pitch. This validates the pitch model, the coordinate conventions and the maths before any ML. Then label the GT set.
  • After M1: contact sheet of worst-10 frames per detector + metric table vs GT. Decide which detector to adopt and whether fine-tuning is needed.
  • After M2: scrub 2–3 full clips with overlay on; watch timeline strip for red stretches; check params plot is smooth across pans and resets at cuts.
  • After M3: play a clip with the minimap; players should stay in the pitch and move smoothly; sanity metrics (out-of-bounds %, max speed) in the report.
  • After M4: same metrics as M1/M2 re-run; must improve on hard frames without regressing easy ones.

docs.title: 5. Risks / open questions
docs.text:
• Few visible lines (midfield close-ups): single-frame fails. Mitigated by temporal propagation (M2) and the camera model (M4); until then such frames get NaN + flagged, never a guessed H.
  • Left/right ambiguity: symmetric pitch, so a half-pitch view can map to the wrong end. Use temporal continuity from wider shots, and confirm it in panel C.
  • Player anchor is bottom-centre of the box; occluded feet bias y. Acceptable for v1; panel D will show how bad it is.
  • Compute: laptop has no GPU. HRNet-class detectors on keyframes only are OK on CPU; full-clip runs go to the WSL GPU box.
  • Pretrained weights licensing: confirm before adopting.

docs.title: 6. Feature store
docs.text:
Full spec: feature_store.md §3.7.

  • Tables. calibration (one row per game, source, run, frame: H as DOUBLE[9], normalised image → pitch m, quality, errors, review_status, origin_*) and pitch_keypoint (one row per correspondence). source ∈ hand_label | claude | classical | model. Runs are run rows with stage=calibration and params_json (model, prompt_version, …).
  • Best calibration. View frame_calibration_best: hand GT (incl. accepted/edited proposals copied into GT) > accepted machine > proposed by highest score; failed/rejected never win; a frame with any not_broadcast row (see below) has no best calibration at all; it reports the winning source/run.
  • Projection. View detections_on_pitch projects every detection in SQL (same anchors and 0.3 quality gate as PitchProjector; NaN when low quality, NULL when uncalibrated).
  • Import. python -m footy_track.feature_store.ingest_calibration --gt-dir <ball_gt_marks> --db <store> [--dry-run] loads calibration_gt/*.json, calibration_proposals/*.json and frame_type/*.json. Re-import replaces; each clip file lands on every game_id alias of that clip that has ball GT, so calibration and ball marks share game_id + frame_index.
  • Inline columns. frame.homography / calibration_quality / calibration_model_version are deprecated and unused.

docs.title: 7. Pre-labelling with Claude + proposal review
docs.text:
To cut the manual GT effort, footy_track.calibration.prelabel proposes calibrations that a human accepts on a phone (/calibration/review).

  1. Mask + hints (classical, no ML): HSV grass mask -> white-line mask (top-hat, low saturation, blobs removed) -> Hough segments merged into long lines -> numbered candidate points (line/line intersections, line ends, ellipse/line intersections, spots). The mask is good; the candidate points are sparse (iteration 1 measured only 1-3 of 5-6 GT points per frame within reach), so candidates are only optional hints.
  2. Localise (Claude, iteration 2): ClaudeIdentifier gets a stable, cached prefix (system prompt, schema, reference diagram with keypoint ids and straight-line ids) and per frame one image: the frame with a light labelled pixel grid (ticks every 100 px of the sent image). Claude returns points - any clearly visible keypoint from the enum with an approximate x, y (it may cite a hint's candidate_id to take its exact position) - and lines: visible lines by name (e.g. R_PEN_BOX_FRONT, HALFWAY_LINE) with two points on each, plus view info and an unusable flag. MockIdentifier takes the human GT, optionally adds Gaussian noise (sigma in px @1920), drops or mislabels points, and emits noisy line labels: this simulates Claude's imprecise localisation. Prompt is versioned (PROMPT_VERSION, now p2); token usage incl. cache read/write is logged in run params.
  3. Coarse fit: RANSAC DLT over the point labels (a points+lines DLT when fewer than 4 points). No fit -> failed with a reason, never a guessed H.
  4. Line refinement (calibration/refine.py, numpy LM, no scipy): all 8 DOF of H are optimised so that pitch-model lines and arcs, sampled where they project into the image and onto grass, land on the white-line mask. Cost = Cauchy of a distance transform of the mask, coarse-to-fine (40 px truncated+blurred -> 20 -> 8 px sharp). The labels stay in as a weak prior and, because a DLT from a few noisy clustered points can be arbitrarily poor, the refinement is multi-start (the DLT over every 4-subset of the labels plus the all-label fit); the winner is the lowest all-sample DT cost (off-image samples count as a miss, so hiding the model cannot win) plus a small term for label error beyond ~45 px. It is rejected - the coarse H is kept - if the cost does not improve, H is degenerate (singular / horizon across the bottom of the image), too little of the model stays on grass, or the in-view model moved more than 35 % of the image width.
  5. Score = fraction of reprojected model-line samples within a few px of the mask (after refinement) and the final DT residual; both are stored. The proposal keeps pre_refine (coarse H, score, errors) and refine (applied, reason, costs) for the eval. When refinement is applied, correspondences are re-expressed through the refined H (image_label keeps the as-labelled position) so that accept's re-fit of H from the points reproduces it.
  6. Proposals go to <gt dir>/calibration_proposals/<clip>.json (format: see the labeller README §16); accepting writes calibration_gt with an origin. Accepting over a frame that already has GT is a 409; for human GT (no origin) it needs an explicit overwrite=true and the review page asks first. The pipeline skips frames with human GT (or flagged not-broadcast, step 8) by default (--no-skip-gt to include them).
  7. Not a broadcast frame. Sampled frames that are not the main pitch view (replay, close-up, crowd/bench, graphic, goal-line camera) cannot be calibrated; they are marked with one tap (review page "Not broadcast" / key n, editor button) and are distinct from rejected (= the fit is wrong). Claude's view.main_camera_wide == false only shows a badge on the card; nothing is auto-marked. Two records: the proposal's status becomes not_broadcast (prev_status, reviewed_at kept; works for proposed and failed), and a frame-level flag in <gt dir>/frame_type/<canonical clip>.json ({"clip", "frames": {"<idx>": {"type": "not_broadcast", "ts", "run_id"?}}}, atomic write, mode kept) that outlives the proposal. It is a sidecar of its own rather than a section of calibration_gt so that file keeps meaning "frames with a calibration" for every existing reader (pre-label skip, feature-store GT import, GT list) and deleting a GT frame never drops the flag. Marking a frame that has GT (hand or accepted) is a 409 unless overwrite=true, which deletes that GT; accept / GT-save on a flagged frame are 409 until the mark is cleared (DELETE /calibration/api/frame_type/{clip}/{idx} restores the proposals' previous status). Consumers: the pipeline skips flagged frames with --skip-gt; the feature-store import turns the file into calibration rows (review_status=not_broadcast, no H, run frame_type_import) and the views drop such frames (frame_calibration_best none, detections_on_pitch no_calibration); the Ball Check labeller and training export can read calibration.frame_type.not_broadcast_frames. GET /calibration/api/proposals/... also returns NaN stats as null (a failed proposal with a degenerate H used to 500 and could not be shown).
  8. prelabel_calibration eval compares a run with human GT; prelabel_calibration sweep is the noise sweep (success rate at <= 5 / <= 10 px before and after refinement per label-noise sigma): it answers how precise Claude has to be.

Frames are read by calibration.video.read_frame: OpenCV 5.0 decodes some clips as all-black frames ("Cannot convert interlaced to progressive frames"), so it falls back to the ffmpeg CLI.

docs.title: 8. Lens distortion (division model)
docs.text:
A homography maps straight pitch lines to straight image lines; broadcast lenses do not. On wide shots the far touchline (long, near the top of the frame) visibly bows, and in the bird's-eye warp that shows as a curved edge and a real line sitting a metre or two off the drawn one (far-field depth is foreshortened: ~1 px of image error at the far touchline is ~0.25 m on the pitch).

Model. One-parameter division model about the image centre, x_u = c + (x_d - c) / (1 + k1 r^2), r^2 = |((x_d - c) * 2) / (1, aspect)|^2 (r = 1 at the middle of the left/right edge, vertical axis aspect-corrected; code in calibration/geometry.py). H maps the undistorted normalised point to pitch metres, so everything observed in the image (labels, detection anchors, drawn lines) is in distorted coordinates. Measured k1 on this footage is positive (about +0.01 to +0.03): the far touchline sags in the middle, pincushion in this convention, so the model's line bows the same way.

Storage / back-compat. A record carries distortion: {"model": "division", "k1": .., "centre": [0.5, 0.5], "aspect": 1.7778} next to H. Missing, null or k1 == 0 is exactly the old behaviour (the old cv2.warpPerspective path, byte-identical). calibration rows get distortion_k1 DOUBLE (added by ALTER ... IF NOT EXISTS on existing stores; only a centred lens is accepted by the importer), and frame_calibration_best exposes it.

Where it is applied. geometry.project_pitch_model/project_polyline_to_image (camera overlay), geometry.warp_to_pitch (per-pixel remap when k1 != 0), reprojection_errors, the labeller /fit, /warp, GT save and proposal accept (points are undistorted before the DLT, the stored H and points reproduce each other), the review/manual pages (they pass distortion through), PitchProjector.project_frame(distortion=...) and the SQL view detections_on_pitch. The SQL direction is image -> pitch, which is closed form (x_u = c + (x - c) / (1 + k1 r^2)), so the view undistorts the anchor itself from distortion_k1 and the stored image_width/height; the difficult inverse (pitch -> image) is only needed for drawing and lives in Python.

Estimation. refine_homography(..., fit_k1=True) adds k1 as a 9th LM parameter in the two finer stages (the coarse capture stage keeps it fixed), with a quadratic (non-robust) prior pulling it to 0 (K1_PRIOR_PX, scaled by k1_prior) and a clamp at +-0.15. k1=<value> without fit_k1 holds a given value (per clip / zoom level) and the coarse fit then undistorts the labels first. prelabel_calibration run --fit-k1 / --k1 0.012; the default stays off. k1 trades off against H (focal length / tilt) on frames with few lines, so a per-clip value is the safe way to use it.

docs.title: 9. The far touchline on a high wide camera (Bournemouth)
docs.text:
Failure seen on arsenal_bournemouth_1st_*: the fitted far touchline landed in the stands / on the hoarding (median 30-100 px off the real line at 1568 wide), most visibly at the HALFWAY_TOP junction. Diagnosed from the masks, not the labels (Claude's centre-circle / halfway points were right):

  1. Grass mask leaked. The hue-only test also accepts the dark green-tinted stands and the apron, so "grass" ran up past the hoardings and the line mask filled with hoarding lettering and crowd texture. grass_mask now redoes the mask with a saturation (0.58x) / brightness (0.5x) gate relative to the pitch's own median colour (pitch_colour) when that changes the result; frames it does not change keep the old mask byte-for-byte.
  2. The far touchline was not in the mask at all. From this camera it is 1-3 px, not brighter than the grass (a saturation dip, V ~ grass) so the V top-hat misses it. far_edge_line finds it as a long, thin, pale strip hugging the top edge of the pitch (opening with +-30 deg line kernels so players' legs drop out); it is ORed into lines_mask and also returned as Detection.far_line. It is suppressed if the strip is much brighter than the grass (FAR_MAX_V_RATIO; that is a white board base, which on Arsenal-Man City sits a few metres behind the real white touchline and must not attract the fit) or in the lower 40 % of the frame.
  3. Capture range. With labels only on the centre circle the coarse H puts the far line 70-200 px away, outside the 40 px capture of the DT. refine_homography(far_mask=...) adds a term (wide capture, weight FAR_WEIGHT = 2) pulling whichever model touchline projects highest to the strip, active only when it lands within FAR_MAX_DY_FRAC of the image height of it. fit_and_score passes det.far_line; other callers are unchanged. "On grass" is also tested with a few px margin, because the touchline is the pitch's edge.

k1 helps further (the circle and the far line cannot both fit a plain homography): --fit-k1 gave +0.05..+0.15 in score on the affected frames, but stays opt-in. Not fixed: frames where Claude gives < 4 usable points, and panned shots where the far line is out of view.

docs.title: 10. Hard views: Aston Villa and Bournemouth (pinhole camera mode)
docs.text:
What the verdicts looked like. Arsenal-Man City 32/14/15 accepted/rejected/failed, Aston Villa 12/23/4, Bournemouth 0/12/37. Most Villa verdicts and all but a few Bournemouth ones were given on fits made before the lens-k1 and far-touchline changes (rerefined/previous is only set on 5 Villa and 3 Bournemouth records; proposals carry no review timestamp). Findings, from rendering camera view + warp for every rejected frame and decomposing each stored H into a camera (refine.decompose_G: square pixels, centred principal point):

  1. Non-physical homographies. The three Arsenal matches' stored fits put the camera at about (0, -65, 15) m (x along the pitch, y behind the near touchline, z up; Villa accepted median (0, -64, 15), Man City accepted (0, -66, 15)). The Bournemouth rejects have |r1|/|r2| of 1.2 to 5.7 (a real pinhole is 1) and cameras at 7-45 m height. A free 8-DOF H can express such cameras; a centre-circle + halfway-line view (4-5 collinear/near-collinear labels) does not pin it down.
  2. The far-edge strip is the hoarding, not the touchline. On circle-only views the strip term of §9 pulls the model touchline onto the advertising-board base 1-3 m behind the real line; the whole pitch shrinks (Villa seg110 f45: model circle smaller than the visible ring and than Claude's own CC_LEFT/RIGHT labels; removing the term made it match).
  3. Claude's labels on Bournemouth failures are often wrong, not just imprecise (seg030 f154, seg009 f87: points floating on the grass or on the hoarding, 0/9 RANSAC inliers; seg035 f320: the circle's right extreme labelled as a penalty-box point). Not fixable offline; needs a prompt change / relabel (not attempted: <= 10 live calls budget, no evidence for a specific prompt fix).
  4. Villa corner/penalty-box views (seg020, seg140): no visible defect. Overlays sit on the visible lines at full resolution and the rejected frames differ from the accepted f36 by 4-17 px mean, so those verdicts are not explained by fit error that we can see.

Fix (opt-in --pinhole on run / rerefine). refine_homography(camera=True) replaces the free H by a 7-DOF pinhole camera (log f, rotation, camera centre) with the same cost; starts are the 8-DOF winner and a look-at grid fitted to the labels; CameraPrior can add a per-match camera-position prior (default weight 0: it did not help on the frames tried). It is skipped when the free fit already decomposes to ratio 0.8-1.25. fit_and_score(camera=...) also refits without the far-edge strip and keeps that fit when it lowers the median label error by > 4 px.

Measured (offline, stored labels, 1 process). 51 frames: see the task report; summary: Bournemouth wide circle frames (f805, f161, f251, f826, f229) go from ratio 1.2-5.7 to exactly 1 with far line on the grass edge and no boards in the warp; Villa rejected frames change by 4-29 px mean; accepted frames change by 2-12 px mean except Man City seg031 f328 (23 px, one regression: the camera fit disagrees with a box line the old fit followed). Not solved: circle-only frames where the model circle is still smaller than the ring (Bournemouth seg015 f586, f251), frames whose far touchline is out of view, and wrong labels (item 3).

docs.title: Calibration: production flow, match video to versioned per-frame calibration
docs.text:
Status: design, revised 2026-11-22 after the P3 evidence run (rig scheme decided by experiment D). No code changed. Classical only (no trained detector, no PnLCalib). Scope: the workflow around the existing PTZ V3 pipeline (reports/ptz_v3.md, ptz_v3_weak.md), not new geometry. Claims marked (V) were checked in code or files this session; (U) are unvalidated or proposed.

KB pages relied on: prefect-job-system (pools, queues, merlin move, one-heavy-process etiquette, S3 pattern), footy-datasets-and-progress (three versioned datasets, eval_result, nightly flow, DuckDB not LanceDB on the mini), footy-data-plane-reconciliation (one authority per data class). Memory: gpu-tests-via-prefect, mini-cpu-one-heavy-process, versioned-datasets-goal.

docs.title: 0. Concept and decisions
docs.text:
User concept: per-frame detection gives good locks; aggregate across many frames and shots to re-adjust the shared rig (match-wide bundle adjustment); offline. That is V3. Decisions: classical only; the rig (C, roll, k1) is shared by all segments of a match, but a segment may come from a different camera and must then be flagged, not forced.

Decisions 2026-11-20 (user): - Label-free at inference. No label-derived prior in a production run (rig JSONs from GT points become eval references only); labels build the eval set (calibration GT + accepted proposals). A run that used any label-derived input is marked contaminated in eval. - Outlier segments: all three, in order. Flag first (never forced onto rig); then try their own camera variant (existing recovery rig_variants, e.g. gantry C_x +-32.7 m); a segment that still fails gets H = NaN and is queued for the calibration editor, where it becomes eval GT (not an inference input). - Rollout: Man City first, then the other known matches. - Accuracy bar (confirmed): <= 1 m at ordinary depths, <= 2 m at the far touchline, > 5 m = failure. Gate tuned on accepted/rejected review proposals. - Two-level per-segment rig scheme dropped (P3, section 2.1); rig comes from a multistart fit_shared over one frame per segment (section 2.2, decided by experiment D). - Review via the existing proposals page* (calibration_proposals, accept -> calibration_gt with origin, section 3b), not a new verdict mode.

Decision (user, 2026-11-20): inference is label-free. No human labels and no GT-derived priors (leave_clip_out_rig, camera_rigs/*.json fitted from labels) may enter a production run. Hand labels exist only to build the evaluation set (calibration GT, plus accepted proposals, section 3b). Consequences: - The rig prior for a new ground must come from generic camera priors (gantry height/distance ranges) plus the match's own evidence; fit_shared's GT-derived prior is for research only. ptz_v3.md section 6 already shows a label-free rig within 0.16 m of the GT rig on Man City, from a good start; a bad start (5 m off) did not converge, so the start-diversity of the multistart carries the weight; P3 confirmed this (section 2.1) and experiment D confirmed label-free starts work for pitch accuracy (section 2.2). - k1 is estimated from the match (free in the refine, or fixed per ground) or left as a diagnostic; it is never seeded from labels (P3: k1 0 / 0.0147 / 0.03 changes GT error by less than noise). Where lines and GT points disagree on k1 (0.032 vs 0.0147), report the effect on metre error rather than choosing silently. - Any evaluation of a label-free run on a GT frame is clean only if no label touched the run; runs using a GT-derived rig are marked contaminated in eval_result (section 3). - Existing per-ground rig JSONs remain usable as evaluation references, not as inputs.

docs.title: 1. What exists vs what is missing
1.1 Exists (V)
docs.text: Piece Where What it does Per-segment solver calibration/ptz_temporal.py (solve_segment, joint_solve), scripts/ptz_temporal_segment.py::run anchors every ~100 frames (lines-only search), motion pairs, joint solve with the rig fixed (free_shared=()), recovery pass for weak segments (ptz_recover.py, only when standard pass accepts <50%). Writes calib_full.npz (marker, shipped last), line_f1_full.json, meta.json, solve_full.json. No GT needed (clip_gt stubbed). Match-wide rig fit ptz_temporal.fit_shared, fit_shared_multistart; driver scripts/ptz_temporal.py shared and sharedms Bundle fit of C, roll, k1 over single-frame Units. Cost knobs: multistart over C seeds, free= to fix k1. Fan-out flow ~/code/jobs/footy_ptz_temporal.py (deployment ptz_temporal.prefect.yaml, ptz-temporal-match, pool cpu, queue desktop), NOT in the footy-track repo one flow run per match, thread pool of max_parallel segments, rsync mp4 to desktop, run ptz_temporal_segment niced, ship results back to scratch/temporal/<match>_segNNN@<rig stem>/, calib_full.npz as done marker, skip_existing, one retry, dry-run plan. Mini is refused. Takes rig_json as a parameter. Combine calibration/match_calibration.py, scripts/calibration_match_combine.py picks main vs recovery result per segment, writes <calibration root>/ptz_v3/<match>.parquet + .manifest.json (content sha256, version_id = ptz_v3+<sha8>, _history/ on --update, refuses silent overwrite). KNOWN_MATCHES hard-codes 4 matches to rig stems. Reader / UI MatchCalibration, labeller/calibration_match.py + page projection by global frame. Store ingest of GT/proposals feature_store/ingest_calibration.py only calibration_gt/, calibration_proposals/, frame_type/ sidecars. Eval ~/code/jobs/footy_nightly_eval.py calibration adapter scores calibration_proposals runs only (n=14, success@5px 0.64 on 2026-11-17).

docs.title: 1.2 Missing (V) for "match video -> versioned per-frame calibration in the store"
docs.text:
1. No whole-match orchestration of the rig. The Prefect flow takes a fixed rig_json. The shared fit (shared, sharedms) is a manual research subcommand: it uses MATCH_DIRS keys mancity|villa|bmth, reads from /mnt/storage/footy_data, takes its prior from leave_clip_out_rig(clip) (GT-derived) and its output (C / roll_deg / k1 in ms_*.json) must be hand-converted to a rig JSON (ptz_v3.md section C says so). Nothing runs prep -> shared fit -> solve -> combine in one go. A new match has no rig JSON.
  2. No per-segment disagreement measure. fit_shared sees ~1 anchored frame per segment (95 frames from 162 Man City segments; 42 from 121 Bournemouth), then per-segment solves freeze that rig. (P3: more evidence per segment did not improve the rig; search/convergence did, section 2.1.) Nothing scores how well each segment agrees with the shared rig (section 2.2 (d)).
  3. No outlier-segment handling. Different-camera segments are only handled in the weak-segment recovery (rig_variants: C_x = 0, +-32.7 m, chosen from 4 probe frames), only when the standard pass accepts <50%, and the variant is stored in meta.json/camera_variant, not diagnosed per segment from the main run.
  4. Combine is not run by any flow, and rerun_weak handling is by directory convention.
  5. No ingest of the match Parquet into the feature store. RunKind.CALIBRATION does not exist (grep: no RunKind in src); the store's calibration table (PK game_id, source, run_id, frame_index, H DOUBLE[9], quality, distortion_k1, review_status) takes ~100k rows/match; its h_convention string (normalised_image_to_pitch_m) differs from match_calibration's (undistorted_normalised_image_to_pitch_m), and frame.calibration_model_version is deprecated. The frame_calibration_best view picks by source/status; machine run rows must not out-rank hand GT (U: check the view's ordering).
  6. No dataset version / per-version metrics for dense calibration. The calibration dataset (v1: 99 items, 74/21/4) is GT clips; nothing scores the V3 output against it (V3 reports score 20 + 5 + 3 + 1 GT frames by hand, err5 in the driver).
  7. Quality gate is implicit: accepted = F1 >= 0.5 on both neighbouring evidence frames; never validated against GT outside the scored frames (ptz_v3.md section 8).

docs.title: 1.3 Other local branches/worktrees (searched)
docs.text:
• Every calibration branch I could check is already merged into main or contains nothing orchestration-related: exp/calib-temporal-flow, exp/calib-temporal-weak-vit, feat/calibration-match-files, feat/calibration-store are 0 commits ahead of origin/main.
  • The only whole-match orchestration is the jobs-repo flow above (~/code/jobs, own git repo, default code_ref now pinned to a footy-track main sha by P0). It covers fan-out + resume only; nothing for the shared rig, combine, gate, ingest, or versioning. The design below extends that flow; it does not duplicate it.
  • footy_calibration.py in jobs is the LLM pre-labeller (proposals), footy_pnlcalib.py is the (deferred) trained-detector path: both unrelated.

docs.title: 2. Rig scheme: multistart shared fit, then fixed-rig solves (V, experiment D)
docs.text: Evidence: P3 (reports/ptz_v4_two_level.md on exp/ptz-two-level-p3, appendix A). Experiment D (section 5) decided the rig fit; report reports/ptz_v5_rig_search.md (tables reports/ptz_v5_assets/tables.md) on branch exp/ptz-rig-search.

docs.title: 2.1 Rejected: two-level per-segment rig scheme
docs.text: Per-segment free (C, roll) estimates plus a covariance-weighted consensus, then re-solve, was tested label-free on 162 Man City segments (P3) and dropped: - Single-start L1: rig 3.06 m from the GT-points rig (C_y -63.65 vs -66.58); per-segment median error 2.69 m (< 1 m for 2 of 145); GT frame median 0.40 vs 0.26 m for the existing fit (near third 0.58 vs 0.28 m, 32 of 39 frames worse, p < 0.001); 8.5 CPU-h vs ~0.1 CPU-h for the fit_shared rig fit. None of the six gantry segments produced an estimate, so d_i flagged nothing. - Per-segment multistart only reaches parity (rig 0.17 m, GT 0.26 vs 0.26 m) at ~10 CPU-h, ~100x the cost, and the covariances are still unusable as weights. - Causes (appendix A): (1) the optimiser stops on a long, curved C_y / C_z / f valley: lm_solve in ptz_temporal.py stops when a step gains < 1e-4 x total cost (2-7 units on a ridge with 130-300 to give), or stalls on a rough floor; tolerance 1e-6 / 1e-8 moves errors e.g. 2.81 -> 1.65 m, more iterations beyond that do not help. From the GT rig the same code stays within 0.1-0.7 m at a lower cost, so the objective is fine for pan-rich segments and each estimate scales with its start (4 m off moves ~1 m; 7.6 m off does not move). (2) Narrow-pan, zoomed segments (pan 2-5 deg, e.g. 080, 104) are genuinely unidentifiable: the per-segment optimum is 2-4 m off. (3) The per-segment covariance is 30-280x overconfident, and estimates sit 15-40 profile sd from the optimum because the solver stopped. Ruled out: evidence diversity as the reason fit_shared works (pooling did not move the estimate; multistart seeds near the truth and free k1 did), and anchors (2-6 per segment, no effect). k1 does not matter here (0 / 0.0147 / 0.03 within noise).

docs.title: 2.2 Revised design
docs.text:
(a) Rig fit (experiment D result): fit_shared_multistart over one frame per segment (the middle frame of each segment the lines-only search accepts; 89 units on Man City), started from the generic label-free prior (gantry height / distance ranges, never GT), k1 free, with the tight LM stopping rule on the finalists (rel_tol=1e-8, n_iter=100; lm_solve takes rel_tol, default LM_REL_TOL = 1e-4 so other callers are unchanged). The coarse (C_y, C_z) grid search with fixed-C pose solves (E3) was not needed: about 3x the CPU and no better. (b) Cost and evidence: about 3.3 CPU-min per match for the rig fit (vs 2.7 for the old rule, 10 for the grid search). All 18 label-free rigs (3 starts, 4 to 7.6 m off) met the accuracy bar on the 39 answered Man City GT frames (frame median 0.26-0.45 m, far-touchline p95 1.4-1.8 m, nothing above 5 m); E2 with k1 free had the smallest start-to-start spread (0.30-0.31 m). k1 free was not worse than fixed (small sample). Caveat: the rig itself is not identified. Fitted C lies 0.2-2.9 m from the GT-points rig, and the 89-frame cost is flat to about 1% along the C_y / C_z / f ridge, so it cannot rank rigs inside that scatter (the GT-points rig had a higher cost than 13 of 18 fits). The per-frame pose absorbs the error: a rig 2-3 m off costs only 0.05-0.2 m of frame-median pitch error. Consequences: (i) rig-hash versions (section 2.3) will change between runs and starts even when pitch accuracy does not, so a version bump is not evidence of a change in quality; (ii) evaluation must be on pitch metres (eval_result, GT frames), never on rig distance or rig cost. (c) Fixed-rig per-segment solves as today (free_shared=(), recovery pass for weak segments, variants for second cameras). (d) Per-segment diagnostic, no per-segment rig fit: fixed-C profile cost at the shared rig (1-5 s per segment) plus calibrated / accepted fraction from meta.json. P3 shows the fractions already isolate the six gantry segments (0% calibrated) with no new code. (e) Deferred: a bigger joint solve over many frames, and cross-segment rotation-only links (stacking frames of different segments on each other). Test only once (a)/(b) are fixed.

Cost class: the rig fit (~3.3 CPU-min), then one fixed-rig pass (Man City 97.6k frames, desktop 0.16-0.25 CPU-s/frame, 4.4-7 CPU-h); no multi-pass iteration. Heavy CPU on the desktop only, one heavy process (mini-cpu-one-heavy-process).

docs.title: 2.3 Versioning and partial re-runs
docs.text:
• Work dir stem <clip>@<rig stem>-<hash8> (P0, merged) so a changed rig never reuses a stale dir under skip_existing.
  • Cache key per segment (segment mp4 sha, code sha, k1, rig hash): a changed rig re-runs all segments, unchanged skips. No L1' round, so segment caches are not needed and keep_cache stays off.

docs.title: 3. Prefect flow design (U)
docs.text:
New flow calibrate-match in ~/code/jobs (own deployment, pool cpu, parent on mini-host/merlin; children use the desktop queue). Parameters: match, ground, version (e.g. ptz_v3), max_cpu_hours, dry_run, resume. No rig JSON in production (label-free); an optional rig_json is an eval-only, contaminated path.

  1. plan: read segments.json, segment hashes, dry-run CPU estimate, refuse if over budget.
  2. rig search (desktop, one process): section 2.2 (a)+(b); writes rig_search.json (per-start screening and final costs, chosen rig, k1). Abort-with-report if the finalists disagree wildly or most segments are rejected (wrong-camera match, e.g. Bournemouth); the cost cannot rank rigs within ~1-3 m, so do not gate on small cost differences.
  3. fixed-rig solves: fan out the existing ptz-temporal-match machinery (reuse calibrate_segment, do not fork) with the rig fixed; weak segments via the existing recovery / variants.
  4. diagnostic + gate (per frame, written as quality): accepted (F1 >= 0.5 both sides) / calibrated-unconfirmed / uncalibrated / other_camera; per segment the profile cost and accepted / calibrated fractions. Abstain (NaN H) for segments with no confirmed anchor or unresolved outliers; no interpolation across abstained frames; unresolved segments are queued for the calibration editor (eval GT, not an inference input).
  5. Combine: combine_match (existing), manifest extended with rig, rig_search.json hash, per-segment diagnostic, code sha; KNOWN_MATCHES becomes a parameter.
  6. Ingest (new feature_store/ingest_match_calibration.py): rows in calibration with source='ptz_v3', run_id=<version_id>, H, quality, distortion_k1, review_status mapped (never hand), dataset_tag='calibration_match'; bulk path (DuckDB on mini pinned 1.3-1.5.3), idempotent by run_id; add RunKind.CALIBRATION; resolve the h_convention mismatch in the ingest.
  7. Proposals export + review job (section 3b): export the seeded sample to calibration_proposals/<clip>.json, submit a labelling job via POST /api/jobs.
  8. Report artifact: Prefect markdown + reports/calibration/<match>/<version_id>.md (fractions per segment, rig, profile costs, flagged segments, CPU/wall, failures).

Resume: segments by done marker keyed on the rig hash; rig search by hash of its inputs; combine by content hash; ingest by run_id. Failed segments do not abort the match (flow ends Failed after combine, listing them).

Versioning and metrics: the calibration dataset is GT; V3 output is a model result scored on it. Extend the nightly eval adapter: per stored version_id, score H on GT frames (clip -> match frame via pts_frame_map), err5_median/p90/p95 split near / mid / far, answered_frac, gross_frac (> 5 m), plus accepted_frac / calibrated_frac; eval_result rows model_name='ptz_v3', model_version=version_id, global split authority, contaminated=true if any label-derived input. ptz-rig GT frames are not independent of a fixed-C solve (ptz_v3.md Bournemouth): scored separately.

docs.title: 3b. Human review: the existing proposals page (U)
docs.text: Reuse the existing review path (V): labeller/calibration_proposals.py reads calibration_proposals/<clip>.json; accept copies a proposal into calibration_gt with origin; reject records a reason. No new verdict mode, log, table or job kind on the match page. - Exporter (new, after combine): for each sampled frame, project the visible pitch keypoints through that frame's stored H into proposal keypoints, then distort them with the row's k1 (division model, as lens.py / the editor do: stored H takes undistorted coords, proposal points are observed coords), so accepting reproduces H and k1; origin ptz_v3@<version_id>; drawn from the stored row, never recomputed. - Sampling (stratified, fixed seed default_rng(sha256(match, seed)) over global frame ids, so every version is asked about the same frames): ~300 frames per match; status (accepted 50%, calibrated-not-accepted 25%, uncalibrated main-camera 10%, not-broadcast negatives 5%); zoom / pan / far-touchline-visible tertiles; segment boundaries and recovery seams; >= 5 frames per flagged or recovered segment; <= 3 per segment per stratum; >= 1 per segment of >= 500 frames (100 left too little of the budget for the status strata). Inclusion probabilities stored with each proposal. - Circularity rule: proposals from version V are never used to score version V. Accepted proposals feed % good (Horvitz-Thompson over inclusion probabilities, segment-clustered intervals), gate tuning (precision of accepted, F1 threshold sweep; the first version gives only an interval), and GT for other versions, always flagged by origin. Metres error for a version comes from hand-clicked / hand-edited frames or other-version proposals. Rejection reasons give failure-mode counts. - Neighbours: a decision covers one frame of one version; never propagate to unsampled frames. Adjacent frames share anchors (correlated errors) and a good sample does not certify a segment: a segment-level claim needs >= 3 decisions spread across it; a rejected accepted-frame queues extra samples from its segment.

docs.title: 4. Open risks, with evidence
docs.text:
• Bournemouth is a different camera: Vitality is low (C_z 7.8 m, C_y -50.8) vs Emirates (15.7, -66.6); lines weak (23/121 anchors accepted at F1 >= 0.55); GT rig from 7 frames (C_y bootstrap sd 1.6 m); k1 0.035 (sd 0.018) vs 0.0147 Emirates. Rig does NOT transfer between grounds (ptz_v2.md: "transfer weaker"); per-ground rig is required. Within Bournemouth the label-free C landed 0.14 m from the rig (multi-start), so within-match estimation works; the 2nd-half has no segments dir. Only one match per ground has been looked at: rig transfer between matches of the same ground is assumed, not tested beyond Man City -> Villa (leave-match-out, 19 GT frames, all answered after the rig change, median 0.45 m).
  • Second camera positions inside a match: Man City gantry (C_x +-32.7) on ~8 of 22 weak segments, Bournemouth seg100 at C_x -36.6; others (seg015, 066, 083, 103, 156) are unrecoverable by the three tried positions (seg156 fits C_x -11.5 / -21.5). The flow must carry an explicit unrecoverable state; 11 of 22 weak segments recovered (0% -> 53% of the weak segments' frames); 9 of the 22 end with 0% calibrated.
  • Far-touchline metre error (V3), Man City only: V1 far half slightly worse; V3 numbers are grid medians over the whole visible grid. The C_y/f ridge says depth error will grow with distance from the camera. Experiment D measured it on Man City (39 GT frames): far third median 0.34-0.63 m, p95 1.4-1.8 m across 18 rigs, within the 2 m bar; other grounds untested.
  • k1 disagreement: lines 0.027-0.034 vs GT points 0.0147 (Emirates), 0.009-0.019 vs 0.035 (Bournemouth). Unresolved; fixing it costs nothing measurable in pitch error on 20 + 5 GT frames but the true lens is unknown. Mitigation: fixed per-ground k1, k1 divergence reported.
  • Acceptance is not validated against GT (F1 >= 0.5 chosen by the author; the sample is small). Gate thresholds are provisional until section 3 metrics exist.
  • Frame-index correctness: seek inaccuracy and dropped frames (Bournemouth segments hold ~13% fewer frames than segments.json; CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES not exact) matter for the global-frame mapping in combine (pts_frame_map); a pts-based map exists, but is verified only on a few segments.
  • Cost surprises: one fixed-rig pass is 4.4-8.5 CPU-h for Man City on the desktop (P3 measured 8.5 h at a 4 m-off rig); desktop is shared with GPU/other flows; memory fault history (desktop-ubuntu-hardware-fault): keep the memory floor (min_avail_gb).
  • Unverified here: whether the multistart rig fit gives the same pitch accuracy from a label-free start on other matches (experiment D, Man City only); Bournemouth / Villa untested.

docs.title: 5. Phased plan (small PRs, each with an acceptance test)
docs.text:
Status: P0 merged (jobs #3: rig-hash work-dir stem, KNOWN_MATCHES parameter). P1 / P2 (per-segment rig estimate, consensus) closed unmerged (#123, #124). P3 evidence run done: two-level rejected (section 2.1).

PR Content Acceptance D (done, 2026-11-22; reports/ptz_v5_rig_search.md on exp/ptz-rig-search) On the 40 Man City GT frames (10 of 14 GT segments) using cached data: compare (i) existing fit_shared from a generic label-free start, current stopping rule vs tight (1e-6 / 1e-8), (ii) match-level (C_y, C_z) grid search with fixed-C pose solves + converged refine; k1 free vs fixed. Report metres error by depth (near / mid / far median, p90/p95, within 1 / 2 / 5 m) and rig distance to the GT-points rig; also from a start 5-8 m off Decision memo in reports/: go/no-go on (a)+(b); result: go on multistart + tight rule + k1 free, grid search dropped (section 2.2); target <= 1 m ordinary depths, <= 2 m far touchline, no frame > 5 m, label-free start P4 calibrate-match flow (jobs): plan, rig search, fixed-rig solves, diagnostic + gate, combine, report Man City end to end from empty scratch with no rig JSON: manifest records rig, resume after a kill does not re-solve done segments, identical re-run = unchanged P5 ingest_match_calibration + RunKind.CALIBRATION, bulk path row count = calibrated frames; re-run no-op; frame_calibration_best still prefers hand GT; 100k rows under ~1 min on the mini P6 Eval adapter: ptz_v3@<version_id> on GT clips, near/mid/far split, nightly wiring, /progress series eval_result rows for the version; contamination flag set for GT-rig variants P6b Proposals exporter (stratified fixed-seed sample, keypoints projected through stored H), job submission, origin flags into ingest accepting an exported proposal reproduces the stored H; same seed gives the same frame ids for two versions; scoring excludes same-version proposals P7 Second ground (Bournemouth), gantry / high-camera handling, deferred items of 2.2(e) if justified Bournemouth rig within ~1.5 m of vitality.json C_y and C_z within 0.5 m; gantry segments flagged, not forced

D is the only item that spends meaningful CPU before the architecture commits; if it fails, keep fit_shared multistart and the rest of the flow.

docs.title: 6. Questions for the user
docs.text:
Answered: label-free at inference (section 0); outlier segments: flag, then variant, then NaN + editor (section 0); accuracy bar confirmed (section 0); review budget (moot: review runs through the existing proposals page at the user's pace); rollout Man City first (section 0). Obsolete, removed: cache retention (no L1' round).

Open: 1. Store trade-off: ingest only accepted frames (smaller) or all calibrated frames with a quality column? Should machine rows ever appear in frame_calibration_best, or only as a separate versioned dataset? 2. Bournemouth halves: the second half has no split_video_broadcast_frames yet; needed before P7?

(Desktop CPU for experiment D: approved 2026-11-22; done.)

docs.title: Proposal: calibrate the camera rig once, then solve each frame for pan / tilt / zoom only
docs.text:
Status: proposal, revised 2026-11-14 after review (gpt-6.1-sol critique). V1 offline validation is the first step; nothing else is built until it passes.

Decisions taken 2026-11-14: - Run V1 first (offline, no LLM calls). Stop if it fails. - Stop further LLM pre-labelling runs for now. - The user will label 2-3 Bournemouth penalty-box frames for the Vitality rig. - Pretrained SoccerNet calibration detectors are being researched (no install yet); see section 8.

docs.title: 1. Why the current approach struggles
docs.text:
Today every frame is calibrated on its own. It gets a free 8-DOF homography H (image → pitch), from LLM point labels plus line refinement, and optionally a lens k1. That works when a frame shows many points that are spread out and not in a line, such as a penalty box with the goal area. It breaks down in the middle third of the pitch. There the visible markings are the halfway line, the centre circle and one or two touchlines: the points are nearly in a line, the circle is a conic that the LLM labels badly, and the far touchline is thin and often confused with the hoarding base. Eight unknowns cannot be pinned down from that. The fitter then drifts into homographies that are not compatible with a square-pixel, centred-principal-point pinhole camera (the review notes this only shows incompatibility with those assumed intrinsics; a wrong principal point, uncorrected distortion or a rescaled feed could also explain it).

The review results show this: - Arsenal–Bournemouth: 0 accepted, 12 rejected, 37 failed. - Aston Villa: 12 accepted, 23 rejected. - Of the rejected Bournemouth fits, many decompose to non-square pixels, |r1|/|r2| from 1.2 to 5.7 (an ideal square-pixel pinhole gives 1). - 21 of the 49 Bournemouth records had only 1–3 LLM labels, so they were starved of points.

docs.title: 2. The key fact: the main broadcast camera does not move, it only pans, tilts and zooms
docs.text:
The working hypothesis is that the main camera sits on a fixed head on the gantry. Between frames only pan, tilt and zoom change, plus a roll that we model as shared but must verify. Its centre of projection C is then approximately fixed for a whole match, and possibly for other matches at the same ground. This is a hypothesis to test, not a fact: the table below shows consistency of a few selected decompositions, not proof of constancy.

We checked this on our own labels by decomposing every hand or accepted calibration into a pinhole camera (square pixels, centred principal point):

Ground Frames (plausible camera) Camera centre C, median (x, y, z) m IQR (x, y, z) m Focal length range Emirates, Man City match 33 (0.0, −65.2, 15.2) (1.4, 3.9, 0.8) 2700–5500 px (2× zoom) Emirates, Villa match 11 (0.2, −64.3, 15.0) (1.9, 5.0, 0.9) 1780–2890 px Vitality (Bournemouth) 4 (−0.1, −49.3, 7.3) (0.8, 5.9, 0.1) 1890–4180 px

Coordinates are in metres from the centre spot: x along the pitch, y toward the far touchline (so negative y is behind the near touchline), z up.

What the table shows: - C is consistent across the frames of a match to within a few metres in y, even though the zoom doubles. The two Emirates matches give similar medians. Shared modelling assumptions (centred principal point, no lens model, pitch dimensions) could produce a shared bias, so this is evidence for the hypothesis, not proof. - The Bournemouth row rests on only 4 frames and cannot establish a fixed C by itself. - Bournemouth's camera is very different: 49 m back and only 7 m up, against 65 m and 15 m at the Emirates. That low angle squashes the far half of the pitch, which is exactly where the labels fail. It also means the default camera prior in refine.CameraPrior, (0, −65, 15), is wrong for Bournemouth. - The spread in y is probably the usual depth-focal ambiguity of one frame. A joint fit across frames should reduce it; V1 measures this with bootstrap uncertainty rather than assuming it.

A note on "extract the intrinsics". The focal length is not constant; it changes with zoom. What carries over from a well-labelled frame is: - the camera centre C; - the principal point and pixel aspect, which are fixed by the camera; - the mount roll; - the lens distortion as a function of zoom, k1(f).

The per-frame unknowns are then pan, tilt and focal length (parametrised as log f), and maybe a small roll: 3-4 DOF instead of 8.

Mechanical definition (to be pinned down in code): rotation R = Rz(roll) Rx(tilt) Rz(pan) applied to a fixed base orientation, intrinsics in normalised image coordinates [0,1] with the principal point at the image centre unless the rig fit says otherwise, distortion applied in the division model before the pinhole. A tilted pan axis does not in general give a constant image roll through a pan; V1 checks whether a shared roll is adequate or roll must be per frame (small, regularised). Real heads can have offset pivots and non-intersecting axes, so C is allowed to differ slightly from frame to frame (see "C as a prior" below).

docs.title: A. Calibrate the camera rig once per ground (and check it per match)
docs.text:
• Pick 3-6 "rich" frames from the main camera: penalty-box views and wide views with at least 6 points that are not in a line and span depth. Select them for diversity of pan, tilt, zoom and pitch coverage, not just point count. Label them carefully in the existing editor. These are the only frames that need full point labelling.
  • Fit them all jointly (bundle adjustment):
  • shared C, shared roll offset and a constant k1 to start with;
  • per frame, the rotation and log f.
  • k1 as a function of focal length (the earlier idea k1(f) = a + b/f) has no demonstrated physical justification. Start with constant k1 and add zoom dependence only if the residuals show a trend against f.
  • C is a prior with tolerances, not hard-fixed. In per-frame solves C enters as a Gaussian prior (sigma set from the rig fit, for example a few metres in y and under 1 m in x and z), so a frame that really needs a different C can have it at a visible cost. Do not assume a rig transfers to another match at the same ground; verify with a handful of frames from the new match.
  • Report parameter uncertainty (bootstrap over frames and over shots), parameter correlations (C_y against f is the expected one), held-out residuals and the per-frame reprojection error. A frame that disagrees is a labelling error, a different camera or model error; do not assume which.
  • Store the result as camera_rigs/<ground>.json. Grounds so far: Emirates (both matches), Vitality.

docs.title: B. Solve each frame for pan, tilt and zoom only
docs.text: With C as a prior, a frame has 3-4 unknowns. Counting alone does not make a solve well conditioned, so the claims below are what V1 tests, not assumptions: - 2 point labels can give a finite solution, though ambiguity and poor conditioning remain (two nearby points mainly constrain pan and tilt, hardly f). Points that are close to a line add little. One point plus an identified image line is different from one point plus a distance-to-line observation. - Lines alone. This is the hard part and must be semantic and multi-hypothesis, not a plain distance-transform match: - the search runs over bounded pan x tilt x log f (coarse-to-fine), with C at its prior; - each hypothesis is scored on visibility-aware, semantic evidence: predicted line segments that fall in the image are matched to detected line pixels (with the direction of the line), and detected line pixels that no predicted line explains are penalised too. A one-sided distance-transform score can reward laying a few predicted lines over unrelated edges (hoarding, goal frames, crowd), and pitch symmetry gives a competing mirror solution; - keep the top K distinct hypotheses (non-maximum suppression in parameter space), refine each with robust LM, and abstain when the best and second-best are near-tied in score or when line support is too low. A wrong answer that looks confident is worse than no answer; - LLM labels or a coarse "which half / which box" cue can disambiguate the mirror, as an optional seed. - Central views may become solvable, but the halfway line alone does not fix pan (it fixes pan only together with tilt/f or a second constraint). The circle and the far touchline constrain tilt and zoom. Whether that is enough is V1's question. - LLM labels (Claude or Codex) become an optional seed, e.g. "left box, near side", to narrow the search, plus a reviewer. They are no longer the main source of geometry.

docs.title: C. Track the camera between frames with a rotation-only model
docs.text:
• For an ideal, undistorted camera rotating about its optical centre, the motion between two frames is exactly H = K2 R K1^-1 for every static point in the scene, at any depth: the pitch, the hoardings and the stand architecture. Real PTZ heads need not satisfy this (offset pivots, focus breathing, distortion, stabilisation), and a more constrained tracker can do worse than a free homography when its assumptions fail. Undistort before applying the rotation model, and use differences between near and far scene depth as a detector of departures from pure rotation.
  • Track features on the stable stand architecture and the pitch, not on the crowd, flags, LED boards or players (those move). Fit the 3-4-DOF inter-frame motion and chain it from anchor frames, preferably with windowed optimisation against the anchor rather than relying only on chained transforms.
  • Every N frames, or when line support drops, re-snap to the lines with B to stop drift. At a cut back to the main camera re-solve with B. Shot-level acceptance by the user does not guarantee later frames stay accurate, so sample frames across the shot for review.
  • This builds on footy-track-df's calibration/temporal.py. Their chaining gives 0.40 m mean on seg010 with a general homography; rotation-only is expected to be at least as good, but that is to be shown (V3), not assumed. Test it early, not last.

docs.title: D. Shots from other cameras
docs.text:
• The shot classifier (calibration/shots.py, main / closeup / other) sends only main-camera shots through B and C.
  • A recurring second camera, such as an 18-yard-line camera or the high camera behind the goal, can get its own rig later by clustering the C values. Close-ups and replays are skipped.

docs.title: E. Labelling
docs.text:
• Rich frames (rig): the existing point editor, plus a live readout of each frame's implied C against the rig and of pixel squareness, so a bad click shows at once.
  • Ordinary frames: a new PTZ alignment mode. The pitch overlay is drawn from the rig. The user drags to pan or tilt and scrolls to zoom, and an "auto-snap" button refines against the lines. Typical effort is a drag and a snap; alternatively click any 2 points.
  • Review page: B and C generate proposals for whole shots and the user accepts or rejects as now. One verdict on a shot anchor stands for the whole chained shot.

docs.title: 4. Validation before building UI (offline, no LLM cost, 1 CPU process)
docs.text:
1. V1, leave-match-out and leave-shot-out on the Emirates. There are 44 plausible GT frames over the two matches. Leave-one-frame-out is not used: neighbouring frames of the same shot leak. Splits are:
  2. leave-match-out: fit the rig on the Man City frames, test on Villa (and the reverse as a check);
  3. leave-shot-out within each match: frames grouped by clip/segment, never split across train and test. For each test frame, solve with C as a prior from:
  4. (a) all its GT points;
  5. (b) random 2-point and 3-point subsets, many draws;
  6. (c) near-collinear subsets (halfway line + centre-circle points only, or one line's points + one other), to mimic central views;
  7. (d) lines only: the semantic multi-hypothesis search of section 3B on the actual video frame, with abstention. Baselines: free 8-DOF homography and the existing 7-DOF pinhole fit without the C prior, from the same inputs. Where they are under-determined (fewer than 4 points) that counts as a failure, and we state it, rather than inventing a regularisation that flatters either side. A comparison against TVCalib-style segment-based optimisation is in section 8.
  8. Metric: pitch-metre error against the GT homography over a grid of visible pitch points. Report median, p90, p95, failure/abstain rate (and accepted coverage), split near half and far half, and by zoom (f). Also pixel reprojection error, and runtime.
  9. Synthetic tests with known ground truth: generate a known rig, project pitch points and lines, add noise, and check that C, f and the angles are recovered, including central views, extreme zooms and near-collinear inputs. This separates solver faults from GT faults.
  10. GT caveats. The GT is itself imperfect: 56 of 70 frames are accepted LLM proposals, 7 pinhole refits and 7 hand labels; 19 frames have exactly 4 correspondences (fit error near 0, weakly determined); the user accepted some with tolerance for curved or pre-lens lines, so GT noise is about 0.5 m. Errors below that are not meaningful, and frames where the rig and the GT disagree are listed, since they may be GT errors.
  11. Pass if: (d) has a median under 1 m on main-camera frames, with p90/p95 and the failure rate reported and not catastrophic (a median hides tails), and (b) and (c) are clearly better than free H.
  12. V2, Bournemouth.
  13. Build the Vitality rig from the 4 existing GT frames plus the 2-3 rich penalty-box frames the user will label. First validate the fixed-centre assumption independently there (4 frames is too few to claim it).
  14. Run B (lines only, plus stored LLM labels as seeds) on the rejected and failed Bournemouth frames.
  15. Publish the results as a review run; the user's verdicts measure usability, so show proposals blinded against the free-H proposals, and also compute independent geometric errors on any withheld hand labels. Low viewing angles amplify pixel errors into metres near the horizon, so report error by distance.
  16. V3, temporal. Compare rotation-only against general-homography chaining on several shots with different zooms and durations (not only seg010), with identical anchors and tracks. Report endpoint and maximum drift, cut recovery and failure coverage, against footy-track-df's 0.40 m on seg010.

docs.title: 5. Risks and open questions
docs.text:
• The centre of projection may move with zoom. The entrance pupil of a broadcast zoom lens can move by up to roughly 0.5 m. At 45-65 m that is about 1% in depth, but translation along the axis is not generally reproduced by a change of f (the effect is depth-dependent), so we do not assume it is absorbed. If V1 shows a trend of C with f, model it as an offset along the optical axis as a function of f.
  • Other camera effects: focus breathing, zoom-dependent principal point and distortion, lens stabilisation, platform vibration, offset or non-intersecting pan/tilt axes, and set-up changes between matches. Cropping, digital stabilisation, resizing, interlacing, blur and rolling shutter change the effective camera. Per-match verification of the rig is part of the plan.
  • The principal point may not be at the image centre (cropped or rescaled feeds, lens decentring). Fit it per rig, not per frame.
  • More than one main camera. Some broadcasts cut between a high and a low "main" camera at similar angles. The C values would form clusters, so handle them as two rigs.
  • Pitch size varies by ground (Vitality is not necessarily 105 × 68). Wrong dimensions bias C, so fit the dimensions in the rig fit or look them up.
  • The rig only covers the main camera. Other cameras still need the per-frame free fit or are skipped. The shot classifier has to be accurate enough.
  • Lines-only search is the largest unresolved component: pitch symmetry, partial circles, repetitive parallel markings, goal frames, hoarding edges and advertising create competing minima, and a near-empty view (only grass and a touchline) is ambiguous along the pitch. Mitigations: semantic, multi-hypothesis scoring and abstention (3B). Temporal chaining may cover such frames; B alone may not.
  • Low camera (Bournemouth): at 7 m height small pixel errors become large ground errors near the horizon; camera height error, pitch crown/slope and occluded markings matter more there.
  • Ground truth quality: see the GT caveats under V1.

docs.title: 6. What changes for the work in flight
docs.text:
• Further LLM pre-labelling runs are stopped (decision 2026-11-14) until V1 reports.
  • LLM pre-labelling becomes a seed and reviewer step rather than the main source of geometry. The Claude-vs-Codex comparison is still useful, re-aimed at "is the seed in the right area?" and "does the reviewer agree with the user?".
  • The Bournemouth pre-label run (bmth_pre1, Claude Opus, 33 calls) is optional under this plan. Its frames can serve as seeds, or as candidates for rig frames.
  • Existing GT stays valid. It is also the training and validation data for V1.

docs.title: 7. Order of work
docs.text:
1. Run V1, about half a day of offline compute and code. Stop here if it fails. (Decided 2026-11-14.)
  2. Build the Vitality rig. Needs the 2-3 carefully labelled Bournemouth penalty-box frames the user will provide.
  3. Run B on Bournemouth as a review run, then get the user's verdicts.
  4. Add the PTZ alignment mode to the editor.
  5. Do rotation-only temporal chaining (C), with footy-track-df's temporal module. Start a small version of V3 in parallel with step 3, not at the end.

docs.title: 8. Comparison with published calibration methods
docs.text: We should compare against, not replace with a free homography as the only baseline: - TVCalib (segment-based camera optimisation): optimises a per-frame camera (focal, rotation, position) so projected pitch line segments match detected segments. Our difference is the shared camera-centre prior and a rig fit across frames; the per-frame solve is closely related. If a pretrained detector for the SoccerNet pitch-keypoint/line segmentation task is usable, its output can seed our search or serve as an extra baseline. - SoccerNet camera-calibration challenge protocols: they report a completeness-weighted accuracy at a pixel threshold and often use a homography-based pipeline with a segmentation of pitch lines and keypoints. Their data lacks per-match rigs; ours is the opposite regime (few matches, many frames each). We should report our metrics in a way that can be related to theirs (reprojection error in pixels at thresholds, and coverage) as well as in metres. - Pretrained SoccerNet detectors are being researched (2026-11-14, no install yet). The outcome decides whether lines-only initialisation uses a learned detector or our hand-built line search.

docs.title: Claude-assisted ball labelling loop
docs.text:
Status: PROPOSAL. Only the calibration pilot of section 8 is built; nothing else in this page is · Date: 2026-11-10 · Code reviewed: the ball-tracker branch (PR #36), which stacks on main @ 26d2506 plus the merged T-01 to T-04 fixes

This page is for anyone deciding how to get many more ball labels, from many more matches, without a person drawing every box. It proposes route J, "Claude-assisted ball labels": a loop in which the detector and tracker propose, a Claude model checks, and a person confirms only what is uncertain. It builds on two June notes, the autolabelling architecture review and the bidirectional tracking research, and on the scored measurement in Ball tracking evaluation.

Every number has a source next to it. Anything with no measurement behind it is marked unverified or proposed. Items that do not exist yet are marked planned.

docs.title: 1. Why
docs.text:
The ball is the whole problem (Best pipeline, summary). Three facts from the existing docs point at the same gap:

  • Diversity beats volume. Going from Roboflow v3 to v11 took RT-DETR-L ball mAP50 from 0.328 to 0.665 and recall from 0.244 to 0.59, while more frames from the same long clips will not help (Best pipeline, section 3). New matches are the lever.
  • Humans are the bottleneck. A Ball Check card takes about 3.3 s (18 per minute), measured from 360 decided verdicts on two days, one person (Best pipeline, route D). That is fast, but every card still costs a person's attention, and a new match has thousands of candidate frames.
  • Much of the loss is the detector, not the tracker. On the held-out clips only 74 of 119 human ball frames have any detector candidate within 25 px (62%), and no tracker can recover the rest (Ball tracking evaluation, results). Frames the detector misses are exactly the frames a person would otherwise have to place by hand.

A Claude model can look at a zoomed crop and answer a narrow question ("which of these boxes is the ball?"). The proposal is to use that to turn a person's job from "draw or judge every box" into "confirm the doubtful ones".

What this is not: it is not a way to produce evaluation data, and it is not a replacement for the human tiers. Claude output is tier 3 until a person says yes (section 6).

docs.title: 2. The loop
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  classDef code fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111

  classDef missing fill:#ffedd5,stroke:#ea580c,stroke-dasharray:5 3,color:#111
  classDef bc fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#111

  HELD[("Held-out registry<br/>planned")]:::missing
  PICK["1 Pick clips<br/>new matches first"]:::missing
  OV["2 Overview pass, optional<br/>scene state and coarse region"]:::missing
  DET["3 Detector candidates<br/>RT-DETR, conf 0.1 or more"]:::missing
  TRK["4 Bidirectional ball tracker<br/>PR 36"]:::code
  CROP["5 Crop and re-detect<br/>where no candidate near the path"]:::missing
  VER["6 Claude verify<br/>multiple choice on zoomed crops"]:::missing
  POOL[("claude candidate pool<br/>tier 3")]:::missing
  FILL["7 Anchors and fill<br/>tracker bridges between anchors"]:::missing
  BC["8 /ball_check<br/>uncertain first"]:::bc
  SC[("Sidecars<br/>tier 1 labeller, tier 2 human_checked")]:::data
  ING["9 Ingest verdicts<br/>ingest_gt, detection_review"]:::code
  EVAL["10 Re-score<br/>ball tracking eval"]:::code
  RT["11 Propose a retrain<br/>when enough new tier 1 or 2"]:::missing

  HELD -. "never enters" .-> PICK
  PICK --> OV
  PICK --> DET
  OV -. "where to look" .-> CROP
  DET --> TRK
  TRK --> CROP
  TRK --> VER
  CROP --> VER
  VER --> POOL
  POOL --> FILL
  FILL --> BC
  BC --> SC
  SC --> ING
  ING --> EVAL
  EVAL --> RT
  RT -. "new weights" .-> DET

Legend, as in Architecture: blue is code in git, orange dashed is planned or not in git, purple is the /ball_check path, grey is data. The diagram shows one pass of the loop: pick clips, find candidates, fill the gaps, have Claude check, show a person the doubtful ones, ingest the answers, re-score, and only then consider a retrain. The detector step is orange because the batch inference script is not in git (T-09).

The steps, in plain words:

  1. Pick clips. Unlabelled clips, new matches first. A clip whose canonical id (footy_track.clip_id) is in the held-out registry is refused (section 7).
  2. Overview pass (optional). For each window, send Claude three downscaled frames one second apart. It returns, per second, the scene state: ball in play, ball in the air, out of play or off-screen, replay or close-up; plus a coarse region of the frame where play is. This pass is only for scene state and where to look. It never gives positions. Evidence: in an informal visual review of 10 clips, the model could not reliably spot a ball of about 11 px at full-frame scale. That review is not recorded in the repo (unverified); the 11 px size is the 1280 px figure in Tracking pipeline design, top risk 3.
  3. Candidates. The existing RT-DETR detections (conf 0.1 or more, route F machine labels) and the bidirectional tracker from PR #36 give one candidate path per frame.
  4. Crop and re-detect. Where no candidate lies near the expected path, crop around the tracker's predicted or interpolated position (or the overview region), upscale the crop, and run the detector again on it, so a ball of about 11 px becomes about 30 to 40 px. The 3x to 4x scale is a target, not a measurement (planned); /ball_check already upscales crops to 640 px wide for people (LAB-1008 in the labeller spec, src/footy_track/labeller/README.md).
  5. Claude verifies. Multiple choice only (section 4).
  6. Anchors and fill. Claude-confirmed detections become anchors and the bidirectional tracker fills between them. This is the anchor-plus-fusion design of the June research note, with Claude supplying first-pass anchors where that note assumed human marks.
  7. Human review in /ball_check. Proposals go to a new candidate pool with provenance claude (tier 3).
