  1. hand_label rows (this includes accepted/edited proposals that were copied into GT; their origin_* columns say where they came from),
  2. machine rows with review_status='accepted',
  3. proposed machine rows, highest quality first,
  4. failed / rejected rows (and any row without an H) are never chosen.

Ties break on newest created_at, then run_id DESC, so the view is deterministic.

detections_on_pitch — every detection row left-joined to its frame's best calibration and projected in SQL: x_pitch/y_pitch (metres) and x_pitch_norm/y_pitch_norm ([0,1], using the calibration's pitch dims, default 105×68), plus projection_status, calibration_source/_run_id/_tier. Anchor: centroid for ball labels, bottom-centre of the box for everything else. Gate: quality IS NULL OR quality < 0.3 (H_QUALITY_THRESHOLD in the projector) → NaN with status low_quality; no calibration at all → NULL with status no_calibration. A test pins the SQL to PitchProjector.project_frame. Note the view covers all detection rows; join detections_enriched on (game_id, frame_index, source, run_id, detection_id) and filter canonical for one batch per frame. PitchProjector itself only treats the exact label ball as a ball; the view also treats the GT labels in_play_ball / out_of_play_ball as balls (otherwise GT balls would be anchored at the box bottom).

Inline frame.homography columns — decision. Deprecated, not removed: nothing in the repo wrote or read them (grep: schema/store only), but dropping columns would break from_parquet of existing exports. The views ignore them. Do not fall back to them: an unattributed H with no run, score or review status is exactly what the calibration table exists to avoid.

Importer (feature_store/ingest_calibration.py): python -m footy_track.feature_store.ingest_calibration --gt-dir <ball_gt_marks> --db <store> [--dry-run] [--clip X] reads calibration_gt/*.json (run calibration_gt_import, source hand_label) and calibration_proposals/*.json (one run per runs key) per the sidecar contract in calibration.md.

  • Replace semantics (as T-04): per game, the file is the truth. One transaction deletes the game's calibration/pitch_keypoint rows with that importer's dataset_tag, then inserts; other writers' rows are untouched. A file whose frames are all malformed keeps the earlier import.
  • game_id mapping: ingest_gt keys ball GT by the sidecar stem (not canonicalised, §3.1a) while calibration files are keyed by canonical_clip_id. A file is written to every game_id whose canonical id matches — each <stem>.jsonl in --gt-dir plus existing game rows — falling back to the canonical id if none. E.g. arsenal_mancity_seg010.json lands on arsenal_mancity_seg010, arsenal_mancity_20250925_seg010 and mancity_seg010, so detections_on_pitch projects the ball GT of each alias at the same frame_index (same video, same frame numbering). The cost is duplicate rows per alias; if the aliases are ever collapsed (§3.1a migration) the duplicates collapse with them.
  • Malformed frames/points (bad key, non-3×3 or non-finite H, unknown convention or status) are skipped with a warning, never a crash.

docs.title: 4. Embeddings live outside the hot path
docs.text: Frame/instance embedding vectors (embeddings.parquet in the old model) are not stored in frame or detection. A 512–1024-dim float vector per frame bloats every scan of the spine. Keep them in a dedicated frame_embedding(game_id, frame_index, embedding LIST<FLOAT>, model_version) table (or a vector store later), joined only when needed. Same rule for any future per-instance appearance descriptors used for re-ID.

docs.title: 5. How each requested feature maps in
5.1 Per-frame info (path, resolution, clock, frame number)
docs.text: → frame columns frame_uri, width/height, continuous_time_s + half + game_time_s, frame_index. (§3.2)

docs.title: 5.2 Broadcast features (binary yes/no, confidence, model version)
docs.text: → frame.is_broadcast (BOOLEAN), broadcast_confidence, broadcast_model_version. The model_version resolves to a run row for full provenance. (§3.2, §3.5)

docs.title: 5.3 Pitch segmentation (final polygon + thresholds/allowances)
docs.text: → frame.pitch_polygon (list of normalised points = the final segregation line), pitch_seg_threshold (the allowance), pitch_seg_confidence, pitch_seg_model_version. Polygon stored as LIST<STRUCT(x,y)> (DuckDB native, explodes cleanly); a WKB/GEOMETRY column is an alternative if we adopt DuckDB's spatial extension for point-in-polygon "is this player on the pitch" queries — recommended once we need geometric predicates. (§3.2)

docs.title: 5.4 Calibration / homography
docs.text: → calibration + pitch_keypoint tables and the frame_calibration_best / detections_on_pitch views (§3.7); the inline frame.homography columns are deprecated. Absorbs geometry.parquet.

docs.title: 5.5 Object detections from multiple sources
docs.text: → detection table, one row per object, tagged by source + run_id. Hand labels, SAM 3, and YOLO predictions over the same frame are distinct rows distinguished by source/run_id; none overwrites another. SAM 3 instance masks are large — store the box in detection and the mask as RLE/PNG in a sidecar referenced by mask_ref (don't inline mask blobs in the hot table). (§3.3, §6)

docs.title: 5.6 Tracking (longer term)
docs.text: → detection.track_id + detection.is_interpolated for per-frame membership, track_meta for per-track summary and identity. Schema and lifecycle already specified in player_tracking_format.md; this store is where those rows live. (§3.3, §3.4, §8)

docs.title: 6. Multiple sources over the same frames — the central pattern
docs.text:
The hardest requirement is "object detections likely from multiple sources/runs — hand-labelled, SAM 3, YOLO — all with locations and confidences." The pattern:

  • source is the kind of producer (hand_label, yolo, sam3, bytetrack). run_id is a specific production of that source (weights + params + date). Two YOLO weights → two run_ids, same source.
  • A detection's full key is (game_id, source, run_id, frame_index, detection_id). The same physical player in the same frame appears as separate rows under each source — by design. No source is privileged in storage.
  • Idempotency: re-running a run upserts on the PK and replaces that run's partition; it never touches other sources. Concretely, ingestion writes detection/game_id=<id>/source=<src>/run_id=<rid>/part.parquet atomically (write-temp-then-rename), so a re-run is a partition swap.
  • Comparison/eval becomes a self-join: ground truth is just source='hand_label'; precision/recall vs YOLO is detections_enriched WHERE source='hand_label' joined to source='yolo' on IoU. No separate eval format needed — the MOT-CSV exporter from player_tracking_format.md §4 becomes an optional view, not a storage concern.

Partition layout on disk:

store/
  feature_store.duckdb            # the single store (index over parquet)
  game/part.parquet
  run/part.parquet
  frame/game_id=<id>/part.parquet
  detection/game_id=<id>/source=<src>/run_id=<rid>/part.parquet
  track_meta/game_id=<id>/source=<src>/run_id=<rid>/part.parquet
  detection_review/game_id=<id>/part.parquet   # Ball Check verdicts, see 6.2
  calibration/game_id=<id>/source=<src>/part.parquet     # §3.7
  pitch_keypoint/game_id=<id>/source=<src>/part.parquet  # §3.7
  frame_embedding/game_id=<id>/part.parquet
  masks/game_id=<id>/<frame>__<detection_id>.png   # mask_ref targets

docs.title: 6.1 Importing existing label sets
docs.text:
Implemented in src/footy_track/feature_store/importers.py. Two label sources land as detection rows under different sources and stay comparable:

  • Roboflow YOLO datasets (import_roboflow) → source='hand_label', run_id='roboflow_v<version>'. Handles the three format gaps: YOLO centre xywh → store top-left xywh; class indices → names via data.yaml; Roboflow's mangled filename (<stem>_<frame>_png.rf.<hash>.jpg) → (game_id, frame_index). Frame dims are read from the image. Validated on roboflow_dataset_3: 257 frames, 4 915 detections.
  • Web-labeller / SAM 3 JSON (import_labeller_json) → source='sam3' by default (so it can be evaluated against the hand labels), or source='hand_label' to treat verified output as ground truth. Boxes are already top-left; uri (<stem>_frame_<frame>) → (game_id, frame_index).

Frame identity is shared because both decode to <video_stem>_<frame_index> (extract_frames names frames <stem>_%06d). Two label sets align frame-for-frame only if extracted from the same video at the same fps; source_overlap(store) reports, per (game_id, frame_index), how many sources are present so overlap (and thus comparability) is verified empirically rather than assumed. continuous_time_s is derived frame_index / fps + time_offset (default 1-fps extraction, offset 0) pending true kickoff alignment.

docs.title: 6.2 Ball Check verdicts (detection_review)
docs.text:
Ball Check (labeller §11) records human yes/no verdicts in a side log, <gt-dir>/ball_checks/<clip>.jsonl, never in the sidecar. They reach the store through feature_store/ball_checks.py::import_ball_checks, run by ingest_gt after the sidecars (--ball-checks-dir, default <gt-dir>/ball_checks; run it after sidecar ingest because the sidecar upsert re-sets reviewed).

Per (source, frame_index, box_index) the latest line wins and a verdict: null tombstone retracts. Every live verdict is written to detection_review(game_id, vsource, frame_index, box_index, verdict, ts, label, bbox_*, matched_source, matched_run_id, matched_detection_id, match_iou) (additive table; replaced per clip on each run, so the import is idempotent). detection_id is positional and box_index counts all boxes on a frame, so a verdict is matched to a ball-class detection on the same frame by IoU >= 0.5 (corrected_bbox also tried), not by index. Unmatched verdicts (candidate boxes never ingested, boxes since removed) are still stored with NULL matched_* and counted in the import report.

Verdict Effect ball, corrected matched detection.reviewed = TRUE (source unchanged) not_ball rejected negative: detection_review.verdict='not_ball' with a match; a cand verdict never rejects a hand_label row (counted as a conflict) unsure, box_off recorded only, no change to detection

scripts/export_training_dataset.py excludes matched not_ball boxes from positives by default (the exporter has no negatives/background concept, so they are just dropped); --include-rejected keeps them. Rows with no verdict are unaffected.

Known limitation. The exclusion joins on the stored detection_id (positional per frame/source). If a sidecar is edited so boxes shift position and is re-ingested without re-running the verdict importer, a not_ball verdict can point at the wrong box. Re-run ingest_gt (which re-imports verdicts) to refresh. The follow-up TODO "match verdicts to detections at export time (by overlap) instead of by stored detection_id" removes this; test_export_survives_reingest_after_boxes_shift (strict xfail) encodes the intended behaviour.

docs.title: 7. Idempotency, keys, and write protocol
docs.text:
• Primary keys (enforced in DuckDB; logically honoured in Parquet):
  • game(game_id)
  • frame(game_id, frame_index)
  • detection(game_id, source, run_id, frame_index, detection_id)
  • track_meta(game_id, source, run_id, track_id)
  • detection_review(game_id, vsource, frame_index, box_index) (§6.2)
  • calibration(game_id, source, run_id, frame_index); pitch_keypoint(game_id, source, run_id, frame_index, point_idx) (§3.7)
  • run(run_id)
  • Upsert semantics: ingestion is INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (DuckDB) / partition-replace (Parquet). Re-ingesting an identical run is a no-op on row count. This satisfies the footy-stats "re-upload must not duplicate" rule from the project CLAUDE.md.
  • GT-sidecar re-ingest is replace, not merge (ingest_gt). A bare upsert never deletes, so a corrected or deleted box left a ghost row (e.g. an old gt_import_vittrack row still marked canonical after the box was rewritten as labeller), and positional detection_ids shift when a sidecar line is removed. So ingest_gt_jsonl / ingest_gt_dir (default replace=True, CLI --replace/--no-replace) treat the sidecar as the source of truth for its clip: in one transaction they delete every detection and track_meta row with game_id = <clip> and run_id starting gt_import_, then insert the freshly parsed rows. An emptied sidecar (or one with only skip markers) therefore clears the clip's GT rows. A malformed sidecar raises before the delete, and an error mid-way rolls back, so old rows survive. Left alone: all other runs for the game (roboflow_v*, sam3, hand-label imports), other games, and the shared game / frame / run rows. Re-ingesting an unchanged sidecar yields identical store contents. detection_id stays positional (per (frame_index, source) in sidecar order); delete-then-insert makes that safe. --no-replace restores the old merge-only upsert. A sidecar file removed from the GT dir is not detected; its rows persist until re-ingested with an empty file.
  • Frame spine first: a run that produces detections requires the (game_id, frame_index) frame rows to exist (FK). Frame extraction is the first writer; analysis stages update/insert against existing frames.
  • Atomic partition writes: write to a temp path, fsync, rename. A crashed run leaves no half-written partition visible.

docs.title: 7.1 Keys as implemented, and what is not in the store
docs.text:
Added 2026-11-08 from a review of main @ 26d2506. Who this is for: anyone ingesting into the store, joining to it, or asking why a label is missing from an export.

flowchart LR
  classDef code fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111
  classDef data fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111
  classDef missing fill:#ffedd5,stroke:#ea580c,stroke-dasharray:5 3,color:#111
  classDef dead fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#111

  GAME[("game<br/>key: game_id<br/>a clip stem in practice")]:::data
  FRAME[("frame<br/>key: game_id, frame_index<br/>frame_uri often NULL")]:::data
  RUN[("run<br/>key: run_id")]:::data
  DET[("detection<br/>key: game_id, source, run_id,<br/>frame_index, detection_id")]:::data
  TM[("track_meta<br/>key: game_id, source, run_id, track_id<br/>0 rows, no writer")]:::dead
  VIEW["detections_enriched<br/>adds the canonical flag"]:::code
  EXP["export_training_dataset<br/>WHERE canonical"]:::code
  GTI["ingest_gt<br/>run_id gt_import_PROVENANCE"]:::code
  RBI["Roboflow importer<br/>run_id roboflow_vN"]:::code
  MISSING["Not in the store<br/>see the table below"]:::missing

  GAME -- "game_id" --> FRAME
  FRAME -- "game_id, frame_index" --> DET
  RUN -- "run_id" --> DET
  GAME --> TM
  GTI --> DET
  RBI --> DET
  DET --> VIEW --> EXP
  MISSING -.-> DET

Legend: grey is a table, blue is code in git, orange dashed is data that is not in the store, red is a table nothing writes. The diagram shows that a detection is found by (game_id, frame_index) plus a source and a run, that two importers feed it, and that only the canonical rows reach the export.

How the keys are built in practice:

Key part Built from Consequence game_id The clip stem for GT imports (ingest_gt.py:202), the frame-file stem for Roboflow Clips are linked to videos only by name. game.source_video_uri and match_date are NULL, and frame_uri is NULL in the samples looked at. run_id gt_import_<provenance> is hard-coded (ingest_gt.py:197, 253); Roboflow uses roboflow_v<N> Two machines' sidecars for the same clip share a run and overwrite each other. detection_id Position within (frame, source) (ingest_gt.py:199, importers.py:228) Deleting or reordering a box repoints old ids. The content-hash version in identity/stable_id.py is never called. Upsert ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on the full key (store.py:197-220) Re-ingest never deletes, so an old row stays next to a corrected one (T-04).

What is and is not in the newest copy of the store (2026-08-04, measured 2026-11-08):

In the store Not in the store Roboflow v3 (hand_label, run roboflow_v3) Roboflow v11 GT sidecars, top-level files only: runs gt_import_labeller, gt_import_vittrack, gt_import_yolo The six GT files added later and the 2026-09-24 Ball Check corrections 26,364 detections, 1,869 frames, 34 of 41 games The 2.77M machine labels and the 357k ball candidates Ball Check verdicts (ingest_gt never reads ball_checks/) Tracklets, link proposals, identity labels (track_meta has 0 rows) Embeddings, pitch segmentation, calibration, broadcast flags: the columns exist, but no importer in the repo fills them (data not checked)

The newest copy is stale and local only. Refreshing it is T-07.

docs.title: 8. Tracking integration (forward-compatible)
docs.text:
Tracking reuses the detection table rather than a parallel tracks.parquet:

  • A tracker run writes detection rows with source = tracker name (e.g. bytetrack), track_id set, is_interpolated flagged for Kalman fills.
  • It may either (a) emit fresh detection rows, or (b) be modelled as a run that copies a detector run's boxes and adds track_id. (a) is cleaner for provenance and keeps tracker output independently rewritable.
  • Per-track summary + identity lands in track_meta. Lifecycle, ID allocation, and re-ID semantics are unchanged from player_tracking_format.md §5 — this doc only changes where the rows live (the store, not a per-match sidecar).

docs.title: 9. Relationship to existing docs (what this changes)
docs.text:
Existing artifact Fate under this design frames.parquet (pipelines.md) → frame table ocr_clock.parquet → frame.game_time_s / half columns detections.parquet → detection table (now multi-source) geometry.parquet → calibration table (§3.7) embeddings.parquet → frame_embedding table (§4) tracks.parquet + tracks_meta.json (player_tracking_format.md) → detection (track_id) + track_meta table GameMetadata block in sidecar → game table MatchExporter (output.md) reads the store instead of N parquet files; JSON/CSV/FiftyOne exporters become views/queries over the store

player_tracking_format.md stays valid as the track lifecycle & semantics spec; this doc is the physical storage spec it plugs into. pipelines.md §Data model should be updated to point here (follow-up).

docs.title: 10. Why this over the alternatives
docs.text: Option Verdict Why DuckDB file + partitioned Parquet, normalised by grain (this design) Chosen Single portable store, real keys/upsert, multi-source clean, DVC-friendly, schema-evolvable One literal wide table No Grain mismatch → array columns or massive duplication; can't rewrite one source cheaply Per-stage Parquet files joined ad-hoc (status quo) No The join glue is exactly what the request wants to eliminate; no enforced keys/idempotency Postgres / a server DB No Adds an always-on service; loses single-file portability and DVC versioning; overkill for a single-writer batch warehouse FiftyOne as canonical No FiftyOne is a consumer; we ingest the store into it, not vice-versa (matches existing stance) SQLite No Row-oriented; poor at the columnar range/aggregate scans (time windows, per-source filters) that dominate here

docs.title: 11. Open questions (file as beads before building)
docs.text:
• Streaming producers. This is batch-on-completion. A live feed wants append-friendly chunk Parquet compacted at end-of-game (same open question as player_tracking_format.md §6). Pick before building a live path.
  • Multiple segmentation runs per frame. Segmentation is still "one final per frame" inlined on frame; promote it to a source-tagged table like detection when a second segmentation model appears. (Calibration already graduated: §3.7.)
  • Geometry predicates. Adopt DuckDB spatial (WKB GEOMETRY for pitch_polygon) so "is this player inside the pitch" is a SQL ST_Contains? Recommended but pulls in the extension.
  • ~~detection_id allocation.~~ Resolved (v1): detection_id is the per-frame object index (0..N-1) and frame_index is part of the PK. This matches how detectors emit, needs no run-global counter, and makes re-ingesting a single frame's detections a clean upsert. A content-hash variant remains an option for non-deterministic detectors but is not needed for the deterministic ingest path.
  • Schema-version enforcement on read. schema_version is recorded but there's no read-side policy (reject / best-effort upgrade). Same gap as noted in player_tracking_format.md §6.
  • Store granularity: per-environment vs per-game. One global feature_store.duckdb for all games, or one per game with a DuckDB ATTACH/UNION overlay? Per-game files are more DVC-friendly and parallel-write-safe; a global view attaches them. Leaning per-game files + global attach view.
  • Embeddings storage. Plain LIST<FLOAT> Parquet vs a real vector index (lancedb / duckdb-vss) once re-ID/search needs ANN. Defer until there's a search workload.

docs.title: 12. Summary
docs.text:
• One store (feature_store.duckdb over partitioned Parquet), normalised by grain: game → frame → detection, plus track_meta and run provenance; embeddings off to the side.
  • The request's "single table" is delivered as the frame_features view (frame ⨝ game) — one wide per-frame table to query — without paying the duplication cost in storage.
  • Multiple detection sources (hand label / SAM 3 / YOLO / trackers) coexist as source + run_id-tagged rows; none overwrites another, eval is a self-join, re-runs are idempotent partition swaps.
  • Pitch segmentation (final polygon + thresholds) and broadcast flags are inlined per-frame with their own model-version provenance; calibration is a source-tagged table (calibration + pitch_keypoint) resolved by the frame_calibration_best view; tracking plugs into detection/track_meta per the existing lifecycle spec.
  • Folds together every previously-scattered Parquet artifact; honours the ContinuousTime / bbox / class-label / track-ID invariants; stays DVC-versioned and schema-evolvable.

docs.title: Full-frame labelling: complete frames, progress, auto-label series
docs.text: Status: Tasks 1-10 implemented and merged 2026-11-19 (PRs #107, #109-#118); the pieces are untested against real models and the real store. Original proposal 2026-11-19. KB relied on: footy-claude-autolabel-loop (Claude verify precision, queue), footy-datasets-and-progress (store, splits, /progress, Prefect nightly), footy-labeller-gotchas (sidecar data loss, _segNNN clips not contiguous). Builds on ball_sampling.md, feature_store.md.

docs.title: Decision 2026-11-21: two detectors (supersedes the single multi-class student)
docs.text:
Decision (user, 2026-11-21): train two separate detectors instead of one multi-class RT-DETR. - Ball detector: ball / in_play_ball / out_of_play_ball. High-resolution or tiled (can run on crops/tiles), its own hard negatives (Ball Check not_ball), evaluated on the ball eval panel. - Player-side detector: player, referee, coach, player_sub, person.

Why: labelling is already split (Ball Check / ball jobs vs Player Check); the ball is tiny and needs different resolution and evaluation; each model gets its own teacher version, targeted queue and eval; the pipeline is easier to label and train. Costs: two inference passes (the ball model can run on crops/tiles); ball false positives lose player context, mitigated by Ball Check hard negatives.

Consequences: 1. frame_complete (both groups complete) stops being the training gate. The ball model trains on frames whose ball state is complete/absent; the player model on frames whose player state is complete/absent. frame_complete / fully_labelled stay as an informational view. Class ids stay frozen (constants.py); the player export simply excludes the ball classes. 2. Progress (/progress/labelling) should show two independent targets: ball-complete and player-complete; "fully labelled" is informational only. 3. Auto-label pipeline (windows, propose, pre-verify, series review, teacher versions, targeting queue; sections 4-4b) runs per group: a ball pipeline and a player pipeline, each with its own teacher version and queue. 4. Eval: the ball eval panel for the ball model; blind hand-labelled heldout frames (the player eval panel, section 4c.6b) for the player model.

Status: | Part | State | |---|---| | Ball-only export (default, no --classes; gate = ball group only; ball classes collapse to one class id 0) | Implemented (scripts/export_training_dataset.py) | | frame_label_state per group, per-group writers, frozen class ids | Implemented | | Player-only export mode (player-group gate, ball classes excluded, frozen ids unchanged) | TODO. Today --classes multi-class export still gates on frame_complete | | /progress/labelling as two independent targets | Implemented 2026-11-21: groups.ball / groups.player (section 3), two sections on /progress, ball and player badges in the clip list | | Per-group auto-label pipeline and per-group teacher versions / queues | TODO. Stages in section 4 are built as one pipeline for both groups | | Ball model training recipe (high-res/tiled) and player model training run | TODO (not covered by this doc) | | Player eval panel (blind heldout frames) | TODO (see 4c.6b) |

Where sections below say "one detector", "multi-class" or that fully labelled frames are the training target, that text is superseded by this decision; it is kept for history and marked inline.

docs.title: 1. Fully labelled frame
docs.text:
A frame is fully labelled when each class group (ball, player) has state complete or absent: - ball: complete = a verified ball box exists; absent = explicit no_ball (sidecar no_ball tag or Ball Check frame verdict). unsure and unreviewed are neither. - player (player, player_sub, referee, coach, person): complete = a human asserted "all visible people are boxed". A zero-person frame is absent.

Storage: explicit table, not a derived view. reviewed boxes prove only that those boxes were checked, never that no other player is missing, so player completeness cannot be derived. Derivation also makes the ball side depend on JSONL verdict logs the store does not hold.

frame_label_state(game_id, frame_index, cls_group, state,  -- complete|absent|partial|unreviewed
                  method, run_id, verified_by, verified_at, PRIMARY KEY(game_id, frame_index, cls_group))
- method: hand_series (accept-all), hand_frame, verdict, offline_audited, sidecar_marker, inferred_gt (rank 0, lowest). - run_id points at the proposing run (provenance). - View frame_complete(game_id, frame_index) = both groups in (complete,absent). Absence of a row means unreviewed. - Writers: labeller flush writes no_ball, plus complete for ball when a human box exists. Ball Check verdicts write ball state. The series review (section 4) writes both groups. Existing GT is NOT back-filled as player-complete, except clips the user flags (--legacy-complete-clips) and the interim inferred_gt rule (section 1b). - Missing label never implies background. Only complete/absent frames reach training. (Superseded 2026-11-21: per group. Ball-model frames need ball complete/absent, player-model frames need player complete/absent; both groups are no longer required.)

docs.title: 1b. Interim rule: inferred player-complete (inferred_gt, user decision 2026-11-23)
docs.text:
Pragmatic override of "existing GT is not assumed player-complete": while full-frame player labelling catches up, a frame that already has

= 1 human box (labeller provenance or human-checked) of a player-side class (player, referee, coach, player_sub, person) and a ball decision (human ball box, or a no_ball mark) gets player complete with method=inferred_gt, verified_by inferred_gt, run_id gt_import_inferred_player_complete. Not marked: players without a ball decision, a ball decision without players, machine-only players, not_broadcast frames, ball/no_ball conflicts. Sparse player labels are likely incomplete, so this is a known approximation.

  • inferred_gt has the lowest precedence (rank 0, below sidecar_marker): any P marker, legacy back-fill, verdict, Player Check or hand label on the frame wins, and removing that stronger row lets the inferred row return on the next ingest.
  • Re-derived on every replace ingest of a clip (delete this method's rows, then upsert): idempotent; a frame whose player boxes vanish loses its row.
  • ON by default in ingest_all (nightly); --no-infer-player-complete disables it and the next ingest purges the rows. OFF by default in ingest_gt (--infer-player-complete).
  • Revert/filter by method: DELETE FROM frame_label_state WHERE method='inferred_gt', or exclude method='inferred_gt' in queries. Progress shows it under by_method and in the other tier (not gold or silver).
  • Existing stores are migrated on open (the method CHECK constraint is rebuilt once).

docs.title: 2. Exporter (scripts/export_training_dataset.py)
docs.text:
• (Superseded 2026-11-21: the gate is per model group, not frame_complete; ball-only mode already does this, player-only mode is TODO.) Query joins frame_complete; only those frames are emitted. Frames with partial state are skipped, with a manifest count.
  • Positives are canonical boxes of reviewed sources. Negatives: ball absent frames are written with an empty ball label set. Ball Check not_ball boxes are kept as hard_negatives.json (and optional empty-region crops), never as a class.
  • Class ids are stable: a fixed list in constants.py (player=0, ball=1, referee=2, ...) replaces sorted-label ids. The manifest records the list, and a test fails if ids change.
  • --sources defaults to hand_label,reviewed (machine boxes enter only via reviewed=true). --sources all remains explicit.
  • Train/val comes from splits.split_of only (existing guard test applies). Manifest reports frames by state, split and class.

docs.title: 3. Progress view
docs.text: GET /progress/labelling presents two independent targets, Ball (ball, in_play_ball, out_of_play_ball) and Player-side (player, referee, coach, player_sub, person); their counts are never pooled. Response: groups.<ball|player> = {label, classes, totals, by_split, by_method, tiers, clips}, where totals, each by_split[split] and each per-clip row hold frames, complete, absent, partial, unreviewed (a frame with no row for the group is unreviewed), labelled (= complete + absent), clip_frames and pct_labelled (of the clip's video frames when known, else of frames with a state row). by_split keys are train / eval_in_match / eval_heldout_match; per-clip clips are sorted least-labelled first per group. The legacy keys stay for compatibility: per clip and in totals, frames, ball_labelled, player_labelled, fully_labelled (both groups; informational only, not a training gate), partial, plus top-level by_method, by_split, tiers, teacher_versions; each legacy clip row also carries groups.<g> counts. It reads the store (not the JSONL), so it can run on the mini. The "Labelling coverage" table on /progress is two sections (Ball, Player-side) plus an informational fully-labelled line, and the clip list shows separate ball and player badges (the old _clip_completion tick remains a sidecar heuristic, not verified progress).

docs.title: 4. Auto-label pipeline (priority)
docs.text:
(2026-11-21: runs per group, one ball pipeline and one player pipeline, each with its own teacher version and queue. The text below describes the combined pipeline as built and is otherwise unchanged. TODO for the split.)

Stages, each writing a run row and resumable:

  1. Select windows (mini CPU). Contiguous windows of N=250 frames (5 s at 50 fps) taken inside one _segNNN clip, since segments cannot be chained. Choose train-match clips only, balanced across matches, favouring windows with lowest ball-tracker agreement or fewest labels. Heldout matches are excluded (rule zero in ball_sampling.md). Output: windows.json.
  2. Propose (desktop GPU, Prefect gpu pool, existing stage-inputs then GPU then push-outputs chain). Per frame: RT-DETR for players and referees and ball candidates (its player mAP50 of ~0.98 comes from the original one-game dataset and says nothing about other matches, camera angles or kits, so player proposals are treated as unmeasured), then ROI-YOLO or ViTTrack bidirectionally for the ball (forward/backward disagreement is a flag). SAM3 is used only to fill missing person boxes when the detector count disagrees with its neighbours. Output: proposals/<window>.npz plus ingest as detection rows (source=yolo|vittrack|sam3, reviewed=false, needs_review=true).
  3. Pre-verify (mini, Claude verify v2.2 as in the queue). Ball verdict on the tracker candidate (precision 61/62 held-out). Mark frames auto_ok when the track is smooth, forward and backward trackers agree, the verdict is ball at high confidence, and the person count is stable within the window. Everything else is flagged. The auto-accept threshold must come from audits (target 0.95; 0.8 measured at about 65%).
  4. Review (human, phone/desktop). A new window card shows a 5 s contact strip of every k-th frame with boxes overlaid, with "Accept all", and per-frame exceptions: tap a frame, then one of: fix box (existing /review/correct), ball not_ball, ball absent, "players incomplete" (frame is demoted to partial). Flagged frames come first, using the Viterbi-margin order. 10% of auto_ok frames are shown blind as an audit. If exceptions exceed 10%, the window is rejected and returns to stage 2 with the corrected anchors as re-track seeds.
  5. Commit (mini). Accept writes reviewed=true on accepted machine boxes, frame_label_state rows with method=hand_series and run_id of the proposing run, and the window's audit stats. Boxes the human touched become hand_label. Windows with every frame complete are registered as a series (series(game_id,start,end,run_id)), which the exporter can use for temporal training.

GPU: stage 2 only. CPU: selection, verify, commit, export. The nightly footy-nightly-datasets ingests, then bumps dataset versions.

docs.title: Ball anchor iteration (design 2026-11-21)
docs.text: A confirmed ball can anchor a forward/backward search that proposes the next most likely ball cards, checked again in Ball Check, until every selected frame is terminal (ball, no_ball, unusable, explicit deferred). The same flow serves the train windows and the ball eval panel (anchoring bias accepted); a frame with no confirmed candidate is never defaulted to no_ball but goes to an explicit full-frame human check (laptop job mode or a phone full-frame card), which is how false negatives are found. Train and eval frame sets stay disjoint by split_of, eval labels never feed training, anchors propagate only inside one job's selected set, and every card/label records the generator/teacher version. See ball_anchor_iteration.md (design only, nothing built; includes the orchestration/sync rules between labeller jobs, Prefect flows and frame_label_state).

docs.title: 4b. Offline teacher pipeline (framing for sections 4 and 5)
docs.text:
Two separate systems, deliberately: - Offline pipeline ("teacher"): a versioned set of heavy models with no real-time limit that auto-labels training data. Members: large detector at high resolution plus test-time augmentation, bidirectional ROI-YOLO/ViTTrack ball tracking, SAM3 for missing people, temporal smoothing/Viterbi, Claude verify. It is a pipeline version (offline_vN), recorded on every label it writes (source=offline_vN, run_id). - Online detector ("student"): the RT-DETR that must run fast. (Superseded 2026-11-21: there are two students, a ball detector and a player-side detector, each trained on frames complete for its own group.) Originally: one model trained only on fully labelled frames (section 1).

Label tiers: gold = human-verified (hand label, accept-all review, exceptions); silver = teacher output that passed the auto_ok rules and the blind audit (method=offline_audited). Each student trains on gold + silver of its own group. The teacher is scored, and the student evaluated, on gold only (held-out matches, never silver).

Human labelling is targeted, not uniform. Every labelling request must be one of: 1. Improves the teacher: frames where teacher members disagree (forward/backward tracker, detector vs SAM3 person count), flagged frames, audit failures, and hard cases it gets wrong (small/occluded ball, crowded boxes). Corrected frames become teacher training data and gold eval. 2. Becomes student training data: windows reviewed as series, where the teacher already does well and human time confirms it. 3. Measures the teacher: the gold eval set and the 10% blind audit, which set the auto_ok precision. Anything that is none of these (random frames, clips already well covered) is not queued. The review queue is ranked by expected teacher gain (disagreement, margin), and the progress view reports gold vs silver counts per teacher version and the teacher's measured precision/recall on gold.

Loop: label targeted frames -> retrain/tune teacher -> teacher v(N+1) relabels everything, audit pass rate rises -> more silver per human minute -> retrain student.

docs.title: 4c. Player Check (verifying player labels, especially clusters)
docs.text:
Ball Check verifies one box per card. Player errors are different: a missed person, a duplicate box on one person, one box over two overlapping people, a wrong class (player vs referee), a ghost box. Almost all of them occur where boxes overlap. So the unit is the cluster, not the box, and the question is "does each person here have exactly one box?"

Box rule (must be fixed before labelling): box the visible extent of each person (modal box), one box per person, even when boxes overlap heavily. Do not box a person under 12 px tall.

1. Triage by geometry (mini CPU, no model). For each frame in a window, group boxes into clusters: connected components where IoU > 0.2 or the centre distance is under 0.6 of the mean box width. Isolated boxes with a stable track and high confidence are auto_ok. Clusters, unstable tracks and frames with disagreement go to a human.

2. Count over time. Track each cluster through the window. The number of people in a cluster changes only when someone enters or leaves it, so a count that flickers (3, 3, 2, 3) points at the bad frame. The reviewer sees a short strip of 3-5 frames of the cluster with a count timeline and resolves only the change points; "count is N for frames a-b" is one tap and fixes all frames in that run.

3. Independent count (flag only). Re-run the cluster crop upscaled 2x with a different model (SAM3 or a pose/head detector) and compare person counts. A disagreement flags the cluster. This is a flag, never an auto-accept, until audits show it is reliable (same rule as Claude verify).

4. Card types. - Cluster card (priority): a zoomed crop of the cluster, boxes in distinct colours with index numbers, overlapping boxes drawn with offset outlines so each stays visible, the count timeline underneath. Swipe right = every person has exactly one box; swipe left = opens fix mode: tap an unboxed person to add, tap a box to delete (duplicate/ghost), drag a line across a box to split a merged pair, tap the class chip to change player/referee. - Frame sweep card: whole frame, boxes shown, one question "anyone unboxed?" with tap-to-place. Catches small far players and people at the frame edge that triage never sees. - Audit card: 10% of auto_ok frames, shown blind (no boxes) for full relabelling. The disagreement with the machine boxes gives the miss rate per overlap bucket (isolated / touching / heavy overlap) and sets the auto-accept threshold.

5. Model-assisted check (optional, gated). Claude gets the numbered cluster crop and lists persons without a box, boxes covering two people, and duplicates. Used first only to order the queue; promoted to a filter if its precision on audited clusters reaches the 0.95 target.

6. State. One row per cluster check: player_check(game_id, frame_index, cluster_id, bbox, n_boxes, verdict, asserted_count, method, verified_by, verified_at). A frame's player state is complete when every cluster is verified and its sweep is done; any flagged or fixed-but-unreverified cluster makes it partial. Fixes write hand_frame boxes (gold).

6b. No trust in the 0.98. The detector's player mAP50 (0.98-0.99) was measured on the original one-game dataset, so it is in-distribution and does not predict performance on new matches (the same gap seen for the ball: 0.92 in-distribution vs 0.49 on held-out clips). Consequences: - Nothing is auto-accepted for players on the strength of detector confidence alone. The auto_ok rule for isolated boxes starts at "audit everything" and relaxes per match only once that match's blind audits show a low miss rate. - Player miss rate and box quality are reported per match and per overlap bucket, never pooled into one number. - A player eval panel is needed beside the ball one (under the 2026-11-21 decision it is the eval for the player-side detector; TODO): fully hand-labelled frames (blind, all people boxed) from the heldout matches, sampled with logged inclusion probabilities, used to score the teacher and the student. Player mAP/recall/precision on this panel is the headline; the one-game number is retired from reporting. - Player audits from train matches measure drift across kits, camera zoom and crowd density, and decide how much human review each new match needs.

7. Cost target. Under 3 s for a clean cluster card (swipe), under 15 s with fixes. Report cost per card type on /progress alongside the miss rate per overlap bucket.

docs.title: 5. Task breakdown (priority order)
docs.text:
Additions from 4b: Task 1's method also takes offline_audited plus a teacher_version column; Task 4 emits disagreement scores used by the queue ranking; new Task 9 below.

  1. State table + ingest writers. Files: feature_store/schema.py, store.py, ingest_gt.py, tests. Writes no_ball/ball-box/verdict state. Accept: re-ingest is idempotent; no_ball gives ball absent; unsure stays unreviewed. Deps: none.
  2. Window selector + propose flow. Files: new autolabel/windows.py, autolabel/propose.py, a Prefect entry in the jobs repo. Accept: windows stay inside a segment and never touch heldout; proposals ingest as unreviewed rows. Deps: 1 (for exclusion of already-complete frames).
  3. Series review API and card. Files: labeller/series_review.py, web/series.html, server.py router. Accept: accept-all writes complete state; one exception demotes only that frame; the reject path re-queues. Deps: 1.
  4. Pre-verify + auto_ok rules + audit sampler. Files: autolabel/preverify.py, tests with fixture tracks. Accept: flagged ordering is deterministic; audit fraction is 10% blind. Deps: 2.
  5. Exporter filter. Files: scripts/export_training_dataset.py, constants.py, tests. Accept (original; per-group gate after 2026-11-21, player-only mode TODO): no partial frame appears; negatives present; class ids frozen; default sources. Deps: 1.
  6. Progress endpoint and UI. Files: labeller/progress.py, web/progress*, clip list badge. Accept: counts equal a fixture store; ball-only clip counts as not fully labelled. Deps: 1.
  7. Series registry + temporal export option. Files: schema.py, exporter. Accept: contiguous series exported in frame order. Deps: 3, 5.

  8. Legacy backfill flag. Files: ingest_gt.py CLI. Accept: only named clips become player-complete. Deps: 1.

  9. Teacher versioning, gold eval and targeting queue. Files: autolabel/teacher.py (pipeline config + version), autolabel/queue.py (rank by disagreement/margin, reject untargeted requests), ball_eval/ gold scoring, progress additions. Accept: every offline label carries teacher_version; scoring a teacher version on the gold set outputs precision/recall; queue never returns frames from non-train matches or already-gold frames. Deps: 1, 4.

  10. Player Check. Files: autolabel/clusters.py (geometric clustering, count timeline, triage), labeller/player_check.py + web/player_check.html (cluster / sweep / audit cards, fix mode), player_check table in feature_store/schema.py, tests. Accept: isolated stable boxes are auto_ok; overlapping boxes form one cluster; a count flicker is flagged; "count is N for a-b" resolves the run; a fixed cluster writes hand_frame boxes; frame player state is complete only when all clusters and the sweep are verified. Deps: 1, 2.

docs.title: 6. Open questions
docs.text:
1. Is a person visible but too small or occluded to box "complete"? Proposal: yes if no human would box it, but we need a minimum size (suggest 12 px height).
  2. Should a legacy clip with hand ball marks plus player marks (e.g. the arsenal_* clips) be treated as player-complete without recheck?
  3. Window length and review budget: is 5 s windows with about 10% exceptions an acceptable human cost, or should reviews be per-clip-segment?

docs.title: Input Stage — Live Stream Completion
docs.text:
Status: DRAFT · Issue: footy_track-yjd

This document specifies the unfinished half of the Input stage (§2.1 of system_design.md): the live-stream consumer. File-based extraction already exists in scripts/extract_frames.py.

docs.title: 1. Stage in §2 of system_design.md
docs.text:
This is the live-stream branch of Input (§2.1). The contract is unchanged from that section:

  • Input — a stream URL (HLS / RTMP / RTSP / WebRTC).
  • Output — (frame_image: np.ndarray, GameTime, video_metadata) per decoded frame. GameTime is the canonical wall-clock; conversion to ContinuousTime happens at the input boundary per timings.md.

docs.title: 2. Module interface
docs.text:
# src/footy_track/input/streams.py

class FrameSource(Protocol):
    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[FrameRecord]: ...

class FileFrameSource(FrameSource):
    def __init__(self, video_path: Path, kickoff: GameTime): ...

class LiveStreamFrameSource(FrameSource):
    def __init__(
        self,
        url: str,
        kickoff: GameTime,
        reconnect: ReconnectPolicy = ReconnectPolicy.exponential_backoff(),
    ): ...

FrameRecord is a Pydantic model: (frame: np.ndarray, game_time: GameTime, continuous_time: float, source_metadata: dict). The two sources are interchangeable from a consumer's point of view — downstream stages (Broadcast Classifier, Calibration, Detection) only ever see FrameRecord.

docs.title: 3. Backing library
docs.text:
Default backend: PyAV (libav bindings). Rationale:

  • Handles HLS / RTMP / RTSP without shelling out to ffmpeg.
  • Exposes per-packet PTS so we can derive frame timestamps without guessing from frame indices.
  • Already a transitive dep of common video tooling.

Fallback: shelling out to ffmpeg with frame-by-frame stdout piping is acceptable for protocols PyAV cannot handle; this should be hidden behind the same FrameSource interface.

docs.title: 4. Reconnection and gaps
docs.text:
A live source can drop. The consumer must:

  1. Reconnect with exponential backoff (default 1s → 30s, capped).
  2. Emit a sentinel FrameRecord with source_metadata.gap=True and no frame payload, so downstream stages can record the gap rather than silently lose time.
  3. Resume ContinuousTime from wall-clock — not frame index — so the gap is reflected in the timestamps.

docs.title: 5. Cross-stage invariants honoured
docs.text:
• ContinuousTime is computed once, at the input boundary, from GameTime. See timings.md.
  • The input emits every decoded frame; downstream sampling is the consumer's choice.
  • Gaps are recorded, not silently dropped (mirrors the rule for non-broadcast frames in §2.2).

docs.title: 6. Out of scope
docs.text:
• Audio extraction.
  • Multi-camera ingest (single-source v1).
  • Authenticated streams (handled by the URL, not by this module).

docs.title: Labeller — Deep Review (Implementation + Design)
docs.text:
Bead: ft-31z · Date: 2026-06-21 · Reviewer: polecat ruby Scope: src/footy_track/labeller/ (app.py, server.py, video_utils.py, web/index.html, _canvas_compat.py) plus how the GT-marking / bake-off and the SAM3 Run-loop integrate. All citations are file:line against the branch at review time.

Headline: there are two complete, divergent labeller front-ends in the tree (a Streamlit app and a FastAPI+Konva web app) sharing one backend engine (video_utils.py). The web app is the intended go-forward UX for mark-once GT + bake-off, but it is missing an export path — it can mark and propagate but cannot save the result. That is the single blocker for marking clips. There is no ball_eval/ module yet (the bead assumed one exists); the bake-off harness is not present in this tree.

docs.title: 1. Component map & data flow
docs.text:
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │  video_utils.py  (shared backend)        │
                         │  • Sam3VideoLabeller  – SAM3 propagation │
                         │  • BackgroundLabeller – daemon-thread    │
                         │       run/pause/restart + anomaly stop   │
                         │  • yolo_seed_objects  – YOLO seeding      │
                         │  • export_frames_json – disk export      │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┘
                                         │              │
              ┌──────────────────────────┘              └──────────────────────┐
              │                                                                 │
   ┌──────────▼───────────┐                              ┌─────────────────────▼──────────┐
   │ app.py (Streamlit)    │                              │ server.py (FastAPI)             │
   │ • server-side state in │                              │ • Session.timeline = single     │
   │   st.session_state     │                              │   source of truth (per-frame)   │
   │ • st_canvas drawing    │                              │ • provenance tags PROV_*        │
   │ • _canvas_compat shim   │                              │ • HTTP + WebSocket              │
   │ • export via Save JSON │   ◄── only this side exports │ • web/index.html (Konva canvas) │
   └────────────────────────┘                              └─────────────────────────────────┘
        run_labeller.py entrypoint                          uvicorn ...server:app  (no entrypoint script)

Pipeline position. The labeller produces FrameDetections JSON whose uri stem encodes the absolute frame index (<stem>_frame_000123). feature_store ingests exactly this format: importers.parse_labeller_uri (feature_store/importers.py:93) parses <clip>_frame_<idx> back out, and import_labeller_json tags rows source='sam3'. So the contract between labeller output and the feature store is the export_frames_json file shape, not any in-memory object — which is why the web app's missing export is fatal to the downstream flow.

docs.title: Module responsibilities
docs.text: File Responsibility LOC video_utils.py SAM3 propagation engine, threaded run loop, YOLO seeding, anomaly heuristic, JSON export 830 app.py Streamlit UI — full interaction, state in st.session_state 911 server.py FastAPI — authoritative timeline w/ provenance, run/pause/restart over WS 406 web/index.html Konva-based browser client for server.py 428 _canvas_compat.py Monkeypatch restoring image_to_url for st_canvas on Streamlit ≥1.40 (Streamlit-only) 44

docs.title: 2a. The two front-ends are the central design problem
docs.text:
app.py and server.py are two ~full implementations of the same feature. They share video_utils.py but duplicate everything above it and embody two different state models:

  • app.py keeps the working set in st.session_state.objects and re-derives view mode every rerun (app.py:331-336). State is implicit, scattered across ~14 session keys (app.py:69-93), and there is no single per-frame timeline — corrections live only in BackgroundLabeller.frames plus transient session state.
  • server.py introduces the right abstraction the Streamlit app lacks: a single authoritative Session.timeline[idx] of ObjectDetection with provenance (PROV_LABELLER/PROV_YOLO/PROV_SAM3, server.py:44-47). Labeller boxes are ground truth and survive re-propagation via the merge rule in merge_propagated (server.py:106-113). This is a cleaner, more correct model than the Streamlit app's.

Recommendation: treat server.py + web/ as the go-forward labeller and deprecate/retire app.py once export parity exists (§5, P0/P1). Maintaining both doubles the surface for the morning's marking work and they have already drifted (see consistency bugs below). Do not invest further in app.py.

docs.title: 2b. Duplicated logic across the two front-ends
docs.text: yolo_seed_objects and _nms_filter exist twice, verbatim: video_utils.py:743-808 (used by server.py) and app.py:96-160 (app.py-local copies). The app.py copies should be deleted and the video_utils.py versions imported (app.py already imports other helpers from video_utils). Pure dead duplication; risk of one drifting from the other.

docs.title: 2c. video_utils.py engine — solid, with sharp edges
docs.text:
The engine is the strongest part of the labeller:

  • Hot-predictor cache (get_cached_predictor, video_utils.py:146-188) keeps SAM3 weights + compiled kernels resident across pause/restart — this is what makes the correct-and-restart loop usable. Good.
  • Restart-mid-clip via temp video (iter_frames_from, video_utils.py:416-490): because SAM3VideoPredictor seeds tracks from the first frame it sees, restarting at frame N writes frames [N, end] to a temp .mp4 and re-streams. Clever and necessary given the predictor's statefulness.
  • Seed frame is ground truth (_seed_frame_detections, video_utils.py:492-517; offset == 0 branch at :477): the user's exact boxes are emitted verbatim rather than SAM3's re-segmentation. Correct call — prevents a corrected box from being mangled on restart.

Sharp edges:

  • Object-index → label mapping is positional and fragile (_result_to_frame, video_utils.py:519-554). SAM3 only preserves object order, so label assignment is self.objects[obj_idx].label. If SAM3 drops a track or returns masks in a different count/order than seeds, labels silently shift ("unknown" fallback at :535). For the ball specifically — the one object most likely to be lost — a dropped ball track means every subsequent object inherits the wrong label. This is a real correctness risk for GT.
  • Temp-clip rewrite is lossy and slow (video_utils.py:449-465): re-encodes with mp4v at the source fps, doubling I/O and risking codec drift vs the original frames. For long clips this is the dominant cost on every restart.
  • Anomaly heuristic is plausible but untuned (_track_anomaly_reason, video_utils.py:683-728): nearest-same-label matching with a 40%-of-diagonal jump threshold and 8× area ratio. No tests; thresholds are magic numbers. It matches by label not track identity, so with two players it can match the wrong pair and false-positive. Fine as a "stop and let me look" aid, not something to trust silently.

docs.title: 2d. Threading / async correctness in server.py
docs.text:
• Session.timeline is guarded by _tl_lock (server.py:67) — good. But BackgroundLabeller exposes running, last_completed_frame, anomaly_frame as plain attributes read from the asyncio loop (_stream_frames, server.py:298-337) while written under self._lock in the worker thread (video_utils.py:652-676). These cross-thread reads are unsynchronized. In CPython they won't corrupt, but anomaly_frame is both read and cleared from the async side (server.py:328) — a genuine race with the worker setting it (video_utils.py:666-668). Low-probability, but it can drop or double-fire an anomaly pause.
  • SESSION is a single module-global (server.py:147). The server is strictly single-session / single-user. Two browser tabs share one timeline and one bg; the second load silently wipes the first. Acceptable for solo morning marking, but must be stated, and the WS handler assumes it (server.py:343 captures bg = SESSION.bg then re-reads SESSION.bg later — inconsistent).

docs.title: 2e. Frame access pattern is O(n) seeks everywhere
docs.text: Every frame fetch opens a fresh cv2.VideoCapture, seeks, reads one frame, and releases — frame_jpeg (server.py:132-144), and in app.py at :405-408, :427-431, :485-488, :730-732. On a long clip, scrubbing is a storm of open/seek/release. video_utils.py has no frame cache. For the morning's UX (scrub back to fix a box, scrub forward) this will feel sluggish. A small LRU frame cache in the Session (web) would help most.

docs.title: 3. Bug / gap register (ordered by impact on "marking clips in the morning")
🔴 B1 — Web labeller cannot export (BLOCKER)
docs.text: server.py has no save/export endpoint. The timeline is never written to disk; export_frames_json (video_utils.py:811-817) is only wired into app.py (app.py:743-745). A user can mark + propagate in the browser and then lose everything — there is no path from Session.timeline to the FrameDetections JSON that feature_store ingests. Without this, the web app produces no GT. Must fix before marking.

docs.title: 🔴 B2 — Web default-model caption contradicts the actual default
docs.text: web/index.html:54 tells the user the default is sam3.1_multiplex.pt. The backend default is sam3.pt, and _default_model_uri (video_utils.py:100-132) explicitly documents that sam3.1_multiplex.pt returns whole-frame masks for every object on this footage and is deliberately NOT used. A user trusting the caption and typing that checkpoint gets garbage GT. Fix the caption text.

docs.title: 🟠 B3 — Hardcoded class list in JS can drift from DETECTION_CLASSES
docs.text: web/index.html:101 hardcodes CLASSES = [...] and :102-103 hardcodes COLORS. The source of truth is schema.DETECTION_CLASSES (schema.py:25-34) and detectors.utils.color_map. They currently match, but any class change updates Python and silently leaves the JS stale → boxes drawn with the wrong class/colour, corrupting GT labels. Serve the class+colour list from an endpoint (/classes) instead of duplicating it.

docs.title: 🟠 B4 — idle_results save-on-leave only triggers if mode is set, but it never is on Run-completion-then-edit
docs.text: In web/index.html, saveCurrentEdits (:306-311) persists edits when mode==="paused"||mode==="idle_results". After a run completes, uiIdle() sets mode="idle_results" (:370) — good. But the seed frame path: on first load mode="idle" (:280), and autodetect draws editable boxes; if the user edits those frame-0 boxes and immediately scrubs, saveCurrentEdits does nothing (mode is "idle", not in the allowed set), so the edit is lost until they hit Run (which calls commitCanvasTo). Subtle data-loss footgun during seeding. Either include "idle" or persist on every box change.

docs.title: 🟠 B5 — Positional label shift on dropped SAM3 tracks (see §2c)
docs.text: video_utils.py:530-536. If SAM3 returns fewer masks than seeds, the mask→label zip misaligns and downstream labels are wrong with no warning. Needs SAM3 to return per-object IDs, or a guard that pauses when mask count ≠ seed count.

docs.title: 🟡 B6 — Anomaly anomaly_frame cross-thread race (see §2d)
docs.text: server.py:320-328 vs video_utils.py:666-668. Read+clear of anomaly_frame from the async loop without the worker's lock.

docs.title: 🟡 B7 — Streamlit app: _load_frame_objects reads completed captured once per run
docs.text: app.py:353-361 closes over completed (app.py:310) computed at the top of main(). During a paused scrub the list is fixed for that run, which is fine, but the prev/next handlers (:557-572) call it after st.rerun() boundaries — behaviour depends on rerun timing. Works today; fragile.

docs.title: 🟡 B8 — _canvas_compat is Streamlit-only debt
docs.text: _canvas_compat.py exists solely to keep st_canvas alive on modern Streamlit. If app.py is retired (§2a) this whole shim + the streamlit-drawable-canvas dependency can go. Tracked as cleanup.

docs.title: 🟡 B9 — No tests anywhere in labeller/
docs.text: No test file exercises Sam3VideoLabeller, the anomaly heuristic, the merge rule, or export_frames_json. The merge rule (merge_propagated) and _track_anomaly_reason are pure functions and trivially unit-testable; they should be, given GT correctness rides on them.

docs.title: 4. Where GT-marking + the 4 bake-off methods plug in
docs.text:
The bead assumes a ball_eval/ module (GT marking + bake-off harness). It does not exist in this tree — find src -iname '*ball*' -o -iname '*eval*' returns nothing, and there are no references to ball_eval/bake-off anywhere in src or docs. So this section is about where the seams are for that work, not a review of existing code.

Mark-once GT is well-served by server.py's provenance model: a box tagged PROV_LABELLER is ground truth and is preserved across re-propagation (merge_propagated, server.py:106-113). The natural GT artifact is the Session.timeline filtered to model == PROV_LABELLER. But (B1) there is no endpoint to emit it. The first bake-off prerequisite is therefore an export endpoint that writes the timeline (or just the labeller-provenance boxes) as FrameDetections JSON.

The 4 bake-off methods (detection/tracking variants competing against GT) would plug in at the /autodetect seam (server.py:212-251) — today that seam hardcodes a single YOLO detector via yolo_seed_objects. To bake off N methods you need: (a) a method registry, (b) per-method runs against the same frames, (c) a metric vs the PROV_LABELLER GT. None of that scaffolding exists yet. The cleanest insertion is a new ball_eval/ module that consumes the exported GT JSON + each method's output and computes IoU/precision-style metrics — keeping it out of the labeller server (which should stay a marking tool).

docs.title: 5. Consistency check
docs.text: Concern Status ObjectDetection schema (schema.py:57-65) ↔ web wire format ✅ server maps model→source over the wire (server.py:173-186) and back (:155-170); normalized xywh both sides. Consistent. DETECTION_CLASSES ↔ JS CLASSES ⚠️ duplicated, currently aligned (B3). color_map ↔ JS COLORS ⚠️ duplicated, currently aligned (B3). Frame-index encoding ↔ feature-store importer ✅ <stem>_frame_<idx> written by video_utils.py:498,521 and parsed by importers.parse_labeller_uri (importers.py:93). Time conventions (ContinuousTime/GameTime) ➖ labeller works in raw frame indices only; no GameTime mapping. Fine for GT marking, but the exported JSON has no period/clock info — downstream must derive it. Worth noting for the broadcast→pitch→tagging vision. provenance (PROV_*) ↔ ObjectDetection.model ✅ provenance is stored in the model field (server.py:56, :167). Slight semantic overload — model doubles as "which model produced this" and "is this ground truth" — but documented.

docs.title: 6. Recommendations (prioritised — each a candidate bead)
docs.text:
# Priority Recommendation Why R1 P0 Add a /session/export endpoint to server.py that writes Session.timeline via export_frames_json B1 — unblocks all GT marking; nothing downstream works without it R2 P0 Fix web/index.html:54 default-model caption (sam3.1_multiplex.pt → sam3.pt) B2 — one-line fix preventing whole-frame-mask garbage GT R3 P1 Decide the canonical front-end; deprecate app.py (Streamlit) in favour of server.py+web/ §2a — stop maintaining two drifting UIs before marking begins R4 P1 Serve classes+colours from a /classes endpoint; delete JS duplication B3 — prevents silent label/colour corruption R5 P1 Persist seeding-mode edits in web (include "idle" in saveCurrentEdits or save-on-change) B4 — data-loss footgun during marking R6 P2 Guard _result_to_frame when SAM3 mask count ≠ seed count (pause + warn instead of silent label shift) B5 — protects GT label integrity R7 P2 Add unit tests for merge_propagated, _track_anomaly_reason, export_frames_json B9 — GT correctness rides on these pure functions R8 P2 Add an LRU frame cache in Session to make scrubbing responsive §2e — UX during correct-and-restart R9 P2 If app.py retired: delete _canvas_compat.py, the duplicated yolo_seed_objects/_nms_filter, and drop streamlit-drawable-canvas B8, §2b — dead-code removal R10 P3 Scaffold ball_eval/: consume exported GT JSON + N method outputs, compute IoU/precision metrics; register methods at the /autodetect seam §4 — the actual bake-off, after R1 lands R11 P3 Synchronize cross-thread reads of BackgroundLabeller anomaly state B6 — correctness hardening

If only two things ship before the morning's marking: R1 and R2. They are the difference between "can produce ground truth" and "cannot."

docs.title: Output Stage — Design
docs.text:
Status: DRAFT · Issue: footy_track-yjd

This document specifies the Output stage (§2.7 of system_design.md) — the serialisation layer that fans out joined per-stage records to consumers.

The canonical Parquet store for tracks is already specified in player_tracking_format.md. This doc covers the parts that are still planned: per-stage Parquet artifacts, JSON / CSV exporters, and the FiftyOne integration.

docs.title: 1. Stage in §2 of system_design.md
docs.text:
This is the Output stage (§2.7). It consumes:

  • tracks.parquet + tracks_meta.json (from §2.5).
  • Per-stage parquet artifacts (detections.parquet, geometry.parquet, ocr_clock.parquet, frames.parquet, embeddings.parquet) per pipelines.md §Data model.
  • (When 2D Projection lands) pitch_positions.parquet.

It produces:

  • A FiftyOne dataset (one sample per frame, with detections and any available track / pitch annotations).
  • JSON / CSV exporters keyed by match_id for ad-hoc analytics and for ingest into footy-stats.

docs.title: 2. Module interface
docs.text:
# src/footy_track/output/exporters.py

class MatchExporter:
    def __init__(self, match_dir: Path): ...

    def to_fiftyone(self, dataset_name: str) -> fo.Dataset: ...
    def to_json(self, out_path: Path) -> None: ...
    def to_csv(self, out_dir: Path) -> None: ...

Each method is pure with respect to match_dir — given the same parquet inputs it produces the same output. Idempotent: re-running overwrites; never appends.

docs.title: 3. JSON schema (top-level)
docs.text:
{
  "match_id": "arsenal_bournemouth_1st_half",
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "frames": [
    {
      "continuous_time": 12.34,
      "is_broadcast": true,
      "detections": [...],
      "tracks": [{"track_id": 7, "x": 0.42, "y": 0.71, ...}],
      "pitch_positions": [{"track_id": 7, "x_pitch": 31.2, "y_pitch": 18.0}]
    }
  ],
  "tracks_meta": [...]
}

Per-frame ordering is by continuous_time. Missing stages (e.g. no projection yet) are simply omitted from each frame record.

docs.title: 4. CSV exporters
docs.text:
One file per logical entity, with match_id as the primary partition:

File Rows detections.csv one row per detection tracks.csv one row per (track_id, frame) pitch_positions.csv one row per (track_id, frame) in pitch coords tracks_meta.csv one row per track

CSVs are derived from the parquet artifacts, never written directly by the pipeline. This keeps the canonical store parquet-first.

docs.title: 5. FiftyOne integration
docs.text:
Builds on the existing to_fiftyone_sample helper in schema.py. Promotion plan:

  1. Existing per-frame BroadcastClassification and FrameDetections land as sample-level fields (already partially wired).
  2. Add tracks field: a fo.Detections instance with track_id on each detection so FiftyOne's track view works.
  3. Add pitch_positions field: a fo.Keypoints instance keyed by track_id (one keypoint per tracked player per frame).

Dataset name convention: footy_track__<match_id>.

docs.title: 6. Cross-stage invariants honoured
docs.text:
• All exports are keyed by ContinuousTime (see timings.md).
  • Bounding boxes are normalised top-left xywh in the JSON / CSV exports — pixel conversions only at the FiftyOne boundary, where FiftyOne demands them.
  • Class labels come from constants.py.

docs.title: 7. Out of scope
docs.text:
• A query API (covered by footy-stats).
  • Video overlay rendering (a later component that consumes these exports).
  • Streaming exports — outputs are batch-on-completion only.

docs.title: Pipeline overview: from broadcast video to "who did what"
docs.text: Where each model sits, what is measured, what is labelled, and how the loop improves. Every number here was measured in this project; anything unmeasured is marked as such.

docs.title: The goal, split into three problems
docs.text:
1. Where is the ball, every frame.
  2. Where are the players, every frame.
  3. Which player is which, within a segment and then across segments.

These are not one problem. The ball is a single ~16 px object with no identity — there is only one, so "which ball" never arises, and the hard part is not losing it. Players are ~20 near-identical objects where identity is the entire problem and localisation is comparatively easy.

Treating them with one pipeline is the main modelling mistake available here.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
broadcast video
      |
      v
  [segmenter]  ── already cut on shot boundaries: 0 interior camera cuts
      |            measured across 3,175 frames / 5 clips
      v
   162 clips (one match), 97,625 frames
      |
      v
  [RT-DETR-L]  ── per-frame detection: player / referee / in_play_ball
      |            2,767,151 detections, ~19.8 fps on a 3060 @ imgsz=1280
      v
  detections (TIER 3, machine-only)
      |
      +──────────────► ball path ──► [temporal/ball tracker]  ── UNSOLVED
      |
      v
  [LapTracker]  ── IoU + Hungarian association -> track_id
      |             ~540 fps on CPU; no training, no GPU
      v
  tracklets  (~5,249 over 40 clips; median length 13-31 frames)
      |
      +──► [kit-colour clustering] ──► team_id      ~99% separable, free
      |
      +──► [human review] ──────────► purity + jersey numbers
      |
      v
  [identity / ReID]  ── UNPROVEN: cluster tracklets into players
      |
      v
  player_id per detection ──► feature store ──► match data

docs.title: Which model does what
docs.text:
Stage Model Trained? Status Detection RT-DETR-L, imgsz=1280 fine-tuned on v11 Works. Ball mAP50 .665 / recall .591 at 1920 on v11-val (211 balls, 74% one clip); not yet measured at the served 1280 or on the v11 test split. (.221/.209 was yolo11n, see Best pipeline and label needs) Player tracking LapTracker (IoU + Hungarian) training-free Works, fragments. Consecutive-frame IoU median 0.72, only 4–6% below the 0.3 threshold; spawn rate 4.2% matches that tail. Fragmentation is a detection dropout problem, not an association problem Ball tracking VitTrack training-free Fails. Holds the ball for 5% of frames; confidence is a constant 0.119 and cannot separate on-ball from drifted. Do not tune — replace Team assignment k=2 on torso HSV none Works. 1.0% ambiguous (n=1,253). Hue 185° vs 23° Identity / ReID — — Unproven. Generic ImageNet features score AUC 0.43–0.49 (chance) because they encode background, not person. ReID-trained weights untested Purity pre-filter Gemini Flash — Not usable yet. 70% agreement, confidence collapsed into 0.65–0.80 so there is no bucket to trust

Two consequences worth stating plainly:

  • Tracker fragmentation is a detector problem. Association is near the limit of what the detections allow, so effort belongs in detection consistency (or interpolation across dropouts), not in a cleverer tracker.
  • The ball needs a different mechanism entirely. A single-object appearance tracker cannot follow a 16 px ball through broadcast motion. The candidates are per-frame detection plus motion-model interpolation, or a prior-conditioned detector — not another SOT tracker.

docs.title: What gets labelled, and by whom
docs.text:
Label Who Cost Feeds Ball position human, per frame expensive detector training + ball eval Detections RT-DETR free everything track_id LapTracker free tracklets team_id kit colour free identity constraint Tracklet purity human, per tracklet ~30/clip vs ~6,500 boxes — 250× cheaper than per-box tracker eval and free identity pairs Jersey number human, when legible seconds identity anchor Tracklet merges human, pairwise expensive without proposals identity clusters

Purity review is the keystone. It is the tracker's benchmark and the gate on identity training data: a pure tracklet is a free bag of same-player pairs, but one undetected switch injects thousands of false positives that teach the model two players are one person.

Provenance tiers hold throughout. TIER 1 human, TIER 2 machine + human checked, TIER 3 machine only. For tracklets the tier attaches to frame intervals, not whole tracks: a human reviewing 288 frames sees ~12, so claiming the whole tracklet is checked is a false claim.

docs.title: Auto-labelling and the improvement loop
docs.text:
The pipeline already auto-labels — 2.77M TIER-3 detections exist. The loop is about promoting that output to trustworthy labels without a human touching every frame.

      machine labels (TIER 3)
             |
             v
   propose  ──►  human verifies  ──►  TIER 2  ──►  retrain
      ^                 |
      |                 v
      └────── uncertainty sampling ◄── model disagreement / low margin

Three grounding mechanisms, cheapest first:

  1. Kit colour — free, ~99% accurate, and a hard constraint: two tracklets of different teams can never be the same player. Deletes a large slice of the pairwise space with no model and no labels.
  2. Jersey number — one legible frame anchors a whole cluster, because number
  3. team is unique within a match. ~40% of tracklets contain a frame ≥110 px, and numbers have been read by a human at 102 px, so the addressable pool is far larger than first estimated. This is the highest-value label per second.
  4. Pairwise merge — general but expensive; only worthwhile once a model can propose candidates and the human just confirms.

Active learning, per stage:

  • Detection — sample frames where tracking implies a detection should exist but none was produced (dropouts are the measured bottleneck), label those, retrain.
  • Tracking — no training; purity review tunes iou_threshold/max_age. Note the asymmetry: fragments are harmless, switches poison. Optimise purity, use coverage only as a guard against one-frame tracklets.
  • Identity — uncertainty sampling on embedding margin, constrained to same-team pairs. Cross-team pairs are trivial negatives and teach nothing.

The discipline that makes this safe: never let machine output promote itself. A pre-filter is only usable if its confidence is calibrated — high-confidence answers reliable enough to accept unreviewed, errors concentrated where the human is looking anyway. Gemini Flash currently fails that test not on accuracy but on calibration, which is why it is not in the loop.

docs.title: Open questions, in the order they should be answered
docs.text:
1. Does a ReID-trained embedding separate same-player pairs here? Everything downstream depends on it. Untested — the two failures so far were ImageNet backbones, which is not the same claim.
  2. What is the tracker's real purity? Being measured now. Needs complete clips; partial coverage biases toward whatever was reviewed first.
  3. What replaces VitTrack for the ball?
  4. What is the ball mAP at the served resolution, across matches? Settled: .665 / .591 is the checkpoint (v11-val, 1920); .221 was yolo11n. Open: one committed eval at 1280 and 1920 on the v11 test split plus held-out dense clips.
  5. Is per-player identity even needed downstream, or is team + role enough for the questions being asked of the data?

Question 5 is worth an hour before answering 1–3: it can delete a workstream.

docs.title: Player Identification & Re-Identification — Design
docs.text:
Bead: TBD · Date: 2026-08-30 · Author: design pass · Status: DRAFT

Scope: associating player detections (a) across frames within a clip and (b) across clips. Covers how to measure it, how to implement it, and how to collect the labels it needs. Resolves the re-ID / team / jersey TODOs deferred in player_tracking_format.md §6 and tracking.md §6.

Headline. The tracking code already exists (src/footy_track/trackers/, 599 LOC, LapTracker + UltralyticsTracker) and the storage already exists (detection.track_id, track_meta.{team_id,jersey_number,player_id,reid_parent_track_id}). Neither has ever been run against ground truth, because there are zero player identity labels and zero MOT metrics in this repo. So the bottleneck is not algorithms — it is measurement. I measured the footage directly (§0) and three facts reshape the problem: clips contain no interior camera cuts (0 in 3,175 frames across 5 clips), so within-clip tracking is single-shot tracking; frame-to-frame IoU is easy (median best-IoU 0.837, only 3.6% of associations ambiguous); and kit colour separates the two teams essentially perfectly (1.0% ambiguous). Meanwhile jersey OCR is dead on arrival — the median player box is 52×111 px, so digits are ~10–18 px tall. The recommendation is therefore: build a ~2-human-hour benchmark, measure the trackers we already have, add a free team-constraint, and build nothing else until the numbers say so. Do not repeat the VitTrack mistake of assuming a tracker works for a year without measuring it.

docs.title: 0. Measurements taken for this document
docs.text:
Everything below was measured on 2026-08-30 against real project data, not cited. Read the denominators. Most numbers come from a single clip (arsenal_mancity_20250925_seg002, 430 frames, 17.2 s) and must be re-run across the corpus before anything is built on them (§5, R2). Reproduction commands are in the Appendix.

# Measurement Value Denominator M1 Interior camera cuts per clip 0 5 clips (seg001/002/004/005/008), 3,175 frames. Each clip has exactly one histogram discontinuity, located in its final 1–4 frames. seg004 (175 fr) has none. M2 Players per frame mean 19.5, median 20, max 32 (conf≥0.10)mean 14.5, median 15, max 18 (conf≥0.5) seg002, 430 frames M3 Player box size @1920×1080 median 52 × 111 px; height p10 74 px, p90 149 px; width p10 26, p90 84 seg002, n=8,398 player boxes M4 Consecutive-frame best IoU median 0.837, mean 0.780, p10 0.545; 4.4% below 0.3; 3.3% below 0.1 seg002, conf≥0.5, n=6,242 instance-pairs M4b Association margin (best − 2nd-best IoU) median 0.810, p10 0.444; 3.6% below 0.05 same n=6,242 M5 Crowding / occlusion 6.3% of player instances overlap another player at IoU>0.2; 2.6% at IoU>0.5; 36.5% of frames contain ≥1 overlapping pair seg002, n=6,242 instances / 430 frames M6 Kit-colour team separability k=2 on torso HSV → split 541 / 712, 1.0% ambiguous. Centroids hue 185° (sky blue) and 23° (red). k=3 adds a 255-crop hue-61° cluster (likely referee/GK). seg002, n=1,253 torso crops, every 5th frame, conf≥0.5 M7 Corpus composition all 162 clips are one match (arsenal_mancity_20250925). 97,625 frames = 65.1 min. Clip length min 50 / p25 225 / median 430 / p75 785 / max 2,535 frames. machine_labels/_manifest.json M8 Per-class detector reliability player median conf 0.919 (74.3% ≥0.5) · coach 0.925 · referee 0.335 (44.5% ≥0.5) · in_play_ball 0.222 · person n=50, median 0.123, 0% ≥0.25 · player_sub n=11, median 0.113 seg002, n=11,512 detections

docs.title: What these imply
docs.text:
1. M1 collapses two of the four sub-problems into one. The clips were cut at shot boundaries by split_broadcast_segments. There is no such thing as "identity across a camera cut within a clip" — a cut is a clip boundary. So "across a cut" and "across clips" are the same problem, and "within a clip" is pure single-shot tracking over a median of 17 s.
  2. M4/M4b say plain IoU association should mostly work. 96.4% of associations have an unambiguous winner. This is a falsifiable prediction: IoU + Hungarian (LapTracker, already written) should score respectably, and its failures should concentrate in the 6.3% crowded instances from M5. If that prediction fails, the model of the problem is wrong and this plan needs revisiting.
  3. M6 makes team assignment nearly free, and — more valuably — makes it a cheap constraint on association (§3.6).
