docs.title: The gaps, in one list
docs.text:
1. No ball tracker. The ball is a set of independent per-frame boxes. The only ball tracker in a running path is VitTrack in the labeller, which holds the ball on 5% of frames (9/176, measured, KB footy-labeller-gotchas).
  2. The producers of the data we rely on are not in git: the RT-DETR training command, the batch inference that made the 2.77M machine labels, and the filter from machine labels to ball_candidates/.
  3. Identity output is unused. link_proposals/ and identity_labels/ are written and read by nothing.
  4. The team gate is inert. linker.candidate_links skips cross-team pairs only when both tracklets have a team (identity/linker.py:125), and no code sets it.
  5. No calibration and no projection. The store has a homography column (feature_store/schema.py:158) that nothing writes, and PitchProjector is called only from tests.
  6. The ball benchmark is narrow. v11-val has 211 balls, but 156 of them (74%) come from one 10-second clip (arsenal_example). All machine labels are one match.

docs.text:
The target: a broadcast match in, and out of it, for every frame where the pitch is visible, every player and the ball on a 105 x 68 m pitch with a team, a player identity where we can get one, and a confidence. docs.title: Calibration per frame, as a state machine
docs.text:
Calibration is where broadcast footage fights back: wide shots show plenty of lines, close-ups show grass and a player, and replays show a different camera. The homography stage must say which case it is in rather than emit a confident wrong matrix.

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> NoPitch
  NoPitch: No pitch view. Close-up, replay, crowd. No H, positions omitted
  Fitted: H fitted from keypoints and smoothed each frame. Enough matches, low reprojection error
  Carried: H carried from last fit by camera motion. Zoomed in, few lines
  Lost: Carried too long or drifted. Positions NaN, flagged
  NoPitch --> Fitted: wide view, enough keypoints
  Fitted --> Carried: too few keypoints
  Carried --> Fitted: keypoints return
  Carried --> Lost: drift check fails or N frames
  Lost --> Fitted: keypoints return
  Fitted --> NoPitch: cut or view change
  Carried --> NoPitch: cut or view change

docs.title: Part 3: phased plan
docs.text:
Effort is for one person: S is days, M is one to two weeks, L is several weeks. These are estimates, not measurements.

Phase Goal Builds Labels and data it needs Effort Success metric 0 A simple inference pipeline in git (separate PR) Video to broadcast clips to RT-DETR at 1280 to per-clip detections and LapTracker tracklets, as one command None new; reproduce the existing machine_labels/ on one clip S Matches the existing machine labels on a sample clip; runs end to end from a clean checkout 1 Trustworthy image-space tracking A committed ball eval; the ball tracker over machine labels; a player tracking eval (player_eval/, mirroring ball_eval/); team clustering wired in as a constraint Dense held-out ball clips with no_ball markers, at least 2 matches (~1.5-3k balls, assumed); the untouched v11 test split (243 balls); purity labels on 10 clips; detector run over a second match M Ball recall and precision at a fixed operating point on the held-out multi-match set, reported per match with instance counts; tracklet purity ≥ 0.95 and ID switches ≤ 1 per 1,000 player-frames (player_reid.md targets); team accuracy ≥ 0.98 2 Players and ball on a 2D pitch Pitch keypoint detector, per-frame homography with the state machine above, PitchProjector wired up, world-state store, a top-down replay Pitch keypoint labels on a few hundred frames across views and at least 2 stadiums (assumed); ~50 held-out frames with hand-clicked correspondences L Reprojection error in pixels on held-out keypoints; position error in metres on known landmarks (penalty spots, box corners); share of broadcast frames with a usable H; player speeds stay physically plausible 3 Who is who across shots ReID-trained embedding in score_links.py; team + number + appearance identity resolution; jersey numbers from humans, OCR only if measured legibility supports it Jersey numbers per tracklet (human, seconds each); merge verdicts; a second match for any generalisation claim L Identity accuracy: share of player-frames with the correct player_id on labelled clips; re-id mAP within a match with the gallery size stated 4 Plays and the ball in 3D Possession, passes and plays from world state; ball height from ballistic fits Hand-labelled events (pass start and end, shots) on a few matches; no height ground truth exists L Pass detection precision and recall against labelled events; possession accuracy per second; for height, consistency checks (landing points against later ground contacts)

Order. Phase 1 first: it reuses labels and machine output we already have, and every later phase needs its evals. Phase 2 can start in parallel once Phase 0 lands, because calibration does not depend on tracking. Phase 3 waits on the player_reid.md R7 question: is per-player identity needed at all, or are team and pitch position enough? Phase 4 comes last.

Where the label loop fits (proposal, not built). Phase 1 needs more diverse ball labels and a held-out eval. The Claude-assisted ball labelling loop is the proposed way to get the labels: Claude checks zoomed detector and tracker candidates on new matches, and a person confirms the doubtful ones in /ball_check. It sits beside Phase 1, not inside it: it consumes the Phase 1 ball tracker and the ball tracking eval as its fill step and its score, and it feeds the labels a later retrain needs. Held-out eval clips stay human-only. It adds no box to the Part 1 diagram, which is already at the diagram size limit.

docs.title: Measured versus assumed
docs.text: Measured (with denominator) Assumed or unmeasured Ball mAP50 0.665 / recall 0.591, v11-val, 211 balls, 74% one clip Ball recall on any match other than Man City Held-out recall at 1280 about 0.60, 74 balls That serving at 1280 costs nothing versus 1920 on a proper benchmark Ball precision by confidence band, 257 verdicts That a tracker can use those bands as its high/low thresholds Player mAP50 0.974 (yolo11n at 1280) RT-DETR per-class player mAP 0 interior cuts, 5 clips, 3,175 frames That this holds across all 162 clips and other broadcasters Team separation 1.0% ambiguous, 1,253 crops, one clip Team accuracy with a second kit pair, and for keepers and referees LapTracker fragmentation on seg000 Tracklet purity, IDF1, HOTA ImageNet re-id AUC 0.912 at 4 frames within a clip Any ReID-trained backbone on this footage — Everything about calibration accuracy on this footage — Every effort estimate on this page

docs.title: Top risks
docs.text:
1. Broadcast cuts break tracking. Every cut ends every track, and replays show the same players from another angle. Within a clip the splitter gives cut-free shots (measured on 5 clips), so cuts turn into a cross-shot identity problem (Phase 3), not a tracker problem. A temporal ball detector must fall back to a single frame at cuts.
  2. Homography fails on zoomed shots. Close-ups show too few landmarks for a fit. The plan is to carry H through pan and zoom by camera motion and to mark positions NaN once drift is too high, never to emit a confident wrong position (consistent with projection.md §5).
  3. The ball is ~11 px at 1280. Recall is 0.59 on a narrow benchmark, and the misses cluster in long gaps. A tracker can raise precision a lot and recall a little. Recall needs more diverse labels (other matches, other camera angles).
  4. An airborne ball projects to the wrong place. A homography maps the ground plane. A ball 3 m up, seen from a camera about 25 m high and 60 m away, lands roughly 5-10 m from its true ground point (geometry estimate). Until Phase 4, the ball's pitch position is only trustworthy when it is on or near the ground, and must carry a flag saying so.
  5. One match. All machine labels, the team measurement and the identity gallery come from Arsenal v Man City. No claim generalises until a second match is processed.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Which phase first after Phase 0: the ball tracker and evals (Phase 1), or calibration and the top-down view (Phase 2)?
  2. How ambitious on the ball in 3D: a 2D ground position with an "airborne" flag, or real height estimation?
  3. Jersey numbers: human anchors only (as player_reid.md §3.7 recommends), or OCR on the best frame of large tracklets? pipeline_overview.md says about 40% of tracklets have a frame at least 110 px tall and a human has read numbers at 102 px; that is the case for measuring OCR legibility before ruling it out.
  4. Is persistent per-player identity needed downstream, or are team, role and pitch position enough (player_reid.md R7, pipeline_overview.md Q5)?
  5. Calibration model: train our own keypoint detector on our labels, or start from a public pretrained pitch-calibration model and fine-tune (licence and fit to our footage to check)?
  6. Where should the world state live: the DuckDB feature store, or the per-stage parquet files from output.md and projection.md?

docs.text: Doc Kept Superseded or changed system_design.md Stage order; calibration in parallel with detection, feeding projection Adds a ball tracker, identity resolution, ball height and an event layer, which the stage list does not have. The calibration design doc it asks for (design/calibration.md) should be written in Phase 2 projection.md Pitch frame (centre-spot origin, metres), feet anchor for players, NaN on low-quality H, no clamping, smoothing downstream "Z-axis not modelled, acceptable for v1" stays true for Phase 2, but the ball row needs an airborne flag, and Phase 4 adds z. The code's ball anchor must match in_play_ball, and uncertainty_m must be in metres. H must be defined on the same normalised image coordinates the projector uses tracking.md ObjectTracker protocol, track ID lifecycle §4 says track state should survive a non-broadcast gap. In practice clips are separate files and a gap is a shot change, so continuity across it is identity resolution (Phase 3), as player_reid.md M1 already concluded player_reid.md P0-first order, tracklet purity as the primary metric, team as a hard constraint, its targets, milestone 1 §3.7 "do not build jersey OCR" becomes an open question for the reviewer (question 3), gated on a measured legibility rate pipeline_overview.md The three-problem split (ball, players, identity), the label tiers Its ball mAP row is out of date: .665/.591 is the RT-DETR figure and .221/.209 is yolo11n output.md MatchExporter, parquet first, JSON per frame Extend with world-state rows and plays once they exist

docs.title: Tracking Stage — Design
docs.text:
Status: DRAFT · Issue: footy_track-yjd

This document specifies the tracker module / algorithm for stage §2.5 of system_design.md. The on-disk output format is already specified in player_tracking_format.md; this doc focuses on the runtime contract and pluggable algorithm.

docs.title: 1. Stage in §2 of system_design.md
docs.text:
This is the Tracking stage (§2.5). It consumes per-frame FrameDetections (from §2.4 Detection) and produces:

  • A stream of Detection rows tagged with a persistent track_id.
  • A tracks_meta.json sidecar summarising each track's lifetime.

The output schema is locked by player_tracking_format.md.

docs.title: 2. Module interface
docs.text:
# src/footy_track/trackers/base.py

class ObjectTracker(Protocol):
    def update(
        self, frame_detections: FrameDetections, frame_t: ContinuousTime
    ) -> list[TrackedDetection]:
        """Assign track IDs to a single frame's detections.
        Stateful — call once per broadcast frame in time order."""

    def finalise(self) -> list[TrackMeta]:
        """Return per-track summaries after the last update()."""

TrackedDetection extends ObjectDetection with track_id: int and continuous_time: float. TrackMeta matches the tracks_meta.json schema in player_tracking_format.md §6.

docs.title: 3. Concrete implementations
docs.text:
Implementation Backing Notes UltralyticsTracker model.track(...) (BoT-SORT or ByteTrack) Wraps the Ultralytics native tracker; cheapest path to a working pipeline LapTracker Hungarian assignment via lap.lapjv on IoU + class Custom; used when we need re-ID hooks or reproducibility guarantees

Both must satisfy the ObjectTracker protocol. The tracker is selected per-pipeline-run via config; downstream code never branches on the implementation.

docs.title: 4. Track ID lifecycle (recap)
docs.text:
Authoritative rules live in player_tracking_format.md §5. Restated for this doc:

  1. IDs are monotone within a match and never reused.
  2. A track is active while its detections continue; after max_age missed frames it is lost; after max_lost_age it is deleted.
  3. Re-ID across deletion is represented by a new track with reid_parent_track_id pointing at the dead track.
  4. Non-broadcast frames are skipped at the tracker level — the classifier already gated them upstream — but track state must survive the gap (a 30-second replay should not split a player's track).

docs.title: 5. Cross-stage invariants honoured
docs.text:
• ContinuousTime is the only canonical timestamp on output rows.
  • Bounding boxes stay normalised top-left xywh.
  • Class labels come from constants.py.
  • Non-broadcast frames are observable in the output via the gap in frame_idx and the classifier's per-frame record.

docs.title: 6. Open questions
docs.text:
• Team / jersey assignment: handled by a downstream component reading tracks.parquet; not the tracker's job.
  • Streaming vs. batch: the protocol is single-frame update() so it works for both. A batch convenience wrapper can iterate.
  • Multi-camera: out of scope for v1.

docs.title: Multi-frame (camera-motion-compensated) dataset for a temporal ball detector
docs.text:
Status: dataset built (CPU only, no training). Branch exp/multiframe-dataset. Date 2026-11-14.

Goal: give the ball detector frames t-k and t+k aligned into frame t's coordinates, for every labelled Roboflow v11 image and for human-GT frames of clips the detector never saw, so a temporal model can be trained and evaluated without any new annotation.

KB pages relied on: footy-ball-detection-findings ("The key enabler": neighbours are recoverable from the file names, cuts are the trap; the dataset notes; the benchmark trap), footy-data-s3 / footy-data-plane-reconciliation (where the data lives, GT tiers), footy-labeller-gotchas. Research note research_notes/Offline football ball tracking models/tiny_object_video_detection.md (YOLOMG: frame differences from t-k and t+k aligned by homography, best k=2; Temporal-YOLOv8 channel stacking, untested on moving cameras; "patching RT-DETR to 9 channels is UNVERIFIED"). Split/exclusion logic read from scripts/export_training_dataset.py, ball_eval/dataset.py, clip_id.py (T-03).

docs.title: 1. Image name to (video, frame) mapping
docs.text:
Roboflow v11 lives at /mnt/storage/footy_data/detection_dataset/roboflow_dataset_11 (train 1035 / valid 215 / test 268, 1920x1080, class ids ball 0, coach 1, in_play_ball 2, person 3, player 4, player_sub 5, referee 6). Two name families, both mappable (multiframe/mapping.py):

Name Meaning Mapping <clip_stem>_<NNNNNN>_(png\|jpg).rf.<hash> (stem like astonvilla_seg080) NNNNNN is the frame index inside the clip ballcheck_clips/<stem>.mp4 (alias symlink), frame = NNNNNN arsenal_mancity_20250925_<NNNNNN>_png.rf... (full-match frames, 388 of 1518 images) NNNNNN is the ordinal of arsenal_mancity/full_video_frames/*.png, a 1 fps extraction absolute source frame = 25*NNNNNN + 12 (ffmpeg fps=1 takes t+0.5 s); inside the broadcast segment clip given by clips/segments.json (start_frame), frame = absolute - start

Gotchas found: the source .webm cannot be used (OpenCV returns the same frame for every seek), so full-match frames are located in the segment clips; the +12 offset is not documented anywhere and was found by pixel search; v11 frames whose absolute frame falls in a non-broadcast gap have no clip (2 images). eval_data/clips/ is empty on this machine, so the harness eval-exclusion list the export script builds from it is empty here too.

Verification: 60 random mapped images, decoded frame t vs the v11 JPEG: all 60 best-match at offset 0 (mean abs grey diff 0.3-2.2, i.e. JPEG noise; t+-1 is >10). Includes 9/9 full-match images. (multiframe_mapping_report --verify 60.)

Coverage (mapping_report.json; ball instance = class in_play_ball, the only populated ball class; the KB's "826 train ball instances" does not match the export on disk, which has 1,010):

split images balls mapped k=1 images / balls k=2 k=4 train 1035 1010 1034 / 1009 1020 / 1000 1017 / 997 1006 / 987 valid 215 211 215 / 211 207 / 205 204 / 202 198 / 196 test 268 243 267 / 243 265 / 241 264 / 241 261 / 239

"k=n" = frames t-n and t+n both exist in the clip (misses are clip edges). 99.9% map; at k=2 98.2% of train, 94.9% of valid images keep both neighbours. We still emit the edge images with a duplicated neighbour (below), so the split is identical to v11.

Leakage note: v11's split is by image, not by clip. By canonical clip id, 18 clips appear in both train and valid and 33 in both train and test (mostly full-match frames that land in the same 101 s segments). The existing val/test numbers therefore reward scene memorisation (the KB already flags astonvilla_seg080 / bournemouth_1st_seg070).

docs.title: 2. Camera-motion estimation
docs.text:
Compared on 30 v11 frames (stratified, <=6 per clip, t vs t-2) at a 480 px working width, single-thread CPU time per pair (the box was at load 20-50, wall time is meaningless). Quality = mean abs grey error (blurred, 480 px) over grass pixels of frame t not under a labelled person, after warping t-2 into t. Identity (no alignment) = 1.07 median; 40% of pairs have a moving camera (identity > 1.5, median 1.98). "worse" = accepted pairs whose aligned residual exceeds identity.

method masking failed pitch resid. median worse than identity ms / pair (CPU) ORB + RANSAC @480 person boxes 0% 1.11 50% 285 ORB + RANSAC @480 none 0% 1.29 47% 308 ORB + RANSAC @960 person boxes 0% 1.39 47% 467 AKAZE + RANSAC @480 person boxes 6.7% 1.10 39% 168 AKAZE + RANSAC @480 none 0% 0.91 33% 154 ECC homography @480 (mine) person boxes 0% 0.62 13% 193 ECC homography @480 (mine) none 0-3% 0.63 7% 195 ORB then ECC @480 person boxes 0% 0.63 13% 455 LK + RANSAC (calibration/temporal, whole frame minus overlay and person boxes) person boxes 0% 0.49 6.7% 57 same, no boxes (whole frame minus overlay) none 0% 0.61 10% 62 same, grass-only mask none 0% 0.81 20% 62 LK then ECC / its own ECC person boxes 0% 0.51 3.3% 520 / 499

(alignment_eval_d2.json, compare_temporal_d2.json; ORB/AKAZE/ECC rows come from an earlier run of the same sample, n=30 with the identical seed. Small n; differences of ~0.1 are within noise. d=1 and d=4 were not measured.)

What the numbers say:

  • Feature matching on ORB/AKAZE is not better than doing nothing on broadcast frames: ~1000 RANSAC inliers, but they sit on the stands and hoardings (different depth/plane), so the homography is wrong for the pitch (50% of pairs worse than identity). Intensity-based methods (ECC) and tracked-corner LK on the whole frame are clearly better; on moving-camera pairs ECC gives 0.85-0.9 vs identity 1.98, on near-static pairs 0.55-0.6 vs 0.92.
  • Chosen: LK + RANSAC from calibration/temporal.py (shared module, see below). Best residual, lowest identity-regression rate, 57 ms/pair CPU (~73 ms wall under load), 3.4x faster than my ECC and 9x faster than LK+ECC, which gained nothing. This agrees with the other session's measurements (LK ~45 ms, ECC 0.6-1.5 s with no accuracy gain, whole-frame mask beats grass-only).
  • Player masking: for LK, boxes help (0.49 vs 0.61 unmasked); for my ECC they did not (0.62 vs 0.63; within noise). Grass-only is clearly worse (0.81, 20% worse than identity).
  • Disagreement recorded: the shared module's cut notes say non-cuts have histogram distance <= 0.30; on my three 500-1400 frame scans non-cuts were <= 0.09 (p99 0.057), cuts >= 0.37 (different histogram: 8x4x4 HSV, 160 px, Bhattacharyya). I use 0.2 for the dataset.

Shared-module provenance: src/footy_track/calibration/{__init__,geometry,pitch_model, refine,temporal}.py and prelabel/{__init__,candidates}.py are copied verbatim from branch exp/calibration-temporal at commit 7988bde (temporal.py needs those files to import; identical blobs at identical paths merge cleanly when that branch lands). Use is through one adapter, multiframe/align.py::estimate_pair_lk, and estimate_pair(a, b, mask_a, mask_b, scale, method) returns PairMotion(H_px, H_norm, ok, inliers, residual, method, reason), a subset of the shared API's PairMotion (which adds n_tracked, score). H maps frame a pixels to frame b pixels; render b into a with warp_to_ref (warpPerspective(..., WARP_INVERSE_MAP)).

docs.title: Full-run alignment stats (k=2, LK, 3,266 neighbour slots)
docs.text:
split ok edge (clip boundary) cut alignment failed train (2068) 2039 17 11 1 valid (430) 418 11 1 0 test (534) 526 3 1 4 heldout (234) 225 8 1 0

So 98.0% aligned; 0.4% cuts, 0.15% alignment failures, 1.2% clip edges. Alignment failures: 2 "too few features", 3 with 17-22 inliers (< 25). Alignment ms per ok pair: median 73 wall (loaded box). Whole build: 4,024 s, single process, 2 threads, for 1,633 images.

docs.title: 3. Cuts
docs.text:
Broadcast cuts make t-k a different camera: the diff turns into noise on exactly the frames that matter. A neighbour is replaced by a copy of gray(t) (so |diff| = 0) when, checked in this order: it is outside the clip (edge); the max Bhattacharyya distance between consecutive frames from t to t+-k exceeds 0.2 (cut); or alignment fails (align_fail: <25 RANSAC inliers, inlier ratio, degenerate H, residual gate of the shared module).

Calibration (multiframe_cut_scan.py, 2,531 frames of three clips): consecutive-frame distance is bimodal; ordinary frames have median 0.03, p99 0.057, max 0.09; the five cuts found are 0.37, 0.45, 0.69, 0.72, 0.80 and ECC alignment of those pairs fails or has residual 30-50 (ordinary pairs: < 5). 14 neighbour slots were flagged as cuts in the dataset, one at 0.24 (near threshold; may be a flash rather than a cut). Each stored image records per-side status, frame number, histogram distance, inliers and residual in meta.jsonl.

docs.title: 4. Channel format decision and Ultralytics support
docs.text:
Decision: (A) 5 channels [gray(t-k) aligned, B, G, R of t, gray(t+k) aligned], one multi-page TIFF per image, 8-bit, LZW, full 1920x1080. (B) RGB + |aligned diff| is derivable from A in one line (abs(g(t) - prev), abs(next - g(t))) and can be made at load time or in a custom dataset; A cannot be recovered from B.

Reasoning: - The viewer shows why signed grey planes matter: a moving ball appears as a bright blob at both t-k and t+k positions in A (a dipole after differencing) and the network can use the sign and direction; |diff| discards both. - A resting ball (e.g. train_astonvilla_seg080_000039_ball_static.png) cancels almost completely in any diff, so a pure-diff model loses the ball exactly when it is easiest. A keeps the full RGB frame, so the model degrades to the single-frame detector there. - Extra channels can be initialised so the model starts as the pretrained single-frame detector (copy the RGB stem filters, zero the other 2 input channels). - Cost of A over B: a model must learn differencing; with ~1,000 balls B's explicit prior may train faster. Cheap to test both: B is a transform of A.

TIFF note: cv2.imwritemulti of 2-D pages; Ultralytics' imread reads .tif/.tiff with cv2.imdecodemulti and stacks 2-D pages on axis 2 -> (1080, 1920, 5) uint8 (checked). Channel order is stored as B, G, R: for 5 channels Ultralytics' Format only reverses the channel order when there are exactly 3, so the tensor keeps this order. When inflating a pretrained RGB stem, put R/G/B filters on input channels 3/2/1 (not 1/2/3).

Ultralytics support, pinned version 8.3.241 (uv.lock), source read and exercised on CPU:

piece result dataset yaml channels: 5 read in data/utils.py:431 and passed to YOLODataset (dataset.py:88) YOLO model (yolo11n.yaml, DetectionModel(ch=5)) builds, first conv takes 5 channels, forward OK (checked) RT-DETR (rtdetr-l.yaml, RTDETRDetectionModel(ch=5)) builds, first conv takes 5 channels, forward OK (checked); RTDETRTrainer.get_model passes ch=self.data["channels"] (models/rtdetr/train.py:55) data pipeline, YOLODataset and RTDETRDataset, augment on/off returns (5, H, W) uint8 tensors with labels (checked); RandomHSV skips non-3-channel images, LetterBox has a multispectral branch, mosaic allocates img.shape[2] channels; cv2.warpAffine/resize/flip work on 5 channels (border fill is 114 only on the first 3 channels, 0 on the rest) pretrained weights stem shape mismatch -> intersect_dicts silently drops it (random stem). Needs manual stem inflation. full train() loop with 5 channels UNVERIFIED: a 1-epoch CPU run of both models was started and killed to shed load before it finished (it did get through model build, dataset build and the first epoch header). Validation, AMP and plotting code paths with 5 channels were not exercised.

docs.title: 5. What the aligned diff images show
docs.text:
Four PNGs in docs/experiments/multiframe_dataset/ (visualise_multiframe.py): top left frame t (ball boxed), top right the aligned |t - (t-2)| x4 over the whole frame; bottom a 96 px crop (x3) around the GT ball: aligned prev, RGB t, aligned next, two aligned diffs and the same diff with no alignment.

  • Static structure cancels. On the pitch, field lines, mowing stripes, hoardings and stands, alignment leaves only thin faint edges; players come out as bright edge outlines. Crowd texture leaves a noisy residual (high-frequency, sub-pixel misregistration) but it is dim and different in character from a ball. The scorebug/logo is bright (screen-static graphics move relative to the aligned pitch) but is a fixed-position artefact the model can learn to ignore.
  • A moving ball is a dipole / short streak in the diffs (bright disc at both its t-k and t+k positions in the two diffs; heldout_seg035_000287, _000232: a clear white blob under the yellow GT circle in |t-prev| and |next-t|).
  • But the ball is not isolated in the diff when it is in contact with players: in the scrum (train_mancity_seg030_000430) and in _000232 it sits inside a bright tangle of leg and boot motion, so the diff alone does not separate it; appearance (RGB) must still do that.
  • A resting ball vanishes: train_astonvilla_seg080_000039 (ball stationary on grass, player nearby) shows only a faint ring in both diffs, which is why A keeps RGB.
  • Alignment helps but is not dramatic when the camera is nearly still (the unaligned crop in _000287 is similar), and the full-frame gap shows up when the camera pans (my 30-pair numbers: residual 0.85 aligned vs 1.98 unaligned on moving-camera pairs).

docs.title: 6. Dataset
docs.text:
/mnt/storage/footy_data/multiframe_v1/k2/ (new, nothing overwritten; not uploaded to S3 or the desktop). 5.4 GB, 1,633 TIFFs (about 3.3 MB each).

images/{train,val,test,heldout}/<id>.tiff      5 pages, 1920x1080, uint8
labels/{train,val,test,heldout}/<id>.txt       YOLO, v11 class ids, copied unchanged for v11 images
data.yaml           train/val/test, nc 7, channels 5       (v11 names, same ids as the detector)
data_heldout.yaml   train/images/train, val -> images/heldout
meta.jsonl          per image: source video, frame, per-neighbour status/inliers/residual/hist
manifest.json       counts and options (copy: manifest_k2.json next to this doc)
split images ball instances both neighbours aligned (images / balls) train (= v11 train, 1 unmappable image dropped) 1034 1009 1007 / 988 val (= v11 valid) 215 211 203 / 201 test (= v11 test, 1 unmappable dropped) 267 243 261 / 239 heldout 117 117 108 / 108

Image ids are the v11 file stems (so train/val/test have the same image ids as the existing detector). RGB(t) is decoded from the video, not from the v11 JPEG (identical up to JPEG noise), so t and its neighbours share codec statistics.

Held-out eval set: human GT (tier 1 labeller, tier 2 vittrack+human_checked; tier 3 excluded) frames with a ball, from ball_gt_marks, in clips whose canonical clip id (footy_track.clip_id) is absent from v11 train, minus frames that are already v11 images. 117 frames / 117 balls. Of these 84 balls (6 clips: arsenal_bournemouth_1st_seg035/031/015/021/060, arsenal_mancity_part093) are strictly clean (clip in none of train/valid/test; flag strict_heldout in meta.jsonl); the other 33 come from clips present only in v11 valid/test (arsenal_example 20, bournemouth_seg009 10, three single frames). Labels for held-out frames are the tier<=2 GT boxes of that frame in v11 class ids. 84 strict balls (76 with both neighbours aligned) is a thin benchmark (the KB's 44-instance warning applies); report instance counts with any metric, and read the 117 as secondary. Because the repo-wide split-by-clip rule makes nearly every GT clip a training clip, there is little clean GT left; more would need new labelling in unseen clips.

Build: uv run python -m footy_track.scripts.build_multiframe_dataset --k 2 --method lk (refuses to write into a non-empty directory). k=2 was chosen on coverage (98% of images have both neighbours; k=4 gets 97%) and because YOLOMG's best k is 2; k=1 and k=4 need only a re-run (about 1.1 h on this box).

docs.title: 7. Reproduce / code map
docs.text:
• src/footy_track/multiframe/ mapping.py (name -> source), align.py (estimate_pair, warp, masks, hist distance), frames.py (reader, labels, machine-label boxes), v11.py.
  • scripts/: multiframe_mapping_report.py (coverage, --verify), multiframe_alignment_eval.py, multiframe_cut_scan.py, build_multiframe_dataset.py, visualise_multiframe.py.
  • docs/experiments/multiframe_dataset/compare_temporal.py documents how the shared-module comparison was run (scratch tree of commit 7988bde; not importable on this branch alone).
  • tests/multiframe/ (5 tests: name parsing, pan recovery for ECC and LK, masked box, cut histogram). Run with PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 pytest -o addopts="" if the hydra pytest plugin is broken in the env.

docs.title: 8. Before GPU training
docs.text:
1. Run one real train() epoch with channels: 5 for YOLO and RT-DETR on the desktop GPU (the part marked UNVERIFIED above), including validation and AMP.
  2. Stem inflation: copy pretrained RGB filters (R/G/B to input channels 3/2/1), zero-init channels 0 and 4, scale if needed; otherwise the stem is random.
  3. Hand the dataset to the desktop (S3 or rsync; 5.4 GB) - not done here.
  4. Decide A vs B on held-out strict (84 balls) and v11 val together, always reporting the instance count and the by-clip leakage caveat above. Train with imgsz=1280.
  5. Mosaic/translate augmentation moves the 5 channels together (good); hsv_* is skipped for 5 channels, so colour augmentation is lost.
  6. Known limits: stationary balls and balls in player contact carry little motion signal; 25 fps with the ball moving < 1 diameter/frame gives short streaks (k=2 is 80 ms).

docs.title: SAM 3 / SAM 3.1 as a slow, offline, background ball labeller
docs.text:
Naming note: the held-out match used to be called "Norwich"; it is Arsenal v Nottingham Forest (scoreboard NFO), now arsenal_nottinghamforest. Old ids (arsenal_norwich_segNNN, *_norwich dirs) and experiment artifacts written under the old name (r3_norwich, exp/temporal/round3/norwich*, S3 exp_temporal_r3/out/*_norwich) keep it, so old numbers can still be traced.

Branch exp/sam3-offline-labeller (from exp/temporal-detector @ 331ae64). Code: experiments/sam3_offline/ (README there), Prefect flows ~/code/jobs/footy_sam3.py + sam3.prefect.yaml, numbers: docs/experiments/sam3_offline_labeller.json (+ experiments/sam3_offline/results/), sheets: docs/experiments/sam3_offline_labeller/. Builds on temporal_detector_round3.md (held-out list, 50 fps handling, S1 gate, SAM2.1-small crop512 tracker). All GPU runs were Prefect flow runs on the gpu pool (desktop RTX 2070 8 GB), one at a time.

Question. Can SAM 3 / 3.1 label balls offline: one known frame (a confident RT-DETR box, an overview, a human click) -> track forwards and backwards through long stretches -> labels written by a queued background job? Speed does not matter, offline quality and throughput do.

docs.title: Answers in brief
docs.text:
1. How far does one seed carry? SAM 3 is no better than the SAM2.1-small crop512 tracker we already have. Held-out clips + the 359-frame Aston Villa run, oracle seeds (1 217 scored frames): recall@10 0.943 (SAM 3) vs 0.945 (SAM2.1), paired -0.002 [-0.007, +0.004]; on the six sparse held-out clips both are at 1.000 (251 frames, up to 100-250 frames from the seed); with RT-DETR conf >= 0.8 seeds both are 0.996 (228 frames). The only place SAM 3 separates is arsenal_example (an out-of-play ball in the crowd, practically invisible): 0.301 vs 0.250 (+0.051 [+0.032, +0.072], one clip; both useless). The set is saturated, so it cannot show a gain and does not show one; SAM 3 costs 3x the time (2.4 vs 7.0 frames/s) and 6x the memory (4.9 vs 0.8 GB). SAM 3.1 (multiplex) is equal to SAM 3 here (0.928 vs 0.932 on dev) and slower (2.1 fps, 6.2 GB).
  2. What helps. A box seed (box ~ box + point > point-only: -0.020), a crop that follows the ball at 512 px (round-3 size; 768 is the same, 384 -0.020, 256 -0.244, no crop -0.039), fp16 (fp32 gives identical labels at 3.2x the time). What does not: text prompts as the tracker (0.73 / 0.63 vs 0.98, no memory), frame_step 2 (2x faster but -0.051), the "offload state to CPU" memory setting (-0.28, a bug-like loss and no VRAM saved), crop 256. Gating: SAM 3's object-score logit is a better gate than SAM2's (score > 8: precision 0.996 at 59 % coverage vs 1.0 at 37 %); the S1 gate (forward track of seed a x backward track of seed b within 5 px) was right 14/14 times in the production demo, whereas a score gate cannot catch a false seed (an RT-DETR conf 0.818 "ball" on a yellow boot was tracked as a boot for ~90 frames with logit 8-10). Recovery and the rest of the tricks: see the sections below.
  3. SAM 3 as a seed finder is the real finding. Text prompt "ball" on 384 px tiles upscaled to 1008: top-1 hit@10 0.85 vs RT-DETR-L 0.60 on the same 94 held-out GT frames (Bournemouth 0.85 vs 0.51; Man City 0.86 vs 0.90), any-candidate recall 0.96 vs 0.71. "yellow ball" is equal on Bournemouth (0.86) and useless on a white ball (0.00): the prompt must follow the match. Whole-frame text detection (one 1008 px pass) is already 0.76; 540 px tiles are worse (0.71); "white ball" / "small white ball" fail (0.14 / 0.11). It costs ~5-6 s per frame at 384 px tiles (15 tiles). So SAM 3 can find its own seeds, slowly. Caveat: on the 80 dev frames (clips RT-DETR was trained on, many blurred in-play balls) it is worse than RT-DETR (0.64 vs 0.85), so the claim holds for footage RT-DETR has not seen.
  4. Throughput / cost on the RTX 2070. SAM 3 tracker 0.42 s/frame (2.38 fps) after a bf16 patch (see Setup; unpatched 0.75 s), SAM 3.1 0.48 s, SAM2.1 0.14 s. A match half (~70 k frames at 25 fps): 8.2 GPU-hours for one pass over every frame with SAM 3 (2.7 h with SAM2.1), 16.4 h if every frame is covered twice for the S1 gate, 2.5 h if SAM 3 only fills the ~30 % of frames the detectors miss; 1.1 h of seed finding per half at one 384-tile probe every 100 frames.

Recommendation (details at the end): do not replace SAM2.1 in the pseudo-label pipeline with SAM 3 / 3.1 as the tracker. Make SAM 3 the background seed finder and seed verifier (text prompt on 384 px tiles, per-match prompt), keep SAM2.1 crop512 as the track engine, and use S1 (two-seed agreement) rather than scores as the trust signal. Use the SAM 3 tracker only for stretches where SAM2 is known to fail (crowd / long occlusion), where it showed its only, small, gain.

docs.title: Main table: SAM2.1-small crop512 vs SAM 3 vs SAM 3.1 (best settings: box seed, crop 512, fp16)
docs.text:

Paired differences (same seeds and frames), SAM 3 - SAM2.1: all (no example) -0.002 frame CI [-0.007, +0.004] / clip CI [-0.002, +0.000]; sparse held-out +0.000; Aston Villa -0.002 [-0.010, +0.005]; arsenal_example +0.051 [+0.032, +0.072] (one clip).

Read it carefully: - Saturation. Every held-out GT frame is a frame where a human could see the ball, and a clean seed on the same shot is enough for both trackers: 251/251 on the sparse clips. The "250+" bin is one clip (Aston Villa, a slowly dribbled ball); its 0.845 is mostly 10-11 px misses (3 px over the 10 px threshold: box-label noise at 720p). The rows cannot rank the models; they show that tracking from one good seed is not where the remaining error is on this data. The ball-in-play motion in the sparse clips is fast (median 20-38 px between consecutive GT frames in Man City) and still 100 %. - Drift / loss behaviour (what the misses look like). Dev (SAM 3 box crop512): 82 % of misses are "tracker reports absent" (a camera cut ends the track: the crop follows the old position), 9 % drift 10-50 px, 9 % wrong object; SAM2: 85 % absent, 15 % wrong object. The drift case in track_sam3_mancity_seg010_o2_bwd_drift_to_player.jpg: the crop follows a player's boot for ~30 frames while the ball is occluded (score logit 1-3 vs 7-9 on the ball), then re-acquires the ball. The held-out + Aston Villa misses (69 of 1 217): 33 % absent, 67 % within 10-50 px (mostly the 10-11 px near-misses). - Scene cuts matter: cuts.py finds 1-2 cuts in the 16 clips (part093 at frame 37, bournemouth_1st_seg070 at 47, mancity_seg010 at 593). A track must be stopped at a cut (not done here; the S1 gate would reject the frames after it).

docs.title: Setup (desktop, RTX 2070 8 GB)
docs.text:
• Separate venv ~/sam3-exp/venv (python 3.12, torch 2.8.0+cu128, numpy 1.26.4); upstream facebookresearch/sam3 @ eef6839 (2026-11-13) installed editable from ~/sam3-exp/sam3_src. Not ultralytics 8.4.213: its SAM3VideoPredictor is the frame-by-frame predictor pipeline, its 3.1 support is image / point only, whereas the upstream tracker has the SAM2-style init_state / add_new_points_or_box / propagate_in_video API the round-3 crop-following driver needs. Nothing was installed into ~/sam2-exp/venv, the jobs venv or the footy venv.
  • Weights: sam3.pt (sha256 9999e234..., identical to the mini copy) and sam3.1_multiplex.pt (complete, 3 502 755 717 bytes) pulled from S3 with presigned urls.
  • Licence: SAM License (Meta, 2025-11-19): royalty-free, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to use / modify / distribute the SAM Materials; redistribution of the model or derivatives only under the same agreement (include a copy); publications of research done with it must acknowledge the use; no use for ITAR / military / weapons / espionage or trade-control-prohibited ends; the licence terminates if we sue Meta over the materials; "AS IS". Fine for an internal labelling pipeline; keep the licence text with any redistributed weights. (pyproject says "MIT" in a classifier, the LICENSE file is the SAM License.) Dependencies: timm, ftfy, regex, iopath, huggingface_hub (unused with a local checkpoint), numpy < 2; no flash-attn / triton on sm_75.
  • RTX 2070 (sm_75) patches, applied as runtime monkeypatches in sam3_track.patch_turing (upstream untouched):
  • sam3.perflib.fused.addmm_act (ViT MLP fc1 + GELU) hard-casts to bfloat16; sm_75 has no bf16 tensor cores, so cuBLAS ran an emulated magma_sgemmEx<bf16> kernel = 59 % of the backbone time. Plain fp16 autocast: backbone 0.63 -> 0.29 s per 1008 px frame (2.1x), tracker 0.75 -> 0.42 s per frame.
  • The upstream constructors enter a global bf16 autocast (bf16_context.__enter__()); it is exited right after building and runs use torch.autocast(fp16). No fp16 overflow / NaN observed.
  • SAM 3.1: decoder.functional_attention forces the FlashAttention SDPA backend ("No available kernel" on Turing) -> efficient / math backends. The standalone 3.1 tracker also needs tracker.backbone = detector.backbone and forward_image(need_sam3_out=False); the multiplex demo tracker has no box prompt: "box" = the ellipse inscribed in the box as a mask prompt, "point" = the centre point.
  • Precision / memory (2 dev clips, 1 seed each, 60 frames, 186 frames scored): fp16 autocast 0.995 recall, 2.38 fps, 4.9 GB peak (fp32 weights resident + fp16 copies cached by autocast); fp32 identical labels (paired +0.000) at 0.74 fps (3.2x slower), 4.3 GB; memory selection off (apply_temporal_disambiguation=False) 1.000 (+0.005 [+0.000, +0.019], n.s.); offload_state_to_cpu 0.715 (-0.280), VRAM unchanged (4.8 GB: the weights dominate) -> do not use. Weights are 3.4 GB in fp32; a half-precision copy of the backbone would free ~2 GB if more headroom is needed (not needed: 8 GB fit, long clips are fine because frames are injected one at a time and per-frame state is ~1 MB; whole-match tracks prune state older than 300 frames, prune_age).

docs.title: Data, seeds, metrics
docs.text:
Clips and GT (spec_v2.json, built by spec.py from /mnt/storage/footy_data/ball_gt_marks; human labeller / human_checked ball marks only; error in 1080p-equivalent px, hit = within 10 px):

set clips how used final / held-out Bournemouth seg009, 015, 021, 031, 035, 060 (50 fps clips handled at 25 fps = every 2nd frame, as round 3); Man City part093, seg101, seg134, seg135 final numbers, never used to choose a setting (the single-GT clips seg060 / 101 / 134 / 135 only enter the realistic-seed protocol) final / dense astonvilla_seg080 (568 labelled frames, 4 runs, longest 359 frames, 720p) the only clip with GT > 250 frames from a seed example arsenal_example reported separately dev mancity_seg010, mancity_seg050, bournemouth_1st_seg070 (dense, yellow ball); mancity_seg031 for seed-finder only every prompt / crop / trick search (2 oracle seeds per clip, 120 frames each way = 488 scored samples)
  • Odd original frames of the 50 fps clips are scored against the mean of the two neighbouring processed frames (GT lies on both parities: seg009 has 2 even + 9 odd GT frames).
  • Oracle seeds: GT frames at the 15 / 50 / 85 % quantile of the clip's GT frames (dense runs: run start + run middle); the first GT frame is avoided (mancity_seg031 frame 0 is not on the ball: gt_mancity_seg031.jpg). Realistic seeds: RT-DETR-L v11 @1280 ball detections with conf >= 0.8, best first, >= 40 frames apart, 3 per clip (Bournemouth from the round-3 labels_bm_audit, Man City from machine_labels, part093 / arsenal_example from a fresh r3_detect.py run). RT-DETR has no conf >= 0.8 ball in seg021 / seg031 (no seed there). A random sample of 64 such candidates over the held-out clips was inspected by eye: 64 / 64 real balls (rtdetr_conf80_seed_candidates_64.jpg; so false seeds are rare, not absent: see the production demo).
  • Nottingham Forest: ball_gt_marks_nottinghamforest holds only the blind-check verdicts (ball_checks), no window labels, so nothing could be scored on Nottingham Forest.
  • A sample = one (seed, GT frame) pair: the forward (g > seed) or backward track of the seed at g; recall@10 counts absent as a miss; precision(emitted) = hits / emitted. Intervals: 95 % percentile bootstrap over frames and (cluster) over clips; paired differences on identical samples.
  • GT sanity (contact sheets): dev and held-out GT are on the ball except mancity_seg031 frame 0. arsenal_example's 20 held-out frames (59, 160-198) are an out-of-play ball inside the crowd (a white blob among spectators; the labels follow a smooth trajectory, so they are not wrong, but the target is practically invisible: gt_arsenal_example_heldout.jpg). RT-DETR (0.05), SAM 3 text detection on full frame / tiles (0.00-0.05 top-1, any prompt) and both trackers fail there: SAM 3 does not find those balls.

  • The crop is the biggest lever, with a plateau at 512-768 px: a 256 px window loses the ball whenever it moves fast (-0.24), 384 -0.02, no crop -0.04 (SAM 3 on the squashed 1080p frame still works: the ball is 5-6 px there). Compute is identical for every crop (the model always sees 1008 px), so "upscale the crop to the native input" is free and automatic; upscaling more (smaller crops) does not help, a larger field of view does.
  • Box seed (with or without the centre point) > point only. SAM 3.1 behaves like SAM 3 (same recall within noise, higher precision, lower coverage, +20 % time, +1.3 GB): its multiplex advantage is for many simultaneous objects, not for one ball.
  • Text prompts as the tracker (no seed memory: per frame, text detection on the crop around the last position, nearest candidate, text:ball 0.725 [0.679, 0.775], text:yellow ball 0.630 (white-ball Man City clips included), reach 80, 346 samples) lose 0.26-0.35 against the box-seeded tracker (0.983): the detector alone drops the ball (coverage 0.73) although what it emits is 99.6 % correct. Text belongs in seed finding / recovery, not in tracking.
  • frame_step 2 doubles throughput (4.75 effective fps) but costs 0.051 recall: linear interpolation over the skipped frame fails on kicks.

The single miss (seg060: the only GT frame is 178 frames from the seed) is the same for both. Seed verification with SAM 3's own text detector (seed_check: best IoU of any "ball" detection on a 512 px crop with the seed box): all 24 seeds had IoU 0.63-0.92 with a detection (text score 0.08-0.85), i.e. no seed in this set was a false positive, so the check could not be shown to separate anything.

docs.title: Gating
docs.text:
• Object-score logit (own presence head). Raising the gate trades coverage for precision; SAM 3's score is the more informative one. Held-out + Aston Villa, oracle seeds: gate 0 / 4 / 6 / 8: SAM 3 coverage 0.98 / 0.94 / 0.87 / 0.59 with precision 0.961 / 0.964 / 0.974 / 0.996; SAM2 0.99 / 0.91 / 0.84 / 0.37 with 0.957 / 0.969 / 0.972 / 1.000. On arsenal_example gate 8: SAM 3 coverage 0.17, precision 0.966 (recall 0.164) vs SAM2 coverage 0.02: SAM 3's scores separate the few correct frames from the crowd; SAM2's do not. (The 0.96 baseline precision is the 10-11 px near-misses of one clip.)
  • S1 (forward track of seed a, backward track of the next seed b, agree within 5 px): with oracle seeds all 217 GT frames between seeds pass and are correct for both models (nothing to reject). In the production demo with RT-DETR seeds on Bournemouth seg035 (below) S1-gated frames were 14 / 14 correct while single-track score-gated frames were 24 frames at only 67 %: the wrong ones come from a false seed.
  • SAM 3 x SAM2 agreement (within 5 px, oracle seeds, held-out + Aston Villa): coverage 0.974, recall 0.937, no precision gain (both make the same 10-11 px drift errors); it is a useful independent-model check against false seeds, not against labelling noise.
  • Lesson (production demo): a wrong seed (RT-DETR conf 0.818 "ball" = a yellow boot at seg035 frame 58) gives a confident, consistent track (logit 8-10, 90+ frames): demo_labels_bournemouth_seg035.jpg. No score gate can catch it; agreement between independent seeds (S1) or a seed check can.

docs.title: Recovering lost tracks
docs.text: Implemented in sam3_track.py (config recover): after loss_k = 3 consecutive lost frames (mask empty or score logit < 0), search around the last confident position (radius 150 px, 512 px crop) and re-seed the tracker with the nearest candidate as a new conditioning box, then continue propagating. Candidates from (a) SAM 3 text detection text:ball on the crop (score >= 0.3) or (b) RT-DETR candidates (conf >= 0.5, cands, the "re-seed from detector candidates" variant). Ablation on the final oracle set, SAM 3 box crop512, reach 400 (astonvilla_seg080, arsenal_example, bournemouth seg035; (b) on the last two): the recovery never fired (0 re-seeds in every track), results are identical to the baseline (0.929 / 0.301 / 1.000). The loss events in these clips are a camera cut or a ball that is not visible (crowd), where there is no candidate within the search radius; the held-out set has no loss that a nearby detection could repair. So the benefit of recovery is unmeasured, and the re-seed code path was never exercised on real data (treat it as untested); a test needs footage with occlusions behind players / long kicks that the tracker loses but a detector still sees (the dev drift case mancity_seg010 o2 backward is such a case, but only 2 of the dev tracks lose the ball). Text detection as a seed finder is the part that works (below). Not done: RT-DETR / text recovery for SAM 3.1 (its detector API differs), re-seeding on a second SAM2 opinion.

docs.title: Text-prompt seed finder (hit rate vs RT-DETR on held-out frames)
docs.text:
SAM 3 image detector, text prompt, boxes in full-frame px, scored on every GT ball frame (original frame index, both parities): "top-1" = the highest-scoring detection is within 10 px, "any" = some detection (score >= 0.02, <= 15 per frame after NMS) is within 10 px. Tilings: full = whole frame squashed to 1008 (ball ~5 px), t540 = 3x2 tiles of 540 px, t384 = 5x3 tiles of 384 px (2.6x up). RT-DETR-L on the same frames (stride-1 labels, conf >= 0.1) for reference. No prompt / tiling was selected on these frames beyond reading the table; a dev-set check follows. top-1 hit@10 / any hit@10:

detector (tiling / prompt) Bournemouth (73, yellow ball) Man City (21) Aston Villa, 39 evenly spaced all held-out (no arsenal_example) incl. Aston Villa subset RT-DETR-L v11 0.51 / 0.63 0.90 / 1.00 - 0.60 / 0.71 (94 frames, without Aston Villa) full / ball 0.74 / 0.97 0.76 / 1.00 0.79 / 0.90 0.76 / 0.95 full / football 0.70 / 0.96 0.90 / 1.00 0.59 / 0.90 0.70 / 0.95 full / soccer ball 0.67 / 0.97 0.76 / 1.00 0.51 / 0.92 0.64 / 0.96 full / white ball 0.03 / 0.56 0.76 / 1.00 0.00 / 0.33 0.14 / 0.56 full / small white ball 0.00 / 0.19 0.71 / 1.00 0.00 / 0.08 0.11 / 0.29 full / yellow ball 0.78 / 0.99 0.00 / 0.00 0.82 / 0.92 0.67 / 0.81 t540 / ball 0.67 / 0.78 0.57 / 0.71 0.85 / 0.95 0.71 / 0.82 t540 / yellow ball 0.75 / 0.79 0.14 / 0.14 0.87 / 0.92 0.69 / 0.73 t384 / ball 0.85 / 0.96 0.86 / 0.95 0.85 / 0.95 0.85 / 0.95 t384 / football 0.63 / 0.93 0.90 / 1.00 0.49 / 0.87 0.63 / 0.92 t384 / soccer ball 0.77 / 0.96 0.95 / 1.00 0.59 / 0.95 0.74 / 0.96 t384 / white ball 0.04 / 0.19 0.95 / 1.00 0.00 / 0.62 0.17 / 0.44 t384 / yellow ball 0.86 / 0.97 0.00 / 0.05 0.92 / 0.95 0.74 / 0.82

(full table with all tilings, thresholds and the other subsets: JSON.) At a detection-score threshold of 0.5, "t384 / ball" fires on 71 % of the ball frames and its top detection is right 95 % of the time (RT-DETR at 0.5: 73 % of frames, 75 % right; at 0.8: 31 % of frames, 100 % right; SAM 3's text scores are lower, essentially nothing reaches 0.8). On the 7-8 GT no_ball frames the false-fire rate at 0.5 is 0.12 (SAM 3) vs 0.14 (RT-DETR): too few to separate. arsenal_example held-out frames: top-1 0.05 for RT-DETR and "t384 / ball", 0.00 elsewhere. Whole-frame detection (0.78 s per frame for 6 prompts) is a cheap first pass (top-1 0.76); tiles cost 4.5 s (540 px) / 11.2 s (384 px) per frame for 6 prompts, ~5.6 s for one prompt at 384 px. Yes, SAM 3 can find its own seeds, better than RT-DETR on the held-out Bournemouth frames, at ~5 s per probed frame.

Dev check (80 GT frames: 20 each from mancity_seg010, mancity_seg031, mancity_seg050, bournemouth_1st_seg070; full / t384 tilings), and an honest limit of the result above. On the dev frames SAM 3 text detection is not better than RT-DETR: t384 / ball top-1 0.64 (seg010 0.85, seg050 0.65, seg031 0.60, seg070 0.45), t384 / soccer ball 0.64, full / ball 0.53, vs RT-DETR 0.85 (seg070 1.00, seg010 0.85, seg050 0.90, seg031 0.65). Two reasons: (1) the dev clips are RT-DETR training material (bournemouth_1st_seg070 is memorised: 1.00) while the held-out clips are exactly the ones RT-DETR has not seen, which is where it is weak (0.60); (2) dev GT frames come from dense runs and include many fast, blurred balls (SAM 3 text on seg070: 0.45 vs 0.85 on the held-out Bournemouth frames), the held-out frames were picked differently. Prompt ranking agrees between dev and final: "ball" ~ "soccer ball" best on white balls, "yellow ball" only on the yellow ball ("yellow ball" t384: 0.45 on seg070, 0.00-0.05 on the Man City clips), "white ball" / "small white ball" poor. So: for a match RT-DETR has not been trained on, SAM 3 text finds more balls than RT-DETR; on footage RT-DETR was trained on it does not, and in general it is a ~10-50x slower, second, independent detector (the property that makes it useful as a seed verifier).

Text + exemplar box (the API supports it: add_geometric_prompt on the same tile; the exemplar here is a rough hint = the GT box inflated 3x, only the tile containing it is searched; dev frames, t384): top-1 0.72 whatever the prompt ("ball" 0.72, "soccer ball" 0.72, "yellow ball" on white balls 0.70 vs 0.12 text-only: the exemplar dominates the prompt), emitted on 78 % of frames, vs 0.64 for text-only "ball" on the same frames. Modest: a coarse click / box is only partly refined into a correct ball box; it also helps simply because the search is restricted to one tile.

component s / frame frames / s peak VRAM SAM2.1-small crop512 track (sam2-exp driver) 0.14 7.05 0.8-1.0 GB SAM 3 box crop512 track 0.42 2.38 4.9 GB SAM 3.1 track 0.48 2.07 6.2 GB SAM 3 unpatched (bf16 emulation) 0.75 1.3 4.9 GB SAM 3 fp32 1.35 0.74 4.3 GB SAM 3 frame_step 2 0.21 effective 4.75 4.9 GB SAM 3 text probe, 384 px tiles, 1 prompt ~5.6 per probed frame 5.6 GB

GPU-hours per match half (~70 k frames at 25 fps; Bournemouth 50 fps segments are processed every 2nd frame): - SAM 3, every frame, single coverage (each seed tracks to the midpoint to its neighbour): 8.2 h; with S1 double coverage (forward and backward over every gap): 16.4 h. SAM2.1: 2.7 h / 5.4 h. - SAM 3 only on the frames the detector pipeline leaves open (round 3: ~30-50 % of balls had no confident detector candidate): ~2.5-4 h; with frame_step 2 half of that at -0.05 recall. - Seed finding, one 384-tile probe every 100 frames: 700 probes x 5.6 s = 1.1 h (every 50 frames: 2.2 h). - Measured end to end: the production demo (3 seeds, ~300 tracked frames incl. overlap) ran at 2.2-2.4 fps, i.e. 0.42 s per tracked frame including decoding.

docs.title: Prefect deployments and how to queue a whole match
docs.text:
Flow module ~/code/jobs/footy_sam3.py, deployments ~/code/jobs/sam3.prefect.yaml (pool gpu, concurrency 1, desktop RTX 2070). Experiment code is not in the jobs repo: every run rsyncs /home/george/footy-track-sam3/experiments/sam3_offline/ (branch exp/sam3-offline-labeller) from the mini, so code edits apply to the next queued run without redeploying. Redeploy only when a flow signature changes: cd ~/code/jobs && ~/.claude/skills/prefect-jobs/scripts/sync-desktop.sh && prefect deploy --prefect-file sam3.prefect.yaml --all.

deployment purpose main parameters sam3-track-eval/sam3-track-eval seed-propagated tracks for an evaluation spec; engine sam3 (model sam3 / sam3.1) or sam2 (the round-3 SAM2.1-small crop512 baseline through the same seeds) spec, clips (dev / final / example / names), protocol (oracle / rtdetr), config (JSON: model, prompt box / point / boxpoint / text:..., crop, recover, ...), max_reach, n_seeds, exp sam3-seedfind/sam3-seedfind text-prompt (whole frame / 540 px tiles / 384 px tiles) ball detection on GT frames, 6 prompts, optional exemplar schemes, prompts, exemplar, only_frames, exp sam3-rtdetr/sam3-rtdetr RT-DETR-L v11 labels (round-3 r3_detect.py) for spec clips that have none clips, exp sam3-script/sam3-script run one script of the code dir with the sam3 venv (profiling, smoke tests) script, args sam3-label-match/sam3-label-match production: queue a whole match (half) for background labelling below

All flows: resumable (per clip file / per track), wait for free VRAM (min_free_mib, default 5500) before starting, push outputs to the mini over rsync with an S3 presigned-PUT fallback (footy_s3hop.py tables), retries=1-2. Zombie / crash automations of the gpu pool apply as for every gpu flow.

docs.title: Queue a whole match
docs.text:
1. Seeds file on the mini (JSONL, one row per seed; box or xy, original frame index): from RT-DETR machine labels python experiments/sam3_offline/make_seeds.py --labels <machine_labels dir> --video-dir <clips dir> --thr 0.8 --spacing 100 > /mnt/storage/exp/sam3/<match>/seeds.jsonl (best conf >= 0.8 ball per 100-frame window; Bournemouth round-3 labels: --index-stride 2). Human clicks / overview seeds are appended in the same format ({"clip": .., "frame": .., "xy": [x, y], "source": "human"}).
  2. Segment clips named <clip>.mp4 in one directory on the mini (or a clip_files map {clip: file name}).
  3. $PF run sam3-label-match/sam3-label-match match=<name> seeds=/mnt/storage/exp/sam3/<name>/seeds.jsonl clips_dir=<mini dir> reach=250 overlap=15 'config={"model":"sam3","prompt":"box","crop":512}'
  4. leave it: per clip the video is staged (S3 presigned GET sam3/<match>/<clip>.mp4 when prepared, else rsync), sam3_label.py runs forward + backward tracks per seed (never past the neighbouring seed + overlap), writes <clip>.labels.jsonl + <clip>.raw.json.gz, pushes them to /mnt/storage/exp/sam3/<match>/labels/, deletes the staged video. Cancel / retry / crash-resume keeps finished clips and finished tracks.
  5. Output rows (JSONL, one per labelled frame): clip, p, frame (original index), x, y, box, score (SAM object-score logit), seed, dir, dist (frames from the seed), gate: seed (the seed itself) | s1 (forward track of one seed and backward track of the next agree within 5 px: position = mean) | score (single track, logit > score_gate) | weak (the rest: do not use as a label).

Demo (sam3-label-match match=demo, Bournemouth seg035, 3 RT-DETR seeds at original frames 58, 116, 270, reach 150): 39 GT frames inside the labelled span: seed 1/1, s1 14/14 correct, score-gated 24 frames 66.7 % correct (the errors all come from seed 58, a yellow boot). eval_labels.py reproduces it; demo_labels_bournemouth_seg035.jpg shows the labels (magenta = seed, green = s1, yellow = score gate).

docs.title: Visual checks (docs/experiments/sam3_offline_labeller/)
docs.text:
• track_sam3_mancity_seg050_o0_fwd_long_good.jpg: 120-frame forward track through blur, a long kick and into the crowd; green = GT, red cross = SAM 3 (crop centred on its own prediction).
  • track_sam2_astonvilla_o0_fwd_359_frames.jpg: SAM2 over the 359-frame Aston Villa run (every 16th frame).
  • track_sam3_mancity_seg010_o2_bwd_drift_to_player.jpg: drift onto a player's boot while the ball is occluded, re-acquisition ~30 frames later.
  • track_sam3_arsenal_example_o1_fwd_crowd_failure.jpg: lost in the crowd, "absent" with logit -4..-6 (scores say so).
  • demo_labels_bournemouth_seg035.jpg: production output including the yellow-boot false seed.
  • gt_arsenal_example_heldout.jpg, gt_mancity_seg031.jpg, rtdetr_conf80_seed_candidates_64.jpg: GT / seed sanity sheets.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The held-out GT is saturated for tracking from a good seed: differences between SAM2 / SAM 3 / 3.1 are below what 251-1 217 frames of 7-8 clips can resolve (clip-level CIs are wide; frame-level CIs are optimistic). A harder, denser GT with fast kicks / occlusions would be needed to rank trackers.
  • The 250+ bin is one clip; arsenal_example is one clip; no-ball precision has n = 5-26; Nottingham Forest could not be scored (no window labels).
  • Odd-frame GT of 50 fps clips is scored against the mean of two neighbours (adds up to a few px of interpolation error); 10 px hit threshold equals about the ball diameter.
  • Seed-finder prompts were not tuned on a separate set before the held-out numbers were read (a dev check is reported); the "yellow ball" result is match-specific by construction.
  • SAM 3.1 was tested with mask / point seeds only (no box prompt in the multiplex demo tracker) and only on the dev set; the text-recovery trick is implemented for SAM 3 only.
  • fp16 autocast with fp32 resident weights; no torch.compile, no lower input resolution (the tracker is hard-wired to 1008 px / 72x72 features; a 504 px variant would need re-deriving the RoPE / memory sizes and was not tried).

docs.title: Recommendation and next step
docs.text:
1. Keep SAM2.1-small crop512 as the track engine of the pseudo-label pipeline: same accuracy as SAM 3 / 3.1 wherever the GT can tell (saturated), 3x faster, 6x less memory, 2.7 GPU-hours per half. SAM 3.1's multiplex gains do not apply to one ball.
  2. Use SAM 3 as the slow background seed finder and verifier: (a) per match pick the text prompt (white ball: "ball" / "soccer ball"; yellow ball: "ball" / "yellow ball"; check on a few dev frames), (b) probe 384 px tiles upscaled to 1008 every ~50-100 frames (1-2 h per half) and add the top detection (score >= 0.5: ~95 % right) as a seed candidate next to RT-DETR conf >= 0.8 seeds, (c) accept a track only where two independent seeds agree (S1, 5 px) or a second model (SAM 3 vs SAM2.1) agrees; do not trust a single track's score (false seed = confident wrong track).
  3. Use the SAM 3 tracker only on stretches where SAM2 loses the ball (crowd / long occlusion): it was the only place it beat SAM2 (+0.05 on arsenal_example, +0.17 at 100-250 frames, one clip) and its logit is the better gate (score > 8: precision 0.97-1.0).
  4. Production: sam3-label-match (built, demoed): ~0.42 s per tracked frame; give it seeds from (2); budget ~8 GPU-hours per half for one SAM 3 pass over every frame, ~2.5-4 h for gap filling, overnight is fine.

Next steps, in order: (i) a harder, denser GT (fast kicks, occlusions, crowd) because the current held-out set cannot rank trackers; (ii) stop tracks at scene cuts (cuts.py) and add the SAM 3 text probe as a seed verifier in sam3_label.py; (iii) run the seed finder + SAM2 tracks on an unlabelled half (Nottingham Forest) and measure the precision of the S1-gated labels with the blind Ball Check (the study could not score Nottingham Forest: no window labels); (iv) feed the SAM 3 text detections as extra candidates to the round-3 B1 solver (union with RT-DETR gave +0.03-0.04 recall before); (v) only if throughput matters, try a 504 px SAM 3 input (4x fewer tokens; needs the RoPE / memory feature sizes re-derived) or half-precision weights.

docs.title: Temporal detector ablation: single frame vs camera-aligned neighbours
docs.text: Branch exp/temporal-detector (from exp/multiframe-dataset), 2026-11-14. Code: experiments/temporal_detector/, tests tests/temporal_detector/, Prefect flow ~/code/jobs/footy_temporal.py. Dataset: docs/experiments/multiframe_dataset.md. Knowledge-base pages relied on: footy-ball-detection-findings (1280 px is the lever, the 44-instance benchmark trap, the "go temporal" research), prefect-job-system / skill prefect-jobs (pools, deployments, desktop sync), footy-data-s3, wsl-gpu-training-box ("Desktop as it is now": bare-metal Ubuntu, flaky Wi-Fi, ~/.local/bin/uv).

docs.title: Question and verdict
docs.text:
Does giving the detector camera-motion-aligned neighbouring frames (t-2, t+2 as extra grey channels) improve tiny-ball detection over the same detector on the single frame?

Verdict: not shown. The input helps on one clip and does nothing measurable on the others. Same YOLO11s, same recipe, same frame-t pixels, COCO-pretrained, 100 epochs, 2 seeds per arm:

  • Held-out clips (the cleanest arbiter, 117 balls in 11 clips; 84 balls in 6 clips that appear nowhere in train/val/test): top-1 recall@10 px A 0.462 vs B 0.479, B-A = +0.017, 95% CI [-0.013, +0.047] (images) / [-0.019, +0.061] (clips); strict subset +0.018 [-0.024, +0.060]. Per seed +0.043 and -0.009. The experiment can exclude a gain much larger than about +0.05 on these clips, not a small one.
  • Test split (238 balls; optimistic because v11 splits by image, 33 clips shared with train): A 0.880, B 0.878, B-A = -0.002 [-0.023, +0.019] (saturated).
  • Val split: B-A = +0.146 [+0.098, +0.191], but it is entirely one clip: arsenal_example (156 of 209 val balls, no train frames from it, so it is a genuinely unseen clip) gives +0.208 [+0.154, +0.266] (seeds +0.167 / +0.250), the other 32 val clips give -0.038 [-0.113, +0.028]. A clip-level bootstrap over val is [-0.082, +0.190]: one clip cannot establish a general effect.
  • Where time does help: candidate recall. Fraction of balls with some detection within 10 px: test+heldout +0.023 [+0.003, +0.044], heldout +0.056 [+0.009, +0.107], and for the fastest third of balls (test+heldout) +0.066 [+0.026, +0.114] while slow/medium balls show +0.000 / +0.009. So the temporal channels make the detector propose moving balls it otherwise missed, but they do not make the top-1 pick better (hit@10 for the fastest third +0.018 [-0.009, +0.044]). A re-ranking / tracking stage on top of the candidates is where this would pay, not the detector input alone.
  • Neighbour fallback (cut / edge / alignment failure, 13 test+heldout balls): both arms 0.462, no difference (n too small).
  • Against production: RT-DETR-L v11 at 1280, same frames, hit@10 val 0.718 / test 0.916 / heldout 0.487 vs B 0.639 / 0.878 / 0.479 (A 0.493 / 0.880 / 0.462). YOLO11s B is on par with RT-DETR-L on held-out clips, lower on val and test. RT-DETR is trained at 1920 and is far less confident (top-1 FP rate on ball-free frames 31% at conf 0.5 vs 14-17% for YOLO), so compare recall at a conf level, not only the top-1 hit rate.
  • Seed variance is large: val recall differs by 0.15 between the two A seeds, and the held-out B-A is +0.043 for seed 0 (CI just touching zero) but -0.009 for seed 1, so a single-seed comparison could have been read either way.

Caveats: one model size (YOLO11s, not m: m is ~2.5x slower per epoch), k=2 only, one recipe, 100 epochs (val ball AP50 is still rising at epoch 100 for all runs; the curves are noisy, +-0.05 between neighbouring epochs, so last.pt is evaluated, no checkpoint selection on val), 2 seeds. The seed-2 runs that were queued were cancelled to bound wall-clock (arm=A|B seed=2 reruns them).

docs.title: Recipe (identical in both arms; only the input differs)
docs.text:
• A: 3 channels = B,G,R of frame t, losslessly re-saved as PNG from the same TIFFs (pixels identical), stock YOLO11s stem.
  • B: all 5 TIFF channels [gray(t-2) aligned, B, G, R, gray(t+2) aligned]; stem inflated by multichannel.make_inflated_checkpoint (pretrained R/G/B filters on input channels 3/2/1, channels 0 and 4 zero, so at step 0 the 5-channel net computes exactly the 3-channel net; unit-tested, including that changing the neighbours leaves the output unchanged).
  • YOLO11s, imgsz 1280, batch 4 (AMP), 100 epochs, seed 0 / 1, Ultralytics 8.3.241, optimiser auto (AdamW lr 0.00091, because iterations < 10k), mosaic 1.0 (close_mosaic 10), scale 0.5, translate 0.1, fliplr 0.5, HSV off in both arms (Ultralytics skips it for 5 channels), Albumentations off in both, plots off, val every epoch, no early stopping, last.pt evaluated. All 7 classes trained as in the export; the ball is class in_play_ball.
  • Evaluation (evaluate.py, report.py): explicit fp16 inference at 1280 (letterbox, NMS conf 0.001 IoU 0.7 multi-label, ball class only), boxes in the 1920x1080 frame (7 of the 599 eval images are 1280x720 sources; they are scaled into the canonical frame). hit@10 = top-1 ball detection within 10 px of a GT ball centre; AP50 = 101-point at IoU 0.5. Cross-check against Ultralytics' own validator at the last epoch (ball AP50 on val, report vs Ultralytics): A0 0.506 vs 0.509, A1 0.376 vs 0.369, B0 0.620 vs 0.626, B1 0.542 vs 0.528.
  • Reference row: production RT-DETR-L rtdetr_1920_v11/best.pt run through the same script on frame t at 1280 (Ultralytics predictor, conf 0.001). It was trained on the v11 train split, as were A and B.

docs.title: Augmentation check (5-channel input stays aligned)
docs.text:
viz_aug.py pulls samples from the very Ultralytics train pipeline (mosaic, affine, flip) and renders RGB(t), the temporal composite R=gray(t-2) G=gray(t) B=gray(t+2) and a zoom at the ball. Static, aligned content stays grey; only moving players and the on-screen graphics fringe; the neighbours are never displaced relative to t.

Quantitatively, over 40 augmented ball samples the mean |gray(t) - neighbour| is 2.16 (t-2) / 1.90 (t+2) vs 3.13 / 2.76 without augmentation (lower because mosaic/affine padding has zero difference; a mis-warped neighbour would raise it), and a real batch confirmed the tensor channel order is the stored B,G,R order (so RGB filters go to 3/2/1). A unit test pushes five identical channels through RandomPerspective + RandomFlip and asserts they stay identical. Files: aug_check_*.

docs.title: What broke or needed a workaround
docs.text:
• Pretrained stem silently dropped for 5 channels (shape mismatch) -> manual inflation; "Transferred 643/649 items" confirms the stem is now loaded. A full train() epoch with val + AMP at 5 channels works (the open item from the dataset note).
  • Border value bug: RandomPerspective calls warpAffine(..., borderValue=(114,114,114)), which OpenCV expands to (114,114,114,0): for 5 channels the R channel is padded with 0 and the second neighbour with 114 (checked on a constant image: [114 114 114 0 114]). Patched in multichannel.patch_ultralytics_multichannel so every channel pads with 114.
  • cv2.resize(..., INTER_AREA) does not accept 5 channels (Ultralytics' own loader uses INTER_LINEAR, so the evaluation does too); the Ultralytics predictor reverses all channels of a numpy input, which scrambles the 5-channel layout, hence the explicit inference path (checked equal to the dataset loader's letterbox content).
  • meta.jsonl calls the val split valid, the directories val: the first evaluation runs lost neighbour status / clip ids for val; report.py re-fills them from meta.jsonl for every run.
  • 7 images are 1280x720; the first evaluate crashed on them (empty motion window) until coordinates were converted to the 1920x1080 frame.
  • Desktop / Prefect: the desktop's Wi-Fi dropped several times (signal -72 to -77 dBm); the zombie automation then marked the running flow Crashed (no heartbeat) while its train.py kept running, and the next queued run started a second training on the same 8 GB GPU (OOM). A retrying flow run also bypasses the pool's concurrency slot. Another session's SAM2 jobs share this GPU outside Prefect (epochs slowed from 52 s to ~105 s; one OOM at start-up). Mitigations: runs are resumable (last.pt, train_done.json), the flow now waits for any orphaned train.py before training (_wait_for_orphan_training), and A seed 1 was resumed once at epoch 20 (kill + resume from last.pt).
  • ball_curve.jsonl has a second row at the end of training (Ultralytics re-validates best.pt); report.py keeps the first row per epoch.
  • Data transfer: 5.4 GB mini -> desktop took about 2.2 h over the Wi-Fi (rsync, resumable).

docs.title: Wall-clock
docs.text: Per 100-epoch run: A seed 0 1.35 h, B seed 0 1.40 h, B seed 1 1.40 h, A seed 1 2.17 h (GPU shared with a SAM2 job, one resume); evaluation of 599 images 52 s (YOLO) / 108 s (RT-DETR). About 6.3 GPU-hours for the four runs on one RTX 2070.

docs.title: Round 2: does pseudo-labelled data (v11 train + filtered pseudo) change the 3ch / 5ch comparison?
docs.text: Branch exp/temporal-detector. Code: experiments/temporal_detector/{pseudo_filter,pseudo_audit_survivors,round2_report}.py, flow temporal-ablation/temporal-ablation ... pseudo=true exp_tag=r2 (~/code/jobs/footy_temporal.py). Builds on temporal_detector_ablation.md (v1) and temporal_pipeline_eval.md. Pseudo labels: /mnt/storage/footy_data/multiframe_pseudo_v1/ (branch exp/pseudo-labels-v1 7c53b25).

docs.title: Questions and answers
docs.text:
Same recipe as v1 (YOLO11s, imgsz 1280, batch 4, HSV and Albumentations off, last.pt), but train = v11 train (1,034) + 1,617 filtered pseudo-labelled images, 60 epochs (v1: 100; the larger set gives 663 vs 259 iterations per epoch, so about 40k vs 26k in total), 2 seeds each: A+ (3ch, same pixels as PNG) and B+ (5ch, inflated stem). Val, test, heldout, strict and the metrics are exactly v1's, so every number compares directly with v1's A / B.

  1. Does pseudo data close the seed variance? Yes. Seed range of hit@10 (A / B, v1 -> round 2): val 0.153 / 0.081 -> 0.038 / 0.000; val clip arsenal_example 0.186 / 0.103 -> 0.051 / 0.006; test 0.013 / 0.008 -> 0.004 / 0.004; held-out 0.034 / 0.017 -> 0.000 / 0.000 (both seeds 56/117 for both arms). Ball AP50 on val at the last epoch: A_s1 0.369 vs A_s0 0.509 in v1, Ap 0.606 / 0.657 and Bp 0.624 / 0.669 now.
  2. Does it raise held-out and arsenal_example recall? It raises in-domain recall, not held-out.
  3. Test (same match and broadcast as the pseudo pool; 33 test clips share a clip with train): A+ - A +0.076 [+0.046, +0.109], B+ - B +0.065 [+0.038, +0.095] (A 0.880 -> 0.956, B 0.878 -> 0.943; RT-DETR 0.916). Candidate recall any@10 +0.055 / +0.044.
  4. val clip arsenal_example (156 balls, no train frames): A+ - A +0.221 [+0.157, +0.285] (0.375 -> 0.596), B+ - B +0.029 [-0.026, +0.083] (0.583 -> 0.612): A catches up with B (RT-DETR 0.667). Other val clips: +0.047 [-0.009, +0.123] / +0.113 [+0.047, +0.189].
  5. Held-out clips (117 balls, 11 clips, other matches / provenance than the pool; strict 84): A+ - A +0.017 [-0.004, +0.043], B+ - B +0.000 [-0.038, +0.038]; strict +0.018 / +0.000. No gain: A+ and B+ both 0.479 against RT-DETR 0.487; candidate recall any@10 stays at 0.54-0.57 (RT-DETR 0.675), i.e. the held-out misses are balls no candidate covers, and more same-match pseudo data does not fix them.
  6. Does B - A widen with more data? No, it narrows or vanishes. B+ - A+ hit@10: val +0.019 [-0.017, +0.055] (v1 +0.146), test -0.013 [-0.029, +0.002] (v1 -0.002), held-out +0.000 [-0.030, +0.030] (v1 +0.017), test+heldout -0.008 [-0.024, +0.006]. The difference of differences (B+ - A+) - (B - A) is -0.127 [-0.187, -0.067] on val, entirely arsenal_example (-0.192 [-0.266, -0.119]: v1's 5ch advantage there was a small-data effect that 3ch closes with pseudo data), and -0.011 / -0.017 (n.s.) on test / held-out. Candidate recall B+ - A+ is ~0 everywhere (test -0.004, held-out +0.026 [-0.021, +0.077]); the v1 gain for the fastest third of balls (+0.066) shrinks to +0.035 [-0.004, +0.075].
  7. Through the trajectory solver (appendix; harness B1 camera on, the 9 test clips, 170 balls): A+ 0.794 raw / 0.826 iso, B+ 0.829 / 0.844 recall@10, precision 0.99 / 0.98-0.99. B+ - A+ +0.035 [+0.009, +0.067] raw, +0.018 [0.000, +0.036] iso (v1 +0.047 / +0.029): the 5ch edge under the solver survives but did not widen. Both round-2 detectors now exceed the production RT-DETR-L (0.759) on these clips: B+ - RT-DETR +0.071 [+0.033, +0.111] raw, +0.085 [+0.047, +0.126] iso at unchanged precision (-0.005 to +0.012), ceiling 0.838 vs 0.829. On arsenal_example (all labelled frames, the labelled deviation) A+ 0.264 / 0.457, B+ 0.256 / 0.420 (raw / iso), B+ - A+ -0.009 [-0.048, +0.031] (v1 +0.071), and RT-DETR (0.540) is still well ahead (B+ - RT-DETR -0.284 raw, -0.119 iso).
  8. False positives on ball-free images (35 images of val+test+heldout, small n): top-1 conf >= 0.5: A 0.171 -> A+ 0.157, B 0.157 -> B+ 0.186; conf >= 0.7: 0.071 -> 0.114 (A+), 0.071 -> 0.143 (B+); confident wrong top-1 picks on ball frames (conf >= 0.5): 0.008 -> 0.013 (A+), 0.005 -> 0.009 (B+). A small rise at high confidence (2-3 images of 35, within noise), no sign of a crowd/kit leak at the scale visible here; RT-DETR remains the noisiest (31% at conf 0.5, 4.1% confident wrong picks).

Reading. The pseudo data is worth about +0.07 test recall and removes seed noise for both input types, so most of v1's A-vs-B difference was a low-data / high-variance effect rather than a lasting benefit of the temporal channels. A 5ch detector keeps a small edge only after a solver ranks its candidates (+0.02 to +0.04 on the test clips) and nothing measurable on held-out clips. The filter rule (conf >= 0.45 and a conf >= 0.8 node within 25 frames) was not ablated: no run with all 759 low-conf B1 images or with the 241 + 257 dropped ones exists, so the effect of the filtering itself is not measured. Epochs differ from v1 (60 vs 100), so "round 2 vs v1" mixes data and schedule.

docs.title: Filter and data
docs.text:
• Counts: of 2,115 pseudo images 1,617 survive: 1,000 easy (conf >= 0.8) + 356 S1 fills + 261 of 759 low-conf B1 (dropped: 241 with conf < 0.45, 257 with no conf >= 0.8 B1 node within +-25 frames). Segment ids are not in meta.jsonl, so segments were rebuilt from the provenance table (provenance_all.jsonl.gz): consecutive B1 rows with gaps <= 25 frames, so the rule reduces to "a conf >= 0.8 B1 detection within +-25 frames"; cuts inside the window are not checked.
  • Audit hit@10 of the survivors (the pseudo doc's audit pipeline: the harness' B1 re-run on the 18 GT-bearing harness clips + arsenal_example; B1 detections with conf < 0.6 on a human GT frame): all low-conf 38/50 (76%; the doc's 38/49), survivors 13/15 (86.7%) (test 3/4, dev 8/9, arsenal_example 2/2). n is tiny; S1 fills (19/20 in the doc) and easy images (138/138) are unchanged.
  • Eval overlap: zero, checked explicitly: no pseudo frame lies within +-5 frames of a v11 val/test/heldout image or in a clip with one (the pool excludes all 97 such clips), and none belongs to arsenal_example or the 9 trajectory test clips (3 of them excluded from the pool by the pseudo build). The near_v11_train_5 frames (91) are kept; near_human_gt_5 frames (52) are of pool clips that are not evaluation clips and are kept.
  • Transfer: only the 1,617 survivors (6.05 GB) went to the desktop, via S3 (new prefix exp_temporal_r2/pseudo_v1/, upload from the mini about 4 MB/s, download by presigned-URL curl, resumable); the direct mini -> desktop rsync measured 1.2-1.8 MB/s over the Wi-Fi. Sizes verified against the mini copy; presigned URL list deleted from the desktop.
  • Training cost: 2.0-2.1 h per 60-epoch run (about 2 min/epoch, GPU not shared, no crash); four runs about 8.3 h.
