docs.text: Naming note: the held-out match used to be called "Norwich"; it is Arsenal v Nottingham Forest (scoreboard NFO), now arsenal_nottinghamforest. Old ids (arsenal_norwich_segNNN, *_norwich dirs) and experiment artifacts written under the old name (r3_norwich, exp/temporal/round3/norwich*, S3 exp_temporal_r3/out/*_norwich) keep it, so old numbers can still be traced. Branch exp/temporal-detector. Code: experiments/temporal_detector/{r3_detect,r3_prep,r3_fuse,r3_build,r3_audit_bm,heldout_by_match,round2_report}.py, flows temporal-r3-{detect,sam2,build} (~/code/jobs/footy_temporal_r3.py, S3 hop in footy_s3hop.py), training via temporal-ablation ... extra_dirs=r3_bournemouth,r3_norwich. Builds on temporal_detector_ablation.md (v1), temporal_pipeline_eval.md, temporal_detector_round2.md. 3-channel only; the 5-channel arm is parked (not run).

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text:
The tool is offline, so it may pseudo-label the match it is processing, using none of that match's human labels. Round 3 trains YOLO11s 3ch on v11 train + the Man City round-2 pseudo set + pseudo labels of Bournemouth (the match 76 of the 117 held-out balls come from) and Nottingham Forest (a target match, no labels yet): arm A++, 60 epochs, 2 seeds, same recipe as v1/round 2.

Held-out recall moves off 0.48, and the whole gain is in the match whose video was pseudo-labelled. - Held-out (117 balls, 11 clips), top-1 recall@10 px: A+ (round 2) 0.479 -> A++ 0.641 (seeds 0.658 / 0.624), paired +0.162 [+0.103, +0.226] over frames, clip-level [+0.040, +0.287]; strict (84 balls) 0.512 -> 0.738, +0.226 [+0.149, +0.315]. Against production RT-DETR-L (0.487): +0.154 [+0.094, +0.222]. - By source match (retrospective numbers for the earlier models included):

held-out subset (n) RT-DETR A v1 A+ r2 B+ r2 A++ r3 (seeds) Bournemouth (76) 0.487 0.421 0.447 0.441 0.697 (0.724 / 0.671) Bournemouth strict (66) 0.424 0.356 0.379 0.379 0.667 (0.697 / 0.636) Man City (41) 0.488 0.537 0.537 0.549 0.537 Man City minus arsenal_example (21) 0.905 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 arsenal_example held-out frames (20) 0.050 0.050 0.050 0.075 0.050

Bournemouth: A++ - A+ +0.250 [+0.164, +0.342] (clip CI [+0.141, +0.412]), strict +0.288 [+0.189, +0.394]; A++ - RT-DETR +0.211 [+0.125, +0.303] (clip [+0.083, +0.292]); candidate recall any@10 on Bournemouth 0.546 -> 0.849 (RT-DETR 0.724). A+ (Man City pseudo only) was -0.039 [-0.112, +0.026] below RT-DETR there. - Man City held-out was already "transductive" in A+ and stayed flat, and still is. Minus arsenal_example the 21 balls are solved by every YOLO arm (1.000; RT-DETR 0.905), so the Man City held-out headroom is only arsenal_example's 20 held-out frames, where every model (RT-DETR included) is at 0.05: that is a hard / possibly mislabelled frame set, not a data-volume problem. The held-out gap was Bournemouth. - The gain concentrates on fast balls: test+heldout, fastest third of balls A++ - A+ +0.118 [+0.066, +0.175], slow and medium +/-0.01 (n.s.).

Costs / side effects (be aware): - arsenal_example (Man City example clip, val): hit@10 0.596 -> 0.510, -0.087 [-0.131, -0.042] (seed range 0.096); through the solver (all labelled frames) B1 recall A++ 0.210 raw / 0.301 iso vs A+ 0.264 / 0.457: -0.054 [-0.091, -0.017] raw, -0.156 [-0.205, -0.108] iso, ceiling -0.119 [-0.165, -0.074]; the two seeds disagree (+0.051 vs -0.159 raw). RT-DETR still leads there (0.540). Test (Man City, in-domain) is flat: -0.008 [-0.023, +0.004]; solver on the 9 test clips -0.003 [-0.030, +0.024] raw. A plausible reading is dilution (Man City pseudo is 34% of the pseudo-labelled data instead of all of it), not verified. - False positives on ball-free images (35 images, val+test+heldout, small n): top-1 conf >= 0.5 A+ 0.157 -> A++ 0.243, conf >= 0.7 0.114 -> 0.171 (RT-DETR 0.314 / 0.171; A v1 0.171 / 0.071); confident wrong top-1 picks on ball frames 0.013 -> 0.010. So the new pseudo data buys recall with a visible rise in confident false positives on ball-free frames (about +3 images of 35 at conf >= 0.5): plausible leakage of the pseudo-label errors, not separable at this n. - Through the solver on the 9 Man City test clips A++ stays at the A+ level (0.791 raw / 0.815 iso vs 0.794 / 0.826) and above production RT-DETR-L (+0.032 [+0.003, +0.064] raw, +0.056 [+0.026, +0.091] iso, precision unchanged).

docs.title: Pseudo-labelling pipeline (per target match)
docs.text:
RT-DETR-L v11 @1280 (Bournemouth: run here with the ffmpeg CLI -fps_mode passthrough, conf >= 0.1, all classes; Nottingham Forest: the existing machine labels) -> harness B1 (camera on, dev-tuned parameters, unchanged) -> S1 (SAM2.1-small crop512 tracks from conf >= 0.8 anchors, forward/backward agreement gate) -> filter -> stride >= 5 -> 3ch PNG + YOLO labels (pseudo ball + machine player/other boxes conf >= 0.5). - Frame rate: the Bournemouth clips are 50 fps. They are handled as 25 fps clips by taking every 2nd decoded frame, so B1's per-frame parameters (vmax 40 px/frame, max_gap 25), the +-25-frame filter window and stride 5 keep their meaning; subsampled index t is original frame 2t. RT-DETR runs on the original even frames, SAM2 on a 25 fps copy (crf 12), training images are the original frames 2t, so labels sit in the GT frame space (GT indices are 50 fps). - Random subset for Bournemouth: 60 of the 114 pool clips (59 used: seg092 is unreadable on the mini, I/O error after ~5 MB of the mp4); 15,722 frames at 25 fps. - Exclusions: every held-out clip and every v11 val/test clip in full (Bournemouth: seg009, 010, 015, 021, 031, 035, 060 never in the pool); Nottingham Forest queue windows +-25 frames (selected frames are >= 28 frames from any window, 0 inside, checked); ball_gt_marks_nottinghamforest is never read: the harness root used for B1 has an empty ball_gt_marks, and the blind-check verdicts in ball_gt_marks_nottinghamforest/ball_checks were not used for anything. - Selection: easy B1 nodes (conf >= 0.8, random, cap 800) + all S1 fills, cap 1,500 per match: Bournemouth 1,025 images (800 easy + 225 S1; 51 clips; 7 within 5 frames of a v11 train image, kept), Nottingham Forest 1,138 (800 + 338; 66 clips).

No low-confidence B1 detections for either match (a change to the round-2 filter, with evidence). Audit off Man City: the harness B1 on RT-DETR labels of the six held-out Bournemouth clips (excluded from the pool, so no leak), scored against their human GT on the 36 GT frames that fall on the 25 fps subsample: B1 node hit@10 by confidence band conf >= 0.8 6/6, 0.6-0.8 5/9 (Man City: 98%), < 0.6 1/8, and the round-2 low-conf survivors 0/6. George's blind check of the Nottingham Forest set agrees (Ball Check, no source shown; verdicts in ball_gt_marks_nottinghamforest/ball_checks, not used for training; figures supplied by the coordinator): easy B1 anchors 58/60 real (97%, CI 89-99%), S1 fills 53/60 (88%, CI 78-94%, plus 2 box_off), estimated set precision about 94% (comparable to the Man City r2 set); B1 nodes with p < 0.5 outside the set 22/40 real (55%), and B1-rejected RT-DETR detections with conf >= 0.6 only 1/40 real, so the solver's rejections are right and RT-DETR confidence is badly calibrated on this match.

Contact sheets (48 random crops each, 64 px at 3x, label box, source and confidence / fill rule and distance to the anchor): - Nottingham Forest easy: 48/48 clear balls; Nottingham Forest S1 fills: mostly balls, about 4 of 48 are blurred streaks or a boot (consistent with the blind check). - Bournemouth easy: 48/48 clear (yellow) balls; Bournemouth S1 fills: about 5 of 48 doubtful or wrong (one box on the Premier League logo, a few on ad boards / crowd): kept, flagged as the weakest part.

docs.title: Training and what was not done
docs.text:
• A++: v11 train (1,034) + Man City r2 pseudo (1,617) + Bournemouth (1,025) + Nottingham Forest (1,138) = 4,816 images, YOLO11s 3ch, imgsz 1280, batch 4, 60 epochs, seeds 0 and 1, last.pt, HSV / Albumentations off (identical to round 2). 3.7-6 h per run (GPU-bound, 1,204 iterations per epoch).
  • Not run: the arm without the Man City pseudo (cancelled: not cheap at ~5 h/run, so "Man City pseudo vs target pseudo" effects are not separated); the RT-DETR-L fine-tune (not started); the 5-channel arm (parked); the Nottingham Forest preview: at evaluation time ball_gt_marks_nottinghamforest held no window labels (only the blind-check verdicts), so nothing was scored on Nottingham Forest. Nottingham Forest pseudo labels are in the training data but untested.
  • Caveat on interpretation: the held-out Bournemouth frames come from the same match (same kit, stadium, ball) as the pseudo-labelled clips, never from the same clips or frames (disjoint segments, held-out and v11 eval clips excluded in full). That is exactly the transductive setting the offline tool has, but it says nothing about a match whose video was not pseudo-labelled; and Man City held-out, the only other match, was flat before and after.
  • Cost: Bournemouth RT-DETR labels for 17,282 processed frames about 17 min (18 fps); SAM2: Nottingham Forest 69 clips / 11.2k steps about 30 min, Bournemouth 42 clips / 5.7k steps about 20 min; most wall-clock went to the desktop Wi-Fi (the tailnet path fell back to a ~30 KB/s DERP relay for hours, so large transfers go through S3 with presigned URLs) and to the 3 x 4-6 h of training.

docs.title: Temporal candidates through the trajectory solver: does 5-channel input help once a solver ranks?
docs.text: Branch exp/temporal-detector. Code: experiments/temporal_detector/{clip_infer,pipeline_eval}.py, Prefect flow temporal-clip-infer/temporal-clip-infer (~/code/jobs/footy_temporal_clips.py). Harness: exp/offline-ball-tracking @ fc05732 (src/footy_track/ball_offline/, imported read-only; its numbers are reproduced exactly below). Follows temporal_detector_ablation.md (v1: YOLO11s, 100 epochs, 2 seeds, arm A 3ch vs arm B 5ch).

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text:
Does the 5-channel detector's candidate set help once a trajectory solver (the harness's B1: offline Viterbi + short gap fill, camera on) does the ranking?

Yes, modestly, and the gain survives the solver; but the YOLO11s detectors stay below the production RT-DETR-L unless their confidence is recalibrated, and then only match it on the test clips.

  • 9 harness test clips (170 clean GT balls: 110 seg010, 53 seg031, 7 single frames): B1(5ch) - B1(3ch) recall@10 = +0.047 [+0.012, +0.086] with the harness calibration knots applied to the YOLO confidence ("raw"), +0.029 [+0.003, +0.059] with per-model isotonic maps fitted on v11 train ("iso"); per seed +0.059 / +0.035 (raw), +0.041 / +0.018 (iso). The candidate ceiling is almost unchanged (+0.009 [-0.020, +0.038]): on these clips the solver gets more out of the 5ch candidates, it does not get more candidates. Precision is unchanged with raw knots (-0.003 [-0.018, +0.010]) and lower with iso (-0.046 [-0.078, -0.018]): the iso map is fitted on train images the detector has memorised, so it trusts almost every candidate (equal-precision min_conf falls to 0.10) and lets the solver emit more wrong points.
  • arsenal_example (250 frames, a clip with no train frames, 176 labelled frames): B1(5ch) - B1(3ch) recall@10 = +0.071 [+0.034, +0.111] (raw; A is nearly blind: 0.139) and +0.253 [+0.202, +0.304] (iso; A 0.196 -> B 0.449), ceiling +0.216 [+0.168, +0.267] (0.213 -> 0.429). Per seed +0.062 / +0.080 (raw), +0.261 / +0.244 (iso). Here the gain is in the candidate set itself (the same clip where v1 saw +0.21 in top-1 recall) and the solver keeps it. Precision is 0.88-1.0 for both.
  • Against production RT-DETR-L (harness machine labels): B1(5ch) - B1(RT-DETR) = -0.059 [-0.092, -0.029] on the test clips with raw knots (YOLO confidences sit well below RT-DETR's, so the knots mark most YOLO candidates as unreliable and the solver's min_conf 0.3 discards them), +0.024 [-0.003, +0.053] with iso (0.782 vs 0.759) at -0.038 precision, and on arsenal_example -0.330 raw / -0.091 [-0.145, -0.040] iso (RT-DETR 0.540, B iso 0.449). The ceiling (any candidate >= 0.1 within 10 px) stays lower for the YOLO arms (test 0.756 vs 0.829; arsenal_example 0.429 vs 0.631): a 5ch YOLO11s still misses balls that RT-DETR-L proposes. So the temporal input narrows but does not close the gap to the production detector; the RT-DETR-L is the stronger base.
  • Exclusions. Test numbers use the harness exclusions exactly (frames within 5 of a v11 train/valid image dropped; 170 GT balls + 2 no_ball frames). arsenal_example is not a harness clip (no machine labels): applying the harness rule, 167 of its 176 labelled frames lie within 5 frames of a v11 valid image, leaving 9 clean frames (a "dev" clip). The harness-clean table has n = 9 and says nothing; the "all labelled frames" table is a deviation, defensible because the YOLO arms were neither trained on this clip (0 train frames) nor selected on val (last.pt); RT-DETR, selected on valid, is if anything flattered there.
  • Caveats: frames in a clip are strongly correlated and the bootstrap resamples frames (the test set is 65% one clip, seg010), so the CIs are optimistic; one model size, two seeds; isotonic maps from train are over-trusting (see above); the solver parameters were tuned on RT-DETR confidences and are used unchanged (B0 tau 0.4, B1 camera-on set), only min_conf and the B0 threshold are moved to the equal-precision confidence in the iso variant.

docs.title: Pipeline and checks
docs.text:
• Decoding: ffmpeg CLI -fps_mode passthrough (no cv2 decoding), one sequential pass per clip, 5-frame window. All 10 clips are 25 fps, 1920x1080; frame counts equal the harness' (ffprobe packets = machine-label manifest frames). Frame indices verified three ways: (1) for 37 dataset images of these clips the ffmpeg frame t equals the dataset TIFF BGR(t) exactly (mean abs diff 0.0; t+-1 gives 3-20), so the indices equal the dataset/GT index space; (2) RT-DETR rerun by this pipeline equals the harness' machine labels: the top-1 candidate of every frame with conf >= 0.3 has the same position (within 3 px) and confidence (within 0.05) in 549/549, 609/610, 311/312, 2293/2294, 212/212, 2126/2132, 426/426, 680/680 and 347/348 frames (seg010 ... seg140); (3) the harness' B1 / B0 on its own machine labels are reproduced to the count (129/170 TP, precision 0.985 and 126/170, 0.947).
  • 5ch input built on the fly like the dataset builder: LK + RANSAC alignment of t-2 and t+2 into t (calibration/temporal, person boxes masked: RT-DETR boxes conf >= 0.3 of the same frame), cut (consecutive-frame histogram distance > 0.2), clip edge and alignment failure -> gray(t). Neighbour slots over the 9 test clips + arsenal_example: at most 8 cut/edge slots per clip, 44 alignment failures (seg115: 42).
  • Candidates: ball class, conf >= 0.1, 1280, boxes in the 1920x1080 frame; camera shift / shot cuts for the solver come from the harness' own estimate (player boxes of the RT-DETR rows; for arsenal_example from the rerun's player boxes), identical for every detector.
  • Isotonic maps: PAV on candidate-level correctness (within 10 px of a labelled ball) of the four YOLO runs on the 1,034 v11 train images (not val/test/heldout), one map per run.
  • GPU: 8,851 frames (10 clips) at about 0.2-0.3 s/frame with RT-DETR + 4 YOLO models + 2 LK alignments per frame, plus 4 x 1,034 train images; one flow run (about 40 min); the flow refuses to start with less than 2 GB of free GPU memory.

docs.title: Union test: do the 5ch candidates add to RT-DETR-L?
docs.text:
Per frame the candidates of RT-DETR-L (harness knots -> p) and of a 5ch YOLO arm (isotonic map fitted on v11 valid without arsenal_example -> p) are merged: cross-source duplicates within 6 px collapse to one candidate (higher-p position, p = max), optionally with a +0.5 logit bonus when both agree. The merged p is fed to the harness' B0 (tau 0.4) / B1 (camera-on parameters) unchanged, through the inverse of the harness knots (RT-DETR alone is reproduced exactly). Ceiling of a union row = any candidate of either source (conf >= 0.1) within 10 px. 5ch YOLO = arm B of v1, seeds 0 and 1 reported separately.

Val isotonic maps (n small: B_s0: 44 candidates (40 correct) from 53 images, 4 knots, p in [0.50, 1.00]; B_s1: 43 candidates (37 correct) from 53 images, 5 knots, p in [0.00, 1.00]).

Paired bootstrap vs RT-DETR alone, B1 (95% CI over frames; over clips in brackets, test only):

candidate set recall@10 diff precision diff ceiling diff 5ch B_s0 alone (val-iso p) -0.028 [-0.085, 0.028] +0.087 [0.037, 0.145] -0.153 [-0.210, -0.102] union RT + B_s0 +0.062 [0.028, 0.102] +0.008 [-0.017, 0.035] +0.006 [0.000, 0.017] union RT + B_s0, agreement bonus +0.062 [0.028, 0.102] +0.008 [-0.016, 0.035] +0.006 [0.000, 0.017] 5ch B_s1 alone (val-iso p) -0.159 [-0.222, -0.097] -0.116 [-0.212, -0.024] -0.250 [-0.318, -0.182] union RT + B_s1 +0.023 [0.006, 0.045] -0.030 [-0.078, 0.013] +0.011 [0.000, 0.028] union RT + B_s1, agreement bonus +0.023 [0.000, 0.051] -0.022 [-0.073, 0.028] +0.011 [0.000, 0.028]

Reading: the 5ch candidates add to, rather than replace, the production detector, but modestly. The ceiling rises only a little (test +0.012 / +0.006 for seeds 0 / 1, arsenal_example +0.006 / +0.011) because most 5ch candidates duplicate RT-DETR's (about 6.5k agreeing candidates against about 1k YOLO-only on the test clips). B1 recall rises +0.029 / +0.041 on the test clips (frame CI excludes 0; the clip-level CI touches 0 because 7 of the 9 clips have a single GT frame and seg010 carries 65% of the frames) and +0.062 / +0.023 on arsenal_example; precision is -0.034 (seed 0) / +0.001 (seed 1) on test, so seed 0 also adds some wrong candidates. The agreement bonus changes almost nothing. On the 2 harness no_ball frames of the test clips no configuration emits a point (n = 2: uninformative). The val isotonic maps rest on 43-44 candidates (4-5 knots): too small to trust, so the union numbers are indicative; they do show that the gain over RT-DETR alone does not depend on a well-calibrated YOLO map.

docs.title: Notable Classifier Training Runs
docs.text:
A curated log of classifier training runs for the broadcast-frame classifier (footy-track-broadcast-frame Roboflow project). Each entry records the hyperparameters, key metrics, and observations needed to understand why a run was notable and how to reproduce it.

Use /train-classifier to run training and auto-append a new entry here.

docs.title: Regression Analysis: aakevy06 vs n5fh28pv (0.981 → 0.433)
docs.text: aakevy06 (reference) n5fh28pv (reproduction) Date 2026-01-25 2026-04-26 W&B project footy_scan_classifier footy_scan_classifier top1_acc 0.981 0.433 train/loss 0.024 0.030 val/loss 0.022 8.018 Model parameters 1,533,666 1,534,947 Runtime 316 s 348 s

docs.title: Hyperparameters compared via the W&B API
docs.text:
Both run configs were fetched via wandb.Api() and diffed. Every training hyperparameter is identical, including:

  • model: yolo11n-cls.pt
  • epochs: 50, freeze: 9, imgsz: 224, batch: 16
  • optimizer: auto, lr0: 0.01, lrf: 0.01, momentum: 0.937, weight_decay: 0.0005, warmup_epochs: 3, warmup_momentum: 0.8
  • device: mps, cache: True, augment: True, auto_augment: randaugment, dataset_version: 10, seed: 0, deterministic: True

The only config differences are environmental: data path, save_dir, and the auto-generated run name (the _freeze_layers=92 suffix on aakevy06's name is YOLO's directory-collision counter — not the freeze value, which is 9 in both runs' configs).

docs.title: Root cause: the dataset behind version=10 changed
docs.text:
The +1,281-parameter delta in the trained model (1,533,666 → 1,534,947) is the smoking gun: the classifier head grew by one output class. Both runs ask Roboflow for footy-track-broadcast-frame version 10, but the dataset was re-uploaded between January and April 2026 to add a third class (Unlabeled) which is present in train/ only:

Split Classes train No (165), Unlabeled (5), Yes (222) valid No (46), Yes (58) test No (47), Yes (53)

Ultralytics warns at startup (found 2 classes, requires 3) but proceeds. The 3-output model is then evaluated against a 2-class val set: any image predicted as Unlabeled is wrong by construction, and the val loss (8.018) reflects an unnormalised softmax over a never-seen class. The 0.433 result is below the 0.558 majority-class baseline (58/104 val images are Yes).

docs.title: Reproducing aakevy06's accuracy
docs.text:
Re-running train_classifier.py with aakevy06's config does not reach 0.981 — n5fh28pv is exactly that re-run, with byte-identical training hyperparameters. The fix is on the dataset, not the script:

  1. Drop or merge the Unlabeled class in Roboflow so train/val/test are consistently binary.
  2. Cut a new dataset version (e.g. v11) from the corrected source.
  3. Re-train with the same hyperparameters as aakevy06.

If reproducing the historical result against the current API is needed, download the dataset snapshot used by aakevy06 directly from W&B (api.run(...).file('train_batch0_*.jpg')) rather than re-pulling version=10 from Roboflow.
